News.title: Kids set to be told from primary school age how to get into work to avoid a life on benefits
News.content:
Next

KIDS are set to be told from primary school age how to get into work to avoid a life on benefits.

Jobs tsar Alan Milburn will call on Ministers to give kids early exposure to different careers to broaden their horizons and help end the youth inactivity crisis.



The recommendation to introduce mandatory work experience with dedicated curriculum time will be in his landmark review to help fix the NEETs travesty.

Mr Milburn fears that teaching youngsters about the workplace and providing hands-on experience has been an “afterthought” and the changes will help make them “work ready”.



The former Health Secretary spoke to The Sun as he visited Thornhill Community Academy in Dewsbury, west Yorkshire, where Channel 4’s Educating Yorkshire was based.

He said: “Just familiarising kids in primary school, maybe not from as young as four, but just familiarising them with what work means, what the possibilities are.



“Because all too often, children are growing up with a very narrow view about what the possibilities are for them.”

He added: “Particularly if they come from a poorer background.

“And partially, this is about getting employers in to primary schools and just beginning to lay the trail of breadcrumbs.

“So that youngsters are getting a sense about, ‘I could be doing this rather than that, I could be being a nurse, but I could be being a doctor.



Yeah, I could be thinking about going into veterinary medicine’.

He added: “I don’t think you want to be heavy-handed about it, but you do just want to begin to give youngsters a real sense of what they might be.”

Mr Milburn insisted he had “buy-in” from both Andy Burnham and John Healey in solving the Neets issue which sees one million 16-24 year olds not in education, employment or training.

He added that parents fearful of their children missing lessons should see it as an “investment” in their futures.

His proposals in his report that could be out within weeks include experience of work starting at the beginning of primary school.



Then in the first three years of secondary school pupils should have meaningful experience with employers.

When pupils are 14-16 years-old they should have a traditional work placement and be given employer feedback.

Mr Milburn added that the work experience can be part of the solution to get them away from benefits and the first step into work.

He said: “But for most youngsters, surely we can’t be ruining their life chances and saying, “Oh, it’s ok to be on benefits.

“We want youngsters to be in work, and by the way, they want to be in work.



“We know that eight and 10 young people who are NEET, they want to be working or they want to be training.

“And we’ve just got to make that possible. And this is part of the way that we do that by making sure that work experience is embedded in the curriculum. It’s not like an afterthought.”

Children’s Commissioner Dame Rachel de Souza who was also on the visit said: “I’ve heard from children all over the county – they are ambitious, they want to do well and they want good jobs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The buzzy students at Thornhill Community Academy are no different.

“If we are serious about helping more young people into work, we must give them the advice, guidance and, vitally, the work experience to help them achieve their ambitions.”

News.title: Hero Israeli plumber who controlled plunging jet learned to fly from TV SHOW as he shares incredible survival story
News.content:
Next

THE hero Israeli plumber who took control of the plunging Flydubai plane has revealed he learned to fly from a TV show.

Yaniv Hayoun, was among the passengers who helped thwart “Israel’s 9/11” after they overpowered the knifeman who stabbed the pilot and allegedly planned to crash the flight.



Incredibly, Yaniv has revealed he knew what to do with the controls after watching Air Crash Investigation – a TV show on major aviation disasters.

He revealed what went on inside the plane to Israel’s PM after safely landing in the country on Wednesday.



Yaniv told Benjamin Netanyahu: “We pinned him down to keep him secure and then I jumped into it (the cockpit) and pulled the controls.”

Incredulously, Netanyahu asked how he knew to pull in a backwards motion, to which he stated: “I watch Air Crash Investigations Mr Prime Minister.”

Prior to their sit-down conversation, Yaniv received a hero’s greeting at Tel Aviv airport from the Israeli president who hugged him tightly as blood remained splattered on his clothing.

Yaniv told how he helped subdue the alleged knife-wielding co-pilot, after barging into the flight deck.



He said: “I pushed the door; the pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door so it was hard for us to open.

“We pulled him out – it was a matter of seconds.”

He then called his friends for help, putting the assailant in a chokehold before dragging him out from the cockpit and grabbing the controls in an incredible show of bravery.



When the plane began to level as he gripped the controls, an off-duty pilot told Yaniv that he would take it from there.

Prime Minister Netanyahu praised the hero for his “tremendous resourcefulness”.

President Donald Trump praised Yaniv’s “amazing” actions, revealing him to be a plumber.



The incident caused the aircraft to plummet 17,400 feet in less than two minutes, flight tracking data shows, with passengers believing they were going to die.

Graphic video taken onboard the plane showed a gruesome scene as passengers and crew aided the wounded pilot.

The captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, suffered serious injuries in the incident which has now been dubbed by officials as “Israeli 9/11”.

Machchhar has about 15 years of experience flying for commercial airlines and had logged almost 10,000 hours on Boeing 737s, according to his social media.

He bravely fought to defend the plane – and the 174 passengers on board – while being attacked with a blade.



Despite his wounds, the veteran pilot managed to unlock the door of the cockpit and alert the crew of the ruthless attack.

This bought just enough time for Yaniv and other passengers to burst through and subdue his co-pilot.

The two off-duty pilots were onboard the aircraft as a potential regional rerouting meant the flight may have required a longer path, The Jerusalem Post reports.

This would push the original crew past their legal duty hours, making extra staff necessary.

There is no indication that their presence was due to an advanced security warning.



Authorities suspect the incident may have been an attempted terrorist attack, Israeli officials and an Israeli source familiar with the situation told CNN.

Israel’s defence minister Israel Katz said early intelligence suggests the co-pilot wanted to carry out a “jihadist terror attack”.

The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar is in stable condition and is being treated in a hospital in Tabuk.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has praised the captain for his “extraordinary bravery.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said on X: “My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery.



“Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back… preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster. He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.”

News.title: Carer facing jail after using patient’s bank card to pay for more than £2k of Deliveroo takeaways
News.content:
Next

A CARER is facing jail after using a patient’s bank card to pay for more than £2,000 of Deliveroo takeaways.

Sophia Anderson, 39, also splurged £5,000 of Carol O’Neile’s cash on online gambling and Amazon purchases.



Prosecutor Mark Edwards told Leeds magistrates’ court that housebound Carol was “a vulnerable female” who needed constant care.

He added of Anderson: “The defendant visited her home regularly.



“She would take a list and her bank card and do her shopping for her.”

He said it was “normal practice” for patients to give cash to their carers for shopping, but because the victim was housebound she was unable to visit cash machines.



Mr Edwards added: “Hence, she gave her card and the PIN number to the defendant.”

But in October 2024, Carol received an alert from her bank about unusual spending.

It was then that she found huge sums missing.

Anderson, of Headingley, West Yorks, was a healthcare assistant for the firm Be Kind.



She admitted fraud on Wednesday and faces up to three years behind bars.

She will be sentenced next month.

News.title: Unabomber Ted Kaczynski’s sister-in-law dies as husband pays tribute to courageous wife who urged FBI tip
News.content:
Next

THE woman whose intuition helped bring Unabomber Ted Kaczynski to justice and end his 17-year reign of terror has died.

Linda Patrik, who persuaded her husband, the Unabomber’s brother David Kaczynski, to investigate after she first suspected her brother-in-law could be the notorious terrorist, died on February 2 after a brief battle with ovarian cancer.



David, 76, described his wife as a “deeply spiritual person with a great capacity for empathy” after a 65-year bond that began when they met as schoolchildren and eventually turned to love later in life.

They were married for 36 years before her death.



In a moving written tribute shared exclusively with The U.S. Sun, he said Linda was “the person most responsible for ending the Unabomber’s reign of violence and for saving lives in the process.”

He added that despite receiving “small credit” for her critical role, Linda’s “insight, compassion, and gentle diligence” guided him through the agonizing decision over whether to turn in his own brother.



“People say, ‘David, you made this very painful, ethical decision,” he said.

“Typically the decision has been attributed to me, but it was actually founded in a process of us.”

News of her death comes as Ted’s descent from gifted Harvard student to notorious serial bomber is revisited in Netflix’s new movie Unabomber.

The film stars Jacob Tremblay as a young Ted, Russell Crowe as Harvard psychologist Henry Murray and Shailene Woodley as fictional FBI agent Joanne Miller.



But behind the Hollywood retelling is the remarkable story of Linda, a philosophy professor who had never even met Ted but whose instincts helped unravel a case that had baffled authorities for years.

Ted terrorized America by mailing and planting 16 bombs that killed three people and injured 23 between 1978 and 1995.

The Harvard-educated mathematician targeted people linked to universities, airlines and technology while living as a recluse in a tiny cabin without electricity or running water in the Montana wilderness.

His identity remained a mystery, until the publication of his sprawling anti-technology manifesto in 1995 provided Linda and David with the crucial clues that led them to suspect Ted.



David told The U.S. Sun he believes he may have remained “deep in denial” if his “soulmate” Linda hadn’t encouraged him to look at the similarities and ultimately tip off the feds.

“I think it was without Linda’s persistence, her intuition that this could be my brother, that this was a serious moral issue,” he said.

“I probably would have easily just stuck it in the drawer and slipped into denial. Who wants to face something that awful unless you really have to?”

“We were in this together.”



Linda knew about her husband’s estranged older brother through David’s stories and Ted’s angry, ranting letters, which a psychiatrist believed suggested he was mentally ill.

Her suspicions were first raised in Paris in 1995, when reports about the still-unidentified Unabomber reminded her of Ted’s fierce opposition to technology and the views expressed in his earlier writings.

David recalled her reasoning: “She’s thinking he’s angry, he’s mentally ill, he’s against technology. Could he be the Unabomber?”

He was initially dismissive, but when the 35,000-word manifesto was published in The Washington Post, Linda urged him to read it and compare it with his brother’s writings.

“I thought I would read it and tell her, ‘Look, I know Ted’s writing. I know how he thinks. This isn’t him,'” David recalled.



“And instead, oh my gosh, you know?”

As they compared the manifesto with more than 100 letters from Ted that David had saved, it became clear he had a life-changing decision to make.

One morning David said he woke believing the situation had been a bad dream, before realizing: “It’s not a nightmare. I’m really seriously considering the possibility that my brother is a serial murderer.”

Soon afterward, sitting across from Linda at their breakfast table, he admitted he believed there was a “50-50 chance” Ted was the Unabomber.



The couple faced an agonizing choice: remain silent and risk another innocent person being killed, or alert authorities knowing David’s brother could face the death penalty.

“If we do nothing and some other innocent person is killed, and it turns out Ted is responsible, we go through the rest of our lives with blood on our hands,” David recalled.

But he also feared, “What would it be like if I turned my brother in? I had my brother’s blood on my hands. How could I live with myself then?”

Overwhelmed, David asked Linda if they could stop discussing Ted for two weeks, hoping some answer to what he called their “awful, impossible dilemma” would come to him.



Linda agreed, but quietly continued searching for a way to establish whether their suspicions were right, contacting a childhood friend and exploring whether experts could compare Ted’s letters with the manifesto.

The couple eventually received an assessment that there was a 60 percent chance the writings came from the same person and took their suspicions to authorities, leading investigators to Ted, who was arrested at his Montana cabin on April 3, 1996.

After his arrest, David and Linda fought to save Ted from the death penalty, with David saying it became their “number one mission.”

Ted ultimately avoided execution, pleading guilty in 1998 and receiving life without parole.

He died by suicide in federal custody in 2023 at the age of 81.



David and Linda would eventually receive the $1 million reward offered for information leading to the Unabomber’s capture, but had no idea about it when they decided to come forward.

“We didn’t know about the reward before contacting attorney Tony Bisceglie,” David said.

“My first reaction when he told me was: ‘Give the money to the victims!’ Linda agreed 100%. No discussion needed.”

“We weren’t going to profit by turning in a loved one.”

Yet David believes Linda never received the recognition she deserved, telling The U.S. Sun she was “really the key player” with “the insight, and the courage, and the skill to help me see the truth here.”



After Martin Luther King Jr.’s assassination in 1968, Linda joined white college students working alongside Black civil rights activists in Cleveland, according to David, and later became an outspoken feminist.

She earned a PhD in philosophy from Northwestern University and spent 35 years teaching at Union College, while also teaching Buddhist philosophy and debate for 20 summers at the Nitartha Institute.

Linda and David had known each other since seventh grade, when he remembers her choosing him as her lab partner in an advanced chemistry class, and their decades-long friendship eventually turned to love before they married in 1990 at the age of 40.

Looking back at how their lives eventually intertwined, David joked: “That’s when I learned what chemistry was all about.”

The couple shared a love of art, philosophy and Buddhism, and although they never had children, they built a rich life together surrounded by close friends and the family.



They eventually worked together as co-directors of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra, a Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Woodstock, New York, before retiring to David’s beloved West Texas desert in 2015.

Around four years before her death, Linda was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s, and as words increasingly escaped her, David said the qualities that had defined his wife remained unmistakable.

“Her touch, her presence, her smile were just as powerful as ever, if not more powerful,” he said.

Her final illness came with devastating speed, with increasing discomfort leading to an ovarian cancer diagnosis and doctors telling David they may have just “a week or two” together rather than the “month or two” he had hoped for.

“And four days later, she was gone,” he said.



The couple shared what David called “really wonderful days together” before he lost the love of his life.

On February 1, the day before Linda died, they attended a Methodist church where David told the congregation about her diagnosis and worshippers gathered around her to pray.

“It was very moving,” he recalled.

Afterwards, they went to one of their favorite restaurants, where David said Linda had a “good appetite” despite having struggled to eat in the days before.

They returned home and spent their final evening together watching movies, with David still unaware how little time they had left.



“I just had no indication that this would happen so quickly,” he said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Linda died in the early hours of the following morning, just four days after her cancer diagnosis.

David has now poured his grief into a collection of poems dedicated to Linda, writing, “Certainly, the best of my life — my time with Linda — has ended, though her spirit and influence will follow me till I die.”

News.title: Teacher who starred in hit Channel 4 show ‘giggled while he sexually assaulted teen girl after offering her lift home’
News.content:
'SEX ATTACK' Teacher who starred in hit Channel 4 show ‘giggled while he sexually assaulted teen girl after offering her lift home’







Next

A TEACHER who appeared on a hit Channel 4 show allegedly giggled while he sexually assaulted a teen girl after offering her a lift home.

Gareth Ritter, 44, had a leading role in the documentary series Educating Cardiff, as assistant head of Willows High School.



But Ritter allegedly carried out a sex assault on the 17-year-old girl after giving her a lift home from an event.

Ritter told the girl he needed to stop off for “five minutes” to check a flat he owned in Cardiff Bay.



A court heard when they went into the flat Ritter took her to see the view from his balcony before commenting on her dress.

He then allegedly touched the girl – who was not a pupil at his school – without permission.



She told the court: “He mentioned his wife did not know about the flat and he liked to keep his money separate. He made several comments about how I looked.”

She said Ritter told her “look at your t**s” and began to giggle before moving his hand to touch her.



The girl said: “He put his right hand on my lower back and moved down to my bum.”

Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court heard Ritter asked the girl if she wanted to see the bedroom and went inside.

But she told the jury she did not follow him, and when he came out of the room he touched her again and put his tongue inside her mouth.

“My back was towards the wall and Gareth was in front of me,” she said.

She said he put “one hand out behind my back and down to my bum and then lent in and kissed me”.



“I remember his tongue going into my mouth. I was against the wall and could not step back,” she added.

“I turned my face away. I couldn’t go anywhere.”

The court heard that she put out her hands out and told him: “I don’t do this. I am a good girl.

“I felt really uncomfortable. I had nowhere to go. I found it hard to say stop and did not know how to react.”

Ritter allegedly agreed to take her home but told her to keep what happened “between us”.



She said: “‘He said ‘are you going to tell anyone?’ I said no. What do you say in that situation? He was someone I looked up to. How do you confront that? Do I argue with someone giving me a lift home?”

Jenny Yeo, defending, said Ritter denies kissing or touching the 17 year-old.

She said: “Nothing at all untoward happened in the flat that night.”

The court heard Ritter had admitted separate charges relating to indecent images of the complainant after they were found on his phone.

The trial continues.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ritter worked as a music teacher and assistant head during the Channel 4 show and in 2013, he won the Pearson award for innovative use of technology.

Ebbw Valley Brass said Ritter – a four-time Welsh conductor of the year – had resigned “due to personal reasons”.

News.title: Burnham talks about giving the public more control over how Britain is run but his half-baked ideas do the opposite
News.content:
Time to deliver







Next

ANDY Burnham has spoken a lot this week about giving the public more control over how the country is run.

Yet he served up two half-baked ideas that would do the opposite — rigging the voting system and unpicking Brexit.

Our PM loves to portray himself as a listening leader but turns a deaf ear when it suits.



Now he plans to ignore referendums that rejected both ballot box meddling and EU membership.



He calls scrapping our first-past-the-post elections “reform” but it’s a recipe for chaos.

Look at Europe’s flimsy systems that deliver endless, weak coalition governments where nothing gets done.

The PM insists proportional representation — shunned by 68 per cent in the 2011 referendum — would ensure “everyone’s voice is heard”.

But it won’t.

If Burnham gets his way, YOU won’t get to decide the agenda any more.

Instead, politicians will trade away your vote in shady, back-room stitch-ups.

If that’s not enough, he wants to surrender our hard-won powers to unelected bureaucrats in Brussels.



Backsliding on Brexit would betray the biggest democratic mandate in British history, when even in the PM’s own Makerfield constituency two-thirds voted to leave.

Does he really want to reopen the toxic debate of a decade ago?

MPs would be bogged down in long, mind-numbing rows over terms and conditions demanded by Brussels.

Britain has no time to waste on constitutional navel-gazing and EU love-ins.

Burnham should get a grip and fix the real problems — most of which he failed to mention in his conference speech.



That means tackling the boats crisis, rebuilding our Armed Forces, fixing the economy and getting people off benefits and into proper jobs.

It’s time to end talking shops and start delivering for Britain.

Third degree

BRITAIN can no longer afford to be naive about China.

The discovery of a spy network infiltrating our top universities is an impossible-to-ignore red flag.

Open research must not become an open door for espionage.



Safeguards should be put in place swiftly to ensure national security is not compromised by legitimate scientific co-operation.

The Government must act swiftly to ensure our world-class universities are never exploited by hostile foreign powers.

What a life

ESTHER Rantzen’s death spells the loss of a fearless champion of the most vulnerable in society.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The much-loved television star undoubtedly saved many lives through her Childline charity.

Her warmth, courage and energetic campaigning will be missed by many whose lives she touched.

News.title: Mass migration fears after Burnham admits he could drag UK back into the EU ‘and open borders to half a billion people’
News.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham has sparked mass immigration fears — after admitting he could drag Britain back into the European Union.

The Prime Minister said reversing Brexit entirely with a second referendum in the party manifesto for the next election was “possible”.



It has opened up behind-the-scenes splits within Labour as Red Wall MPs fear a voter backlash.

Mr Burnham confirmed that a return to full Brussels membership was an option after using his Labour conference speech to slam the “harmful” decision to leave the bloc.



It would mean signing back up to the free movement of people that gives citizens of the 26 member states the right to live and work in each other’s countries.

Despite pledging earlier this year he would not seek to rerun the Brexit debate, he said: “We can’t really avoid the question anymore.”



Asked if a referendum is on the table, he said: “Yeah, things are possible. I think where we are isn’t good enough.”

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told The Sun: “Andy Burnham demonstrated to voters his word means absolutely nothing.

“It’s now obvious Open Borders Burnham wants a return to freedom of movement. If he gets his way, we will open our borders to nearly half a billion people.”

Around 452million EU citizens would be given the legal right to live in the UK should Britain return to free movement.



Border control was a driving force behind the 52 per cent vote to quit the bloc in 2016.

But immigration shot up post-Brexit, peaking at nearly a million in 2023, as politicians opened the floodgates to non-EU nationals.

Mr Burnham said that EU immigration was more fluid and short-term whereas non-EU immigrants are more likely to settle for good.



A UK-EU summit later this year will kickstart a process for the PM to draw up a range of options.

This could also involve sticking with the status quo, becoming an associate member, or rejoining the Customs Union that would require Britain to follow trade rules.

Mr Burnham, who joined in singing the socialist anthem The Red Flag on the last day of the conference in Liverpool yesterday, said Britain should consider its position.

He said: “I think it’s right to have a quite calm discussion about what broadly are our options, is there a centre of gravity or a consensus around one of them, and then see where British public opinion is.”

The comments have opened a huge split inside Labour, with Cabinet ministers and Red Wall MPs warning against dragging Britain back into the Brexit wars.



One Cabinet minister told The Sun the Government should be looking forward, not to the past.

They said: “There are huge challenges coming down the track, from AI to new technology, where being able to move faster and make our own decisions is a massive advantage.

“We should be focused on the future and not relitigating arguments the country thought it had settled.”

The move also risks infuriating Labour MPs in Leave-backing seats, with one pointing out Mr Burnham had previously struck a very different tone on the subject.



In May, while fighting to return to Westminster, Mr Burnham insisted: “I’m not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU.”

Unite boss Sharon Graham had said at the conference: “The British people voted for Brexit.

“I think if we’re going down a road of trying to undo that, I think that will be seen as a problem.”

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has previously rejected rejoining the Customs Union, arguing Britain must retain the freedom to strike its own trade deals.



Mr Burnham made immigration key to his argument for closer ties with Brussels — claiming at the conference on Tuesday that Brexit had “done more harm than good”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But his own Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood had told MPs last month it was a “mistake” to see the EU’s new migration pact as “some sort of new silver bullet” that would solve the Channel crisis.

She also pointed out that the Government’s bilateral deal with France had already returned more migrants than Britain managed under the EU’s old Dublin system.

News.title: Grow a pair Burnham and hit benefits cheats & migrant chancers with your ‘tough love’ cuts… not hard-up pensioners
News.content:
Next

OH look, Andy Burnham has found a pair of balls and is finally taking the axe to Britain’s bloated benefits bill.

Bravo! Crack open the spumante.





But wait, hang on, what’s this?

The “benefits” he wants to trim are not the billions squandered on lazy dossers who can’t be arsed to get a job.

It’s not BMW-driving PIP fraudsters, ripping everyone off with their phoney tales of anxiety, who he’s talking about.

He’s not about to stop spraying cash at all those rapists, deviants and fake gays breaking into Britain after ­crossing the Channel in a flimsy dinghy.

Oh no, it’s the old folks’ modest state pensions that Burnham has prioritised for some tough love.

So, boom, there goes the triple lock, “adjusted” to a double lock and crucially removing the part — the link to average earnings growth — that has done the most to lift pensions up every year.

This announcement, ostensibly to help fund a new social care system, was, of course, met with the kind of automatic clapping that becomes utterly meaningless at party conferences (especially given that half the ­Cabinet were said to have been against it).

But outside the hall in Liverpool you could almost hear the sound of Britain’s pensioners letting out an almighty, “F*** you, Burnham!”





Pardon their French but you can understand why.

Britain’s state pension, despite its annual increases, is unequivocally modest — £241.30 a week — and one of the lowest in the G7.

For around a million people in Britain that is their only income — an equivalent annual salary of HALF a 40-hour-a-week job on minimum wage.

This year’s weekly rise was £11, enough for a couple of extra pints and a bag of crisps, or, more pertinently as the nights draw in, a few hours of heating.

But the kicker here is not simply that our silver surfers will have less silver than they were promised by successive governments (Tory Chancellor George Osborne introduced the triple lock in 2011).

No, there is further hi- octane fuel to their rage.

And that is that dipping their pensions is being ­prioritised over other areas of arguably far more urgent Government cost-cutting.

Tweaking the triple lock might have been more ­palatable if — and it’s a very big if — Burnham and his head-in-the-sand Benefits Party were not recklessly draining the public cash reservoir elsewhere.



I mentioned some of these earlier on but let’s add some numbers.

I’ll start with the £207billion we are expected to blow on (non-pension) welfare payments in the next year.

A figure that becomes more inflated as the feckless and the fraudulent realise just how easy it is to game the system.

More than FOUR MILLION are now sucking up PIP payments, increasingly for overexaggerated and imagined problems.

Then there’s the £8billion a year we’re blowing on dealing with our migrant ­crisis. “Oh well, £2billion of that comes from the foreign aid budget,” I hear some lefties cry.

Well, yes, about that foreign aid budget.

Despite recent efforts to get it down, we are still spending more than £13billion a year on foreign aid projects such as handing out rubber ­johnnies to randy fellas in nuclear state Pakistan.

And what about Ed Miliband’s mad pursuit of Net Zero, a set of suicidal policies that even Tony Blair has admitted are “doomed to fail”.



It’s costing us £30billion a year.

Of course, if Andy Burnham really cared about extravagant spending on pensions he could look at the £56billion handed over to gold-plated public sector retirement payments, a figure that has ­DOUBLED over the past ten years as The Blob continues to swell.

But Our Andy doesn’t seem too fussed about any of that — it would hurt all his mates on the public sector gravy train.

He would rather nickel and dime those ­trying to enjoy the last years of their lives.

Our new Prime Minister had made a lot of noise about making hard decisions to fix Britain.

As he told his rictus-grinned party faithful in his Hallmark card-worthy speech on Tuesday: “Someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off.”

Well, he might be doing the ripping but, as ever, it’s the rest of us who will be feeling the pain.

DELIGHTED to see some new shoots appearing on the stump of the felled ­Sycamore Gap tree, right.

Can’t wait to see it back to its former glory in, er, 2146.

A LOAD OF RAN FLAKES ONE of the first “grown-up” books my mother gave me was To The Ends Of The Earth, by Sir Ranulph Fiennes. A big fat hardback, it charted “Ran’s” extraordinary account of how between ’79 and ’82 he circumnavigated the globe via the poles. It was a riveting Boy’s Own story with all its jungles, swamps and freezing polar winds. It’s a distant memory now but learning of the sheer determination of the man never left me. So I find it incredibly sad that he is now hidden from view, left to crumble in a nursing home (or tumbledown farm as may now be the case). I can’t imagine for a second that he is happy with this “arrangement”. Myriad theories swirl as to why he’s effectively been locked away, none of which paint certain family members in a very positive light. If they had a moral compass they would come out and explain themselves, or preferably let Sir Ranulph speak for himself. Habeas corpus and all that . . .

Stick to the day job, Tom



TOM CRUISE is a fine actor, but he’s best when he’s ­playing Tom Cruise.

You know, the wise- cracking pina colada shaker in Cocktail or the cocksure pilot in Top Gun, two of my favourite films built around that twinkle in the now 64-year-old’s eye.

Sadly his bleak new flick, Digger, has none of that charm. Hidden beneath some heavy-handed prosthetic make-up, Cruise plays a loathsome oil tycoon who is slowly, then quickly, destroying the planet.

It’s a hell of a leap from his last outing, ­Mission: Impossible 8, and clearly he wants us to know he has more in his locker than just playing the geezer who jumps out of planes.

But his chaotic turn as the swivel-eyed Digger Rockwell left me cold. It was a role made for someone naturally kooky, like Woody Harrelson, not the Peter Pan of ­Hollywood.

Cruise should relax – we know he’s a great actor.

With this itch now scratched I hope he gets back to doing what he does best and stops trying to be such a, ahem, maverick.

AUNTY'S CRAVEN NOT sure why Katherine Ryan had to apologise for calling Posh Spice a c**t on Have I Got News For You. I’m sure Mrs Beckham – arriviste of the notoriously bitchy fashion world – has been called worse. But you do have to wonder why it took the BBC nearly a year to come to their craven conclusion. Once again the paranoid Beeb is tying itself in knots when it comes to what counts as comedy. It was happy to broadcast it (HIGNFY is pre-recorded) but then fell apart when just TWO people complained. What a joke.

ROONEY HO-HUM TRUTHS

WHEN the trailer dropped for Disney+’s The Real Rooneys a week or so ago, I thought, “Looks alright, that.” Then I watched the show.

Now I wasn’t expecting to get a full deep dive into all of Wayne’s granny-shagging and adventures in Prostitute Land.



There were enough shots of the Rooneys’ all-seeing agent to remind us that this would never be anything more than a Hello! magazine-strength hagiography.

It was like an eight times 40-minute Omaze promotion, with so many sweeping shots of their soulless mega-mansion I was waiting for Coleen to start telling me how to enter the prize draw.

Something I would have thought twice about as I watched Wayne and his brood churning up the manicured gardens in buggies like Lotto Lout Michael Carroll.

Look, Wayne and Coleen seem like a nice enough couple, and despite his appalling treatment of her during their marriage they do seem to be close.

But what this series shows is that they don’t really have anything interesting to say.

Wayne may be making a good fist of being a Match Of The Day pundit.

But that compelling commentary is rarely on display in The Real Rooneys, which ultimately – to borrow a critique from the great man himself – “was crap”.

POOR old Man City – from heroes to zeroes in less than a week.

But what brilliant timing, coming in the international break.

Gives us rival fans a solid three weeks to come up with a songbook of new chants.



All set to Oasis tunes, naturally.

AAAH, didn’t Totnes Castle look pretty as a picture this week, wrapped in that lovely rainbow Pride flag?

It’s nice to see this charming 11th Century castle is so welcoming to being adorned with flags.

I think I’ll pop down with my 300 metre-long St George’s Cross banner. Quite apt for an English Heritage-run fortress, don’t you think?

Yeah, right. Can you imagine?

I wouldn’t even be able to get my stepladder up before some purple-haired busybody had convinced a local bobby to arrest me for being “racist”.

News.title: FlyDubai live: Brave pilot fought to stop 'Israel's 9/11' despite 'being stabbed'
News.content:
The pilot allegedly stabbed on board FlyDubai flight FZ1073 has been named as Indian national Smit Machchhar, with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu calling him 'extraordinarily brave'

A pilot on a FlyDubai flight bound for Tel Aviv who was allegedly stabbed by his colleague has been called "extraordinarily brave" for fighting to prevent what Israeli security forces believe could have been the country's "9/11".

The wounded pilot who has been named as Indian national Smit Machchhar, is said to have opened the cockpit door so others could overpower the attacker.

Mr Netanyahu said: "Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster.

"He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals. I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery." Mr Machchhar is in a stable condition in hospital.

FlyDubai flight FZ1073 issued an emergency hijacking alert shortly after 6.30am BST today. Mr Netanyahu alleged one of the pilots "stabbed the other pilot and apparently tried to crash the plane".

Israeli security services believe there may have been a plan to crash the aircraft into a city in a "9/11 scenario".

Mr Netanyahu has also met a passenger named Yaniv who he says "broke into the cockpit" and is a "great hero".

Yaniv says in footage: "When I entered, I saw the attacker on the instruments, between the two seats...there were no pilots in the seats. One was down, one was on the instruments. And another guy came in with me. I grabbed the attacker, put him in a chokehold, and pulled him - first and foremost - outside." He says he then pulled at the controls.

Two other pilots, who were on board ahead of connection flight from Tel Aviv, reportedly helped take control of the Boeing 737 MAX aircraft and land it. A passenger has claimed one of them was British.

Have you been involved in the FlyDubai incident? If so, please get in touch and share your story by emailing livenews@reachplc.com

News.title: Met Office shares its El Niño outlook which points to increased UK flood risk
News.content:
Met Office shares its El Niño outlook which points to increased UK flood risk

The Met Office says there is heightened potential for wet, windy and stormy weather and flooding this autumn — which forecasters say is in part due to the El Niño phenomenon

View 3 Images Tewkesbury, which is in Gloucestershire, suffered flooding in February (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

Chilly temperatures and unsettled conditions could be on their way to the UK over the coming months as El Niño continues to wreak havoc on weather patterns across the globe.

‌



The Met Office says there is "heightened potential" for wet, windy, stormy weather and flooding this autumn. Forecasters also cautioned the phenomenon could interfere with cold winds near the Arctic, known as the stratospheric polar vortex.

‌



But the latest forecasts indicate El Niño is currently more likely to trigger a drop in temperatures this winter, rather than producing a polar vortex over the UK this autumn. Downpours are already forecast for October, including a band of showers to make landfall on Saturday for many regions.

‌



View 3 Images El Nino is likely to cause extreme weather conditions (Image: WMO)

Atmospheric waves set off by El Niño destabilise the polar vortex, also raising the likelihood of heavy snowfall, according to experts, reports the Express. The Met Office's long-range outlook covering the next three months points to higher-than-average chances of rain, strong winds and mild conditions.

The probability of the October to December period being wet overall is twice the normal level, while windy and mild weather is also more likely than usual.

‌



Dr Will Lang, chief forecaster at the Met Office, described it as a "subtle shift in the odds" rather than a certainty that conditions would be wetter, milder and windier. He said: "We are going in with a heightened potential for wet weather, heightened potential for potentially stormy conditions, and that leads through to a heightened potential for flooding."

Early indications also suggest that towards the end of winter, there is an increased likelihood of drier, colder and more settled conditions. The Met Office states that the expected conditions are consistent with the influence of El Niño on UK autumn and winter weather.

View 3 Images The phenomenon could bring storms, heavy rain, and snow to the UK in the coming months (Image: Getty)

‌



El Niño is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that originates in the Pacific Ocean when sea surface temperatures across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific become considerably warmer than usual, altering atmospheric circulation patterns and impacting weather across the globe.

A record-breaking "Godzilla" El Niño has already taken hold in recent months. These latest predictions follow a drier than average September across much of the UK, which came on the back of a record-breaking hot summer with widespread drought across England and Wales, bringing hosepipe bans, damage to crops and wildlife, and outbreaks of fire.

The UK received just 77% of its average summer rainfall, with every region except north-west Scotland enduring a dry summer. Parts of southern and eastern England were particularly badly affected, including a remarkable run of 62 consecutive days without rain at Wisley, Surrey.

Article continues below

The Environment Agency has warned that the drought will persist until reservoirs and aquifers are fully replenished, with above-average rainfall required to restore conditions to normal levels.

News.title: Boy, 8, died after being kicked in the head by horse in Warrington stables
News.content:
Boy, 8, died after being kicked in the head by horse in Warrington stables

Louie Isaac Webster, from Wigan, entered a fenced-off arena while his mum's back was turned, an inquest has heard

View Image An air ambulance landed at the scene (Image: Liverpool Echo)

An eight-year-old boy died after being kicked in the head by a horse after he entered a fenced-off arena while his mum's back was turned.

‌



Louie Isaac Webster, from Wigan, was at the The Beeches Livery Centre, in Warrington, with his mum Rebecca and teenage sister, whose horse was kept there, when tragedy struck.

‌



Louie had complained of being thirsty, so Rebecca told him to sit on a bench near the stables while she went to their car to get a drink. She had been gone "a matter of minutes" when Louie was struck, Cheshire Coroner's Court heard today (Wednesday).

‌



Det Insp Joanna Morgan, who led the investigation into Louie's death said his older sister was "experienced and confident with horses", and had used The Beeches Livery Centre for about three months. Louie had not visited the livery before as his behaviour was described as "challenging" due to suspected ADHD.

River Wear deaths: First pictures of three teens killed when car plunged into water READ MORE :

Coroner Victoria Davies said: "Louie complained he was thirsty and she (Rebecca Webster) returned to her vehicle to get him a drink. Rebecca described it as a short walk to the car, around 15 to 20 paces, however the view of the yard was obscured by a horse box.

"She described being at her car for minutes when she then heard her daughter shouting at Louie to 'get out', and then shouting 'mum' in a panicked tone."

‌



The teenage girl was shown on the car park CCTV running up to her mum and another livery user as she told them Louie had been kicked by the horse. All three returned to the arena, where they found Louie lying unresponsive near the fence.

Several livery users performed CPR on the eight-year-old as emergency services were called to the scene. Air and land ambulances attended, and Louie was taken by land ambulance to Alder Hey Children's Hospital cardiac arrest. Despite the efforts of medics, he could not be revived and died at 7.45pm.

The inquest heard Louie's sister had also been interviewed by police. She said her mum had told Louie to sit on a bench near the stables and wait. However, he walked up to the arena and entered it through one of the gaps in the fence.

Article continues below

At this point, she said, she had stopped riding the horse and was sitting on it, using her mobile phone. Louie had walked up to the animal and stroked its belly, causing it to become scared and kick out with its back legs, the inquest heard.

Louie's sister told police that she had owned two other horses previously, and Louie had enjoyed stroking one of them on its belly. She said she had warned Louie about the new horse as it was an ex-racehorse, but he may not have understood due to his suspected ADHD.

The coroner handed down a conclusion of accidental death.

News.title: Bloodied passenger on FlyDubai flight says: 'We’ve just taken control of the terrorists'
News.content:
Bloodied passenger on FlyDubai flight says: 'We’ve just taken control of the terrorists'

An off-duty British pilot is said to have raced into the cockpit and pulled the Boeing 737 Max out of a nosedive after "attempted jihadist attack" on the Israel-bound flight

View 7 Images Assaf Regavim - with blood on his face - records himself begging for assistance, saying: "Whoever is hearing me, we need help" (Image: X)

A wounded passenger on a plane subject to an alleged attempted jihadist terror attack begged for help — and said "we’ve just taken control of the terrorists".

The remark was said as a relief pilot helped to land the Israel-bound jet after one pilot stabbed the other in the cockpit and allegedly tried to crash the plane. The hero, identified as a British national by fellow passengers, raced to the front of the FlyDubai Boeing 737 Max as the attacker was pinned to the ground.

He is said to have pulled the plane out of a nose-dive and stabilised it before landing it at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia. Passengers said the fight broke out at the front of the plane just 90 minutes into the 1,300-mile flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

Distressing mid-air footage sent by people on board – some soaked in blood – showed them restraining the attacker and pleading for help. Graphic video also showed one of the pilots also drenched in blood.

Killer who fled custody twice and murdered pensioner in Costa del Sol whines he should be freed READ MORE :

View 7 Images Yaniv Hayun helped prevent the hijacking (Image: Kobi Gideon/GPO)

Israel’s defence minister Israel Katz described yesterday’s incident as an attempted jihadist terror attack.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilot who carried out the stabbing had been arrested. The victim, Smit Machchhar, was last night stable in hospital.

A video shared by Israeli media shows a bloodied passenger, Assaf Regavim, saying: “We’re here – the plane – we’ve just taken control of the terrorists.

“We’re about to land. Anyone who hears me: we need help. We’re landing in Tabuk. All onboard the flight are healthy and in one piece – aside from the pilot. We need help.”

View 7 Images Mr Hayun was seen with bloodstains on his clothes aboard the Flydubai commercial flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

Another passenger, Almog Itali, described the two pilots at the back of the plane as “relief pilots” who were due to operate a subsequent flight, adding one of them was British, while the other was European.

He said the exact details of what happened in the cockpit are unclear. Mr Itali, who said he had spoken to people from the front of the plane, added: “There are quite a few versions. What is clear is that there were two pilots in the front – one stabbed the other.”

The attack took place at 34,000ft. Officials said the plane nosedived 17,400ft in just two minutes before an “Israeli 9/11” was averted.

View 7 Images A flight-tracking map shows the route taken by FlyDubai flight FZ1073 before it made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. (Image: Flightradar24)

Fighter jets were scrambled to escort the aircraft during its emergency landing. The plane touched down at 8.44am local time. Travellers were recorded clapping and cheering.

Tensions are running high in the Middle East, with the ongoing conflict in Iran and Israel’s relentless shelling of Gaza.

Mr Netanyahu warned in recent days of unspecified, escalated security threats ahead of Israel’s October 27 election, sparking accusations of fear-mongering.

He said yesterday: “During the flight, as they were approaching Israel, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot and, apparently, tried to crash the plane with its passengers on board.”

View 7 Images Passengers were seen in tears of relief after eventually arriving at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel (Image: AP Photo/Ariel Schalit)

He said of those on board who intervened: “I salute these heroes, who displayed extraordinary resourcefulness and courage. They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.” A spokesman said he had ordered security to be ramped up on Israeli and non-Israeli carriers.

Mr Katz said the attack was “thwarted only thanks to the bravery of several Israeli passengers who broke into the cockpit, overpowered the terrorist and, with their own hands, restored control of the plane to another flight crew”.

‌



He added: “According to the initial information in our possession, the terrorist had one intention: to crash the plane.” Another Israeli official reportedly claimed: “One pilot stabbed the other and tried to do 9/11 – either hijack the plane to the ground or crash it. The plane started to dive, and a team of pilots who were present took control of the stabber and the plane – a dramatic disaster was averted.”

View 7 Images All passengers were reported safe following the emergency landing

Israel Ohayon, whose sister Miriam was on board the Flydubai flight, said she reported “pressure and panic” with passengers feeling that they were “staring death in the face”. He said she was sitting directly behind the pilots and had a good view as “a few Israelis took initiative” and subdued the attacker.

‌



He said: “Mentally, she’s not in a good state. We lost our brother on October 7, 2023, so this brings us back a little to that time.”

Another passenger who stormed the cockpit told Israeli media: “We jumped on the pilot with force and tied him up with headphones.”

Photographs from the flight show one passenger standing up in the aisle with his white T-shirt covered in blood.

‌



Another recorded a video with blood on his face, saying: “We’re here during the hijacking of an airplane. At this point we’ve subdued the terrorists, we’re approaching landing.

“Whoever is hearing me, we need help. We’re landing in Tabuk, apparently in Saudi Arabia. An unknown, unfamiliar area. On the plane, everybody is safe and sound, other than the pilot. We need help.”

Another passenger said: “We were either going to crash or be murdered. It was like a terrorist attack in mid-air.”

‌



View 7 Images Mr Regavim spoke to reporters (Image: Getty Images)

Yitzhak Lieber was one of the passengers who helped overpower the attacker. He sent a video to his children from the plane, saying: “There is a pilot who was seriously injured, they’ve evacuated him. We overpowered the terrorist and he is tied up.”

The video was later posted on social media. He said: “It was a very difficult incident. We

‌



will probably come home in a few hours. I need to change my clothes. Everything is full of blood, we caught him... we caught the terrorist.”

Flight data shows the plane dropped 17,400ft in just under two minutes, climbed 5,000ft and then fell another 7,000ft. An emergency “squawk code” was issued from the plane with 180 passengers on board, tracking data shows.

FlyDubai FZ1073 passenger claims British pilot landed plane

‌



The international emergency alert was followed by a 7500 code, meaning a hijacking or unlawful interference, as it entered Jordanian air space.

A spokesman for UAE based airliner Flydubai said: “An altercation occurred in the flight deck of flight FZ 1073, operating from Dubai International to Ben Gurion International Airport on September 30. The aircraft was successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport. All passengers and crew are safe and accounted for. We have deployed two replacement aircraft to Tabuk to relieve the passengers and crew.

“The underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation. We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation.

Article continues below

“Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved.”

News.title: Tyson Fury accuses Anthony Joshua of trying to CANCEL box-office fight for petty reason
News.content:
Tyson Fury accuses Anthony Joshua of trying to CANCEL box-office fight for petty reason

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are set to clash in Cardiff in mid-December and the pair have had their first chance to face-off at their pre-fight press conference

View 2 Images Tyson Fury during Wednesday's press conference (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury has revealed that negotiations between him and Anthony Joshua almost put their historic fight in doubt - with the name an apparent sticking point. The pair are set to clash in a historic bout on December 11 in Cardiff.

‌



The fight will finally see the two come together after protracted talks. And despite the fight now being set in stone, the Gypsy King has suggested that even in the days leading up to Wednesday evening's press conference, Joshua's camp were still complaining.

‌



Joshua however hit back by claiming that he had received a phone call about the naming rights - with Fury's camp keen to get his name at the front, to which he repeatedly replied "b******".

‌



Fury said: "In the build-up to this fight, Eddie and AJ were talking about being the landlord and the boss, the governors.

"When I look behind me, I only see one Don and that's Fury vs AJ. Now you've come to get the rent and I ain't f****** paying, because I'm number one. We're going to walk out seeing Tyson Fury versus his opponent Anthony Joshua - an old dosser who works for me."

Asked by Joshua why he takes the things that Hearn says personally, Fury replied: "I don't take it personally. Eddie Hearn is a sausage."

‌



How to buy tickets for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury row resolved after fight plunged into doubt READ MORE :

He added: "You've been crying behind the scenes to get out of this fight. I've checkmated you. You have to fight. I've said I'll fight anywhere. I've actually never won a world title here [in the UK]. Now it's on the line, we can become a three-time."

Despite calling out Joshua and his camp, Fury has however claimed that he would be happy to share a pint with the pair following their titanic clash.

He added: "GK is number one and you don't own anything. I'm the boss. I would have a beer with Eddie right now. The man is a good promoter and manager but I don't like his crying.

‌



"Have I ever been rude to Eddie? I would go for a beer with you today. Same for you AJ. I hope we can have a pint of Guinness together after this fight."

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua has responded to Tyson Fury's claims (Image: Getty Images)

The pair however did have a slight disagreement when it comes to a sparring session between them in 2010. On that incident, Fury said: "I've sparred a lot of amateur boxers in my time. AJ was in that ring; he knows what happened. There was a Rolex watch thing too."

Article continues below

Joshua responded: "He left the ring with a black eye as well. He left with a Rolex but he had a black eye."

He added: "I can't remember it. It was so many years ago. He spoke about it, it wasn't me. It was just another day. He went online and spoke to Steve Bunce about the experience. Sparring is meant to be kept in the gym."

The pair then had the first chance to face-off ahead of their fight, albeit the occasion appeared to be somewhat respectful between both Fury and Joshua.

News.title: River Wear deaths: First pictures of three teens killed when car plunged into water
News.content:
Two teen boys and one girl died after the Audi A3 they were in plunged into the River Wear in Sunderland - a 17-year-old boy who survived has been arrested on suspicion of death by dangerous driving

River Wear deaths: First pictures of three teens killed when car plunged into water

Three teenagers who died when the car they were in plunged into the River Wear in Sunderland have been named and pictured.

Jackson Duke, 17, and Luke Etheridge and Zara Shaw, both aged 16, were all in the black Audi A3 when it hurtled off the road near Wearmouth Bridge and entered the water shortly before 1.30pm yesterday (Tuesday). A 17-year-old boy who survived the crash has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and remains in custody.

Northumbria Police said enquiries "remain ongoing" to establish who was the driver of the car at the time it entered the water. The car was lifted from the river by crane after a painstaking recovery operation today.

All three of the teenagers who died went to Sunderland College. Jackson and Luke were from the Sunderland area, while Zara was from Houghton-le-Spring

A statement from the college said: "This is a heartbreaking loss for our college community, and the wider city of Sunderland.

"Everyone at Sunderland College extends our heartfelt thoughts and deepest condolences to their families, friends, and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time."

News.title: Dame Esther Rantzen: A presenter who campaigned for change
News.content:
Dame Esther Rantzen, known for her role presenting the BBC's That's Life! and for later establishing the Childline helpline, has died at the age of 86.

Her children confirmed her death in a statement, saying: "We are grateful she is finally at rest with her beloved husband, Desmond Wilcox, but we will miss her immeasurably."

"We hope the humour, ingenuity and audacity she brought to her work may continue to inspire you as it will do us."

The veteran broadcaster had been diagnosed with stage four lung cancer in January 2023 and in the years that followed, was a prominent campaigner supporting assisted dying.

News.title: UK believes Iran involved in RAF Fairford incident, PM says
News.content:
The government believes that Iran played a part in the RAF Fairford incident which resulted in five men being arrested and then bailed, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said.

"There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford," he told the BBC. He did not provide further details.

Iran has responded, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the UK leader was "barking up the wrong tree".

"I can confirm Iran's belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all," he wrote on social media.

Asked why the suspects had been released on bail - a decision which has been openly questioned by President Donald Trump - Burnham insisted the men were subject to the "strictest possible bail conditions".

Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said: "I will tell you, I would have said, 'don't let them have bail'. I'm surprised that they released them. I wouldn't have done that."

But Burnham said: "I think people need to understand that when it says released - that isn't as people might think. It's obviously with the strictest possible bail conditions.

"The authorities have this under the strongest grip and closest control, and I can assure you of that."

Burnham's comments come after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that the incident at RAF Fairford "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor".

News.title: China funding UK research and sending it to Beijing's spies, MI5 warns
News.content:
More than 100 academics linked to British institutions have unwittingly assisted China's espionage operations against the UK via a front company working for its intelligence and security services, MI5 has warned.

In the highly unusual public alert, the UK's internal security service warned universities and academics that continuing ties with China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) could ultimately lead to criminal charges for aiding a foreign state.

Security minister Dan Jarvis said MI5's warning exposed attempts by Chinese intelligence agencies to use British academic research to undermine UK national security.

A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in London said the accusation was "imaginary and purely fabricated".

Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, meanwhile said it was reviewing the alert and focusing on "supporting our universities as they assess any implications for existing or future partnerships".

In June, MI5 and its closest partners in the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, issued a joint warning that China's military intelligence services were targeting professional networking sites and online job platforms.

This new UK-specific alert goes further, revealing what the service says is a threat that has been growing within British academic institutions.

MI5 says that the CGTRI, sometimes translated as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), has "very strong ties" to the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS).

"MI5 has identified that the primary purpose of CGTRI is to fund academic research that directly improves MSS technical capability for espionage," it says.

"More than 100 UK-linked academics have contributed to projects funded by MSS via CGTRI," adding that in some cases the researches would not be aware of the front company's role in their project.

News.title: Teens who died in car that entered River Wear named
News.content:
Two teenage boys and a teenage girl who died when the car they were in ended up in the River Wear have been named by police.

Jackson Duke, 17, Luke Etheridge and Zara Shaw, both 16, were in a black Audi A3 that came off the road at Panns Bank near Wearmouth Bridge, Sunderland, and plunged into the water just before 13:30 BST on Tuesday.

Jackson and Luke were from Sunderland and Zara was from Houghton-le-Spring, a town about seven miles (11km) from the city. All were students at Sunderland College.

Northumbria Police said there were four people inside the car at the time and a 17-year-old boy, who managed to reach safety, had been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

News.title: Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, Burnham tells BBC
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said it is "possible" a future Labour election manifesto could promise a new in-out referendum on the European Union.

The prime minister told the BBC a referendum "wouldn't be the right thing to do right now" but the UK needed to "consider the options" for its relationship with the EU as "where we are isn't good enough".

It comes after he pledged in his Labour conference speech on Tuesday to explore closer ties with the bloc at a summit later this year.

The move could set up a huge dividing line at the next general election, with the Conservatives accusing Burnham of trying to "reopen old wounds by restarting the battles of the Brexit years".

As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, Burnham had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".

In an interview with BBC political editor Chris Mason, Burnham was challenged over whether he was reopening divisive arguments about rejoining the EU, despite promising not to in May.

In response, the PM said: "No, I'm not proposing that, am I? I am saying that in a context when we're looking at a 10-year plan for Britain, Britain needs to consider the options as to where we will be.

"That is way before you even get to anything that's put before the public, this is about now just looking at what are the broad options for our relationship."

He suggested these options could include staying "exactly as we are", a closer relationship similar to that being discussed by the EU and Canada or rejoining the EU customs union.

However, Burnham stressed that "to leap back to a proposal and a referendum on it wouldn't be the right thing to do right now".

Pressed over whether including an in-out referendum in a future Labour manifesto was a possibility, Burnham said: "Yes, things are possible. I think where we are isn't good enough."

News.title: We fear for our lives after being told our abusive exes will be freed from jail early
News.content:
Dame Nicole Jacobs, the domestic abuse commissioner for England and Wales, called the scheme "shameful" and said she's had "no assurance that the danger perpetrators pose has been properly considered and assessed with meaningful input from victims".

"Ultimately, we cannot ignore the fact that the early release scheme has caused untold damage to victims' confidence in the justice system," Dame Nicole added.

She said Prime Minister Andy Burnham "must take urgent steps to address this" and called on the probation service to be given "the resources it needs to safely manage more offenders in the community". She also called for additional funding for domestic abuse services to support victims.

A recent report raised serious concerns about electronic tagging, which can be used to monitor offenders' movements in the community. It found almost half of tags were not fitted on time.

Alice told the BBC she had been looking to buy a doorbell with a camera fitted to help make her feel safer, but said she cannot afford one. "I don't feel prepared in the slightest and I don't feel safe," she added.

"I think the early release scheme is a joke to victims and survivors, who spent years preparing for trial, going through evidence and re-traumatising themselves to go to court, just for the perpetrator of their crimes to be released after just 33% of their sentence".

The MoJ said: "Anyone who is released faces the toughest-ever controls on their movements, including world-first restriction zones and the largest expansion of electronic tagging, with victims having a say in their perpetrators' licence conditions."

News.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp after coach denies rift
News.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he has left Portugal's international camp and will explain the reasons why "in time".

It comes after head coach Jorge Jesus earlier said there was no rift with the captain, following claims the five-times Ballon d'Or winner had refused to train.

Ronaldo has said he considered retiring from international football after the World Cup in the summer but opted to continue as he chases down 1,000 career goals.

He was included in Jesus' 25-man squad for the current international break and started the opening Nations League game against Wales.

However, the Al-Nassr forward did not feature in Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway in Olso on Sunday and did not join his team-mates in going over to the visiting fans at the final whistle.

Instead, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United player headed to the changing rooms - prompting reports he was unhappy with the manager.

Speaking to media before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark on Thursday, Jesus said: "There was no incident whatsoever.

"Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that."

Jesus said he had told Ronaldo before the match he would not be starting, but might be brought on later in the game.

"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," he added.

Former Benfica manager Jesus also dismissed suggestions Ronaldo had refused to train on Tuesday, saying the 41-year-old instead had to do individual exercises for "mobility" and "strengthening" but would train as normal on Wednesday.

However, Ronaldo did not join his team-mates on the pitch in Denmark with Portuguese media sharing a video of him leaving Parken stadium alongside two members of the backroom staff.

And the player later took to Instagram to announce his departure.

"After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp," he wrote.

"In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave."

He added he wished his team-mates good luck in their forthcoming games.

Goncalo Ramos scored the winner against Norway and Jesus had said the AC Milan striker would again be preferred to Ronaldo against Denmark.

"If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."

The Portuguese Football Federation later confirmed Ronaldo's departure in a statement which added: "Preparation for the two matches against Denmark and Norway continue as planned with the 24 remaining squad members.

"The entire delegation remains totally focussed on the national team's next fixtures and on achieving the established objectives."

News.title: Singer Lola Young says vaping has made breathing feel like a 'chore'
News.content:
Singer Lola Young has said her breathing feels like a "chore" due to the effects of vaping.

In a TikTok video,, external the Grammy winner told her followers her lungs feel "battery powered".

The 25-year-old has previously acknowledged in videos she "should quit", but suggested in her latest post that is unlikely to happen any time soon.

Vocal coach Lizzii Hills has told BBC Newsbeat vaping is "not advised" for artists and that difficulty breathing can affect a singer's voice and performance.

"Somebody once said to me, 'Lola there will be a day when you wake up, you'll be 25 or 26, from a deep sleep, and you'll start to feel the effects of vaping'," the Messy singer said in her post.

"You know what I said? I said 'nah' and rolled my eyes.

"But let me tell you something, the day has come."

News.title: Residents near RAF Fairford left 'like sitting ducks'
News.content:
A couple, who asked not to be named, claims Whelford villagers were warned to stay home on Saturday night - hours before the alarm was first raised by a farmer.

The pair were evacuated from their home the following morning, after the vans were found abandoned at the end of their driveway.

But when the husband stepped outside, he said he was confronted by armed police.

"I was trying to get my wallet out to say, 'look I'm a resident here'," he said.

"Then one of them got out of the vehicle and put a gun on me, in my direction.

"Then the other officer also got out, put a gun on me, and said 'Who's asked you to leave?'."

The couple said they and and their terrified child were briefly trapped inside their home before managing to escape through a neighbour's property.

After being allowed to return home, the pair saw the van doors had been "blown off" and their contents emptied, with water butts and oil drums strewn on the ground.

"All of a sudden, you see on the news the five suspected terrorists have been released," the husband said.

"You're thinking, 'Is this for real?'.

"We've all been panicking for the best part of a day and a bit. Are our homes going to get blown up? Could we have been blown up?"

The family say they are "angry" over an absence of communication from authorities in the days leading up to the incident, alongside the lack of reassurance afterwards.

News.title: Burnham 'really concerned' if Man City owners sell up after rule breaches
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's owners decide to sell up after the club was found guilty of Premier League financial rule breaches.

The prime minister said the situation was "contested by Manchester City" and he praised the club's owners since 2008 - led by Sheikh Mansour, United Arab Emirates deputy prime minister and royal family member - for investing in Manchester.

An independent commission found the club guilty of the majority of the 115 charges they faced, a verdict that City are expected to appeal.

The club continue to deny any wrongdoing and have until 2 October to submit an appeal.

It comes as the Independent Football Regulator â set up by the government in 2025 â said the case had raised "serious issues".

The regulator suggested it would be exploring options â including whether to strip the owners of their licence to own the club â once the disciplinary process was completed.

Among the independent panel's findings were that City arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than Â£830m.

The Premier League said City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".

The independent panel will hold a sanctions hearing â which could take months to convene â to decide the punishment. City can appeal both the guilty verdicts and the sanction, leaving City and the league in a state of chaos and uncertainty.

The punishment could range from a huge fine, being deducted points or ejected from the Premier League, to being stripped of the eight trophies they had won in the affected period.

Some fans and pundits have questioned how the club's owners can carry on if they deliberately breached rules over the course of nine years.

Asked by the BBC's political editor Chris Mason if he was concerned that Manchester City's owners would now sell the club, Burham said on Wednesday: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

News.title: Bayeux tour to include audio account of tapestry
News.content:
Osman, who has no sight in either eye, contacted the museum via solicitor Leigh Day to ask whether audio-described tours would be available.

The law firm told him the museum had said self-guided visits would be prioritised over tours and events.

The British Museum said this was because there are limits on how many hours of light to which the tapestry can be exposed - and this in turn restricted visitor numbers.

Osman is seeking damages and a declaration that he was discriminated against and an order requiring the museum to change its policies.

He also said relevant staff should be given disability awareness training and he hoped the legal action would "help make sure blind and partially sighted people are properly considered" when major exhibitions are planned.

His solicitor said the Equality Act placed obligations on service providers to anticipate the needs of disabled people and take reasonable steps to avoid substantial disadvantage.

"Our client is asking for the same opportunity as sighted visitors to experience this exhibition."

A British Museum spokesperson said the museum was "committed to making the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition as accessible as possible" and had worked with specialist access consultants.

Provisions currently include a sensory map to help visitors prepare for their visit, as well as dedicated tours during the exhibition run which will include an in-person audio-described tour, the spokesperson said.

"We are also exploring including a separate audio-described tour as part of the exhibition's app-based audio guide."

The 70m (230ft) embroidery, which depicts the events leading up to the Norman Conquest of 1066, is on loan from France and is on display at the museum until 11 July 2027.
