News.title: Met hands Grenfell fire investigation file to CPS
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has submitted its final investigation file into the Grenfell Tower fire to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), seeking charges against 54 individuals and 20 companies.

These include corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, health and safety offences, fraud and fraud-related offences and misconduct in public office.

Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) and the Department of Housing have both been referred to the CPS following the fire which killed 72 people at the tower block in North Kensington, west London.

The CPS said charging decisions would be made before the 10th anniversary of the disaster, which is on 14 June 2027.

RBKC said it had been informed by the Met that it had referred the council to the CPS for three offences: corporate manslaughter, section 3 of Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, and acting contrary to the Regulatory Reform (fire safety) Order 2005.

The council said in a statement on Wednesday: "They have told us that the CPS will now independently review the evidence, and they will decide whether to charge the council with those offences."

Elizabeth Campbell, leader of the council, said their "commitment to candour, openness, and accountability has not changed".

News.title: Oasis take legal action to stop sale of unheard tapes
News.content:
A set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between Â£1.2m and Â£1.6m have been pulled from an auction after the band filed an injunction.

Earlier this month, it was announced that Littleton Auctions, in Evesham, were selling a set of recordings which included 63 live shows, as well as soundchecks and more than 100 hours of Noel and Liam Gallagher in the 1990s.

They were collected by Oasis sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with the band from the release of their debut album Definitely, Maybe in 1994, until 2001.

However, the auction house said the sale of the recordings had been suspended after the band intervened.

Managing director Ben Homer said: "Littleton Auctions confirms that the Oasis recordings known as The Desk Tapes have been withdrawn from our October 3 auction in light of legal proceedings.

"We are very disappointed that we cannot offer this significant archive as planned."

News.title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs
News.content:
High street bakery brand Greggs has announced plans to shut four of its factories and cut 740 jobs.

It plans to close manufacturing sites at North Lakes near Penrith, Cumbria, Pettigrews in Kelso, Scotland, Seaham in County Durham and Enfield, Greater London, though distribution operations would continue to run from the latter.

The proposals will also impact manufacturing operations at its Treforest site in Wales, but this will also continue as a distribution centre for the business.

The chain, which has headquarters in Newcastle, said its retail shops would not be affected by the proposed changes and like-for-like sales had grown across its managed stores.

It said the plans would save it about Â£20m across the 2028 and 2029 financial years.

The changes would take place over the next two and a half years, with parts of Greggs' manufacturing processes relocating, the firm said.

The range of products manufactured at its Clydesmill Glasgow and Manchester locations would be reduced and production of tinned bread at Gosforth would be stopped.

Some products would also be sourced from specialist suppliers.

The general secretary of the Bakers, Food and Allied Workers Union (BFAWU) Sarah Woolley said the union was "deeply concerned" about the announcement.

She said: "Our immediate priority is our members, their jobs, their families and the communities that could be affected by these proposals."

She added Greggs was clear in its own announcement the business continued to "perform strongly".

News.title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales
News.content:
A national inquiry into child sexual abuse by grooming gangs has announced that targeted investigations will take place in Birmingham and Wales.

The inquiry said the probes would "examine the sexual abuse and exploitation of children by grooming gangs and the response of organisations responsible for protecting children" in both areas.

Oldham in Greater Manchester, Bradford and Keighley in West Yorkshire and London were announced as the first locations for investigations earlier this year.

It is unclear whether further locations will be selected. Some survivors have expressed frustration that their area has not yet been included and said they were concerned about expanding the inquiry's scope.

Fiona Goddard, who was sexually abused as a child by groups of men in Bradford, said there was clearly evidence from Birmingham and Wales "that needs to be properly heard" and welcomed their inclusion.

But she told the BBC that the scale of the inquiry "must not come at the expense of the depth of investigation". This was especially concerning, Goddard added, given "we are already almost a year into the inquiry with relatively little progress".

Carly, not her real name, was 12 years old when she was first groomed in Huddersfield in 2004. She said she could not understand "how an investigation covering an area as enormous and complex as Wales can be described as a deep dive".

"How are survivors in Huddersfield supposed to have confidence that our experiences will not simply be absorbed into a much bigger national picture and effectively watered down?"

Meanwhile, Welsh grooming gang victim Emily Vaughan, not her real name, welcomed the announcement - saying it marked "a day that has been needed for a very long time".

"It's about institutions that failed children and the questions that have remained unanswered. The expansion of the inquiry means those failures can no longer simply be brushed aside."

News.title: BBC commentator thanks Cardiff City legend for saving him after heart attack scare
News.content:
A football commentator has thanked Nathan Blake for saving him when he had a suspected heart attack after a game.

Rob Phillips had just finished covering Cardiff City's last-gasp defeat to Bolton earlier this month, when he started experiencing severe chest pains.

He intended to drive home to south Wales from the Greater Manchester town, but club legend Blake stepped in and said he wasn't going anywhere, seeing that he had lost all his colour.

Veteran commentator Phillips was still laughing and joking when he was taken to see the Bolton club doctor, who casually told him: "I think you're having a heart attack."

Blake, who played 131 times for City as well as winning 29 Wales caps, credited his actions to his mum's nurse training.

The 54-year-old, who also played for clubs including Sheffield United, Bolton Wanderers, Blackburn Rovers and Wolves, said: "She always used to say to me 'if someone loses colour like that call an ambulance'."

It had been business as usual for Phillips alongside him in the commentary box, as Cardiff lost "having played really well", he told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast.

Thierry Gale had scored a 90th-minute header at the Toughsheet Community Stadium in the Championship match, and after completing the post-match interviews, Phillips said he started "having severe chest pains" as he got back to the press box.

He added: "I said to Nath 'I'll be fine now', but he told me I'd lost all my colour."

Phillips said he was still laughing and joking around when he was taken to see the Bolton club doctor, adding: "He casually said to me 'Rob, I can't be sure, but I think you're having a heart attack'."

Within an hour he was on an operating table with a pipe up his arm, as doctors tried to unblock his artery.

Survivors across the country will be “looking over their shoulder”, the domestic abuse commissioner has warned, as hundreds of prisoners walk free from jail on Thursday in the first wave of the government’s early release scheme.

Some 4,500 prisoners are scheduled to be released in stages over the next year in a bid to manage chronic prison overcrowding and prevent the justice system from collapsing. Around 700 offenders are due to leave English and Welsh jails on Thursday.

Criminals convicted of rape, and the most serious child sex offences will be exempt from release. Prisoners guilty of manslaughter will also be excluded after a public outcry over the potential release of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

However, many domestic abusers remain eligible for release, prompting a warning from the commissioner Dame Nicole Jacobs, who said “survivors across the country will be looking over their shoulder and living in fear because the government and our criminal justice system has failed to protect them”.

She added: “It is frankly shameful that as the scheme begins - which ministers have had months to prepare for - I still have no assurance that the danger perpetrators pose has been properly considered and assessed with meaningful input from victims and the specialist services supporting them.”

Dame Nicole said many survivors were now “being forced to make their own plans to protect themselves, including uprooting their lives, because they simply do not trust that sufficient safeguards are in place to manage their abuser safely in the community”.

open image in gallery Freed prisoner Sheik Yaqub al-Sabah, 49, praised the early release scheme after leaving HMP Wandsworth (pictured) in 2024, before jumping into a £250,000 Lamborghini Urus ( Getty )

Alice Russell-Harris, public affairs lead at the charity Refuge, said the failure to exempt domestic abusers from early release would put survivors at risk. She added: “Although perpetrators may be released with licence conditions, including electronic tagging and restriction zones, we know that licence conditions are frequently breached by perpetrators, and we are concerned that an under-resourced probation service will not respond swiftly enough to keep survivors from further harm.”

She added that some survivors “may have no alternative than to seek emergency refuge accommodation away from their place of residence”, with these services already under immense pressure.

Victims’ commissioner Claire Waxman said “confidence being projected by government is not yet matched by the reality on the ground”.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has insisted that offenders will be released under the “toughest supervision in British history”. New restriction zones will be put in place to control the movements of the highest-risk sexual and violent offenders, confining many to an area just a few miles wide, the government said.

The department also promised that new technology being rolled out later this year will give probation near-live access to tagging data, so that any breaches of conditions are quickly spotted.

Justice secretary Alex Norris said: “We understand the anxiety victims face ahead of offenders release dates, but the greatest danger to victims would be prisons running out of cells for dangerous criminals which was the crisis this government inherited.

open image in gallery Justice secretary Alex Norris has said he has taken action to stop prisons running out of cells ( Getty )

“Our plan will make sure this never happens again by building 14,000 prison places while subjecting offenders to the toughest ever controls – leaving them nowhere to hide and under no doubt that we are watching them."

Pia Sinha, chief executive of the Prison Reform Trust, said the early release scheme “was absolutely necessary to head off the prospect of a capacity crisis once again engulfing our prison system”, adding: “Although the introductions of exemptions may be politically understandable, it has disrupted the careful planning required to successfully implement these changes.” She warned that a new capacity crisis could emerge in the months and years ahead as prisons continue to battle for room.

A report by His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Probation (HMIP) revealed this week that almost half of electronic tags used to track offenders’ movements are not fitted on time.

Some criminals are waiting up to five months to be fitted with a tag, the report said.

Vice president of the Police Superintendents’ Association, Sara Crane, warned that the financial cost of early release would now fall on policing. She added: “Forces will be expected to manage increased demand from offender monitoring, licence breaches, recalls, safeguarding concerns and further offending, while colleague in the Probation Service face huge capacity crises...Every hour spent dealing with the consequences of this scheme is an hour that cannot be spent tackling neighbourhood crime, protecting vulnerable people or supporting victims.”

The total prison population of England and Wales is now 1,022 below the record high of 88,521, which was reached on September 6 2024 in the wake of the public disorder that followed the Southport killings earlier that year. The government launched the early release scheme just four days later, on September 10 2024.

Images of prisoners celebrating their early release caused public anger in the following weeks. Inmate Daniel Dowling-Brooks said “big up Keir Starmer” as he was picked up in a convoy of a white Bentley and black Mercedes G-Wagon outside HMP Swaleside in Kent in October 2024.

Another prisoner at the same jail was welcomed with an embrace as he was picked up in a black Rolls-Royce by a group of men in matching hoodies. A total of 70,066 prisoners had been released under the scheme up to the end of March 2026, according to the latest MoJ data.

Under a separate process introduced by the previous Conservative government, 13,325 prisoners in England and Wales were freed early between 17 October 2023 and 9 September 2024.

Donald Trump’s administration has done much to turn Hispanic Americans against the president many of them supported in 2024 — but Wednesday may have truly taken the cake.

As he hosted an event honoring Hispanic Heritage Month, the president, in real time, seemed to realize that his rambling, 20-minute diatribe about every topic except the one at hand was likely to be a point of coverage for the mainstream press.

He began his remarks Wednesday afternoon with a long set of prepared comments about the final withdrawal of U.S. forces from Iraq, which took place this week, and transitioned to talking about his war with Iran, the strike to capture Nicolas Maduro in Venezuela, and (of course) his planned White House ballroom, with the president excitedly telling his guests they would be the first people to step on its floor.

In a moment of self-reflection, he noted: “The press will say tomorrow, ‘he rambled for 20 minutes about unrelated subjects,’” before defending himself for talking about issues that he said would be good for the entire country, Hispanic Americans included.

It wasn’t just that the actual message of honoring Hispanic Americans got buried under a lengthy opener, however. It was what came next that compounded the image that was already forming: He persisted with an event that largely ignored any mentions of Hispanic culture, heritage or impact on American society — save for the one impact that mattered to him, their votes for him during the 2024 election.

open image in gallery Donald Trump led a surreal ‘Hispanic Heritage Month’ event at the White House on Wednesday ( Reuters )

Trump proudly and repeatedly boasted that he’d won more Hispanic votes than any other Republican president in history as his party now faces the consequences of those voters abandoning the party in scores ahead of the rapidly-approaching midterms.

“I won all of the Hispanic cities,” Trump remembered, telling his audience how Texas Gov. Greg Abbott called him to tell him about his success in areas with high Hispanic populations. “I’m a politician that got the most, for a Republican who got the most but almost for anybody, got the most Hispanic votes of anybody.”

Now, his party is rushing towards a November midterm election where those voters appear ready to abandon the party they broke for in larger numbers than ever in 2024, and Trump is finally blaming himself. Or, at least, he said Wednesday that the real reason Republicans need to “turn this around” (his first public admission that the party is on the verge of a bloodbath in much polling) is because he himself has done a “bad job” at explaining how well the country is doing.

“You gotta spread the word of how well we’re doing. We’ve got to turn this around,” said Trump. “Our numbers are through the roof. We have the best numbers in the history of our country.”

open image in gallery Trump admitted to his audience on Wednesday that Republicans were trailing Democrats in projections for control of the House and Senate ahead of the midterms ( Getty )

With gas prices at heights only reached during the height of Covid-era fuel squeezes and a ripple effect driving up the prices of food and other goods, Americans’ pessimism about the economy is the worst it’s been since Trump took office.

But as much as Trump admits that he himself needs to get back on message, it’s not clear what that winning campaign message from the White House actually will be, even as he repeated his promise Wednesday to hit the campaign trail every day in October for vulnerable Republican candidates. The unfocused, disrespectful address to an audience of close Republican loyalists on Wednesday will likely do little to stem the bleeding the party is suffering among Hispanic and Latino voters in Texas, North Carolina, Ohio and other states where key Senate and House races are playing out this cycle and will determine the fate of Trump’s legislative agenda for the remainder of his presidency.

The event ended with one final surreal moment that summed up the entire event. As the president ushered his fans toward the entrance to the new White House ballroom, which remains under construction, and warned them not to fall. Then he uttered one final gasp-inducing quip.

“Only a Hispanic could survive that fall!” joked Trump. “I’m not worried.”

Maybe that makes sense; as he reminded his audience Wednesday, he’s not on the ballot -- as much as Republican candidates need him to be.

A woman who filed a lawsuit saying she was sexually assaulted by seven men at a Cornell University fraternity house told police weeks after the incident that she could “say with 100% confidence I was raped,” according to a transcript obtained by CBS News New York.

The transcript, which has not been publicly released, raises new questions surrounding the local district attorney's decision not to prosecute anyone at the time.

In recent days, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has maintained the woman's first account to police didn't include allegations that she was drugged, incapacitated beyond the ability to consent, or forced into sex. Yet, he also said he had reopened the investigation based on new information in the woman's lawsuit, which was filed this month.

The woman initially went to Cornell's campus police about three weeks after the alleged attack that began on Oct. 19, 2024, then went back on Nov. 14 and 15, 2024, to be interviewed.

“Yes. It was coercion, yes,” she told a campus police officer, according to the transcript. According to CBS News, she said she was “completely and totally incapacitated” before some of the sexual abuse.

The woman acknowledged she had been drinking alcohol and used drugs the night she visited the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024, and that she had gaps in her memory.

She also told police she was comfortable with an initial sexual encounter with two of the men, but not with what happened later in the night, when other men began to enter the room.

“And then, of course, I was being hit at the same time. Physically hit very, very hard," she told police, according to the transcript. “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," she told investigators.

The woman, identified only by the pseudonym Jane Doe in the lawsuit, filed a complaint Sept. 16 saying she was sexually assaulted at the Chi Phi fraternity house after being pressured into snorting ketamine, smoking marijuana and drinking alcohol. She became completely incapacitated while fraternity members were sexually assaulting her, she said.

The district attorney, Van Houten, didn't immediately respond to emails and phone messages from The Associated Press on Wednesday, but he told CBS News he never saw the transcript of the woman's interview when his office declined to bring charges, and relied instead on a statement written by a campus police officer but signed by the accuser.

Van Houten has released a summary of that statement, with some of her direct quotes included. He has defended his office’s decision not to do additional investigation after the woman first came forward in 2024.

“There were no question marks. There was no additional need to find information because we had all of the information that the police collected from Jane Doe through her very detailed, very comprehensive statement that she provided,” Van Houten told CNN earlier this week.

Cornell University first publicly disclosed that it was investigating the woman's allegations on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day she first went to police. The school sent students an email alert warning them that a person had reported they had been sexually assaulted at a fraternity house and coerced into consuming drugs. Cornell suspended the Chi Phi fraternity the same day.

In another public statement to students in late November 2024, Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said campus police were investigating “deeply disturbing allegations of drug abuse and sexual violence” at the fraternity house.

Later, Cornell appointed a task force designed to address sexual assault on campus. But with the district attorney's decision not to pursue charges and the university's internal disciplinary investigation being shielded from the public, attention on the matter waned.

Cornell said in a statement this week that it supported the decision to reopen the criminal investigation, adding that its own investigation had led to some students being disciplined or expelled. The Chi Phi chapter remains barred from campus, but the university has declined to release more information on discipline for individual students, citing privacy rules.

Pennsylvania health officials reported a fifth measles-associated death Wednesday as the U.S. endures its worst year for the disease since 1991.

The Pennsylvania Department of Health said the person was from Lancaster County and was unvaccinated. The state did not provide any further information about the person who died. Lancaster County’s coroner, Dr. Stephen Diamantoni, said that his office did not handle the death and that state officials have not provided him with any details.

The state's other deaths have included an 18-year-old resident of Mifflin County, in the center of the state; a 40-year-old woman from Jefferson County, a rural area in western Pennsylvania; and two infants in Lancaster County, in the southeastern part of the state.

None of them were vaccinated, according to the state health department. The infants were too young for vaccinations, according to current recommendations.

The U.S. has now seen eight reported measles-associated deaths in the last two years — more than the combined total of reported deaths over the previous three decades.

Pennsylvania’s measles outbreak continues to grow, with 943 illnesses reported so far this year across 39 counties. The measles-associated deaths are the first reported in the state in 35 years, state officials say.

The nation eliminated the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks. Meanwhile, measles infections have been surging in recent years.

In November, international health officials will meet to determine if the U.S. and Mexico have lost their measles-free status.

The problem has been years in the making, as fewer kids get routine vaccines because of parental waivers, healthcare access issues and rampant disinformation. More recently, Trump administration health officials, including Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., have questioned and sown doubt about the established safety of vaccines at an unprecedented level while also defunding local efforts to improve vaccination rates.

The pilot who fought off his co-pilot who stabbed him during an attempted midair attack on a flight to Israel has been named as Captain Smit Machchhar.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised Cpt Machchhar, an Indian national, as a "true hero" for fighting back against the attacker and opening the cockpit door during the commercial flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

"My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery," Netanyahu posted on X. "Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker."

open image in gallery ( Israel media )

The attack unfolded on Wednesday morning, roughly two and a half hours into Flydubai Flight FZ1073.

As the Boeing 737 crossed over Jordanian airspace, Machchhar’s co-pilot — who Israeli intelligence believe is an Omani jihadist — launched a knife attack inside the cockpit and attempted to sabotage the flight controls to crash the airliner. The aircraft plunged an extraordinary 17,000ft in roughly two minutes.

Despite bleeding heavily after sustaining multiple severe stab wounds, Israeli officials said Cpt Machchhar was able to hit the cockpit's door release mechanism before collapsing.

open image in gallery Machchhar’s co-pilot launched a knife attack in an attempt to sabotage the flight controls ( AFP/Getty )

Several passengers then charged forward to breach the unlocked flight deck, joining crew members to physically restrain the attacker on the floor.

"My daughter heard screaming and saw a man with a knife put the pilot on the floor, with blood everywhere," said passenger Yasmin Abu Kasis. "The plane started to lose control, so all the people were screaming."

Meital, a passenger whose husband attempted to help, told Israel’s Channel 12: "There were stabbings and a lot of blood. My husband rushed to the front of the plane, and ... neutralised the terrorist."

Control of the aircraft was restored after an off-duty British pilot traveling on board entered the cockpit and executed an emergency landing at Tabuk Airport in northeastern Saudi Arabia.

Local authorities arrested the suspect on the tarmac immediately after touchdown. Both pilots were then hospitalised in Tabuk, where the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia has since confirmed Machchhar underwent emergency surgery and is in stable condition.

open image in gallery Passengers reunited with their families at Ben Gurion airport later on Wednesday ( Getty )

Netanyahu added that Machchhar "saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," wishing him a full recovery.

Israeli defence minister Israel Katz formally classified the incident as an attempted "jihadist terrorist attack," stating the suspect intended to crash the plane with everyone on board.

In response, Netanyahu has ordered security services to immediately tighten screening protocols across all domestic and international carriers entering Israeli airspace.

The 174 passengers were later flown from Tabuk to Ben Gurion Airport on a replacement aircraft sent by Flydubai, where they were reunited with emotional family members late Wednesday evening.

The Israeli prime minister personally met with several of the returning passengers on the tarmac at Ben Gurion, praising their courage and thanking them for intervening.

Flydubai has confirmed that formal investigations into the attacker's underlying motives remain ongoing.

A Maryland travel company reportedly cut short a luxury France trip for more than 70 women and postponed another trip, travelers say, leaving some still waiting for refunds.

Younique Ventures, a Charles County-based travel company owned by married couple Kendra and Kelvin Brown, is facing complaints from customers who say they were hit with unexpected travel costs, lost portions of planned vacations and struggled to reach the company afterwards.

In July, more than 70 women traveled to Europe for the company's “Goddess Refresh Experience,” a women's retreat that included stops in the South of France.

WUSA9 reports that it spoke with 12 women who attended the trip, several of whom said they were suddenly left to figure out their own travel plans after the experience was cut short by four days.

According to the travelers, Kendra Brown told the group that a flight disruption meant the planned itinerary could not continue.

open image in gallery There were reportedly complaints from more than 70 women who attended Younique Ventures’ July retreat in the South of France ( AFP/Getty )

“The trip is ending here,” Dell Sibury recalled Brown telling the group. “At that point, the room erupted with different emotions.”

With the remaining accommodations and activities canceled or unavailable, travelers said they had to decide what to do next on their own dime. Some found flights home, while others stayed in France and arranged later flights themselves.

Travelers said Brown promised refunds for canceled portions of the trip and reimbursement for unexpected costs within 60 days, but that deadline has passed, and they say they are still waiting for the money.

Younique Ventures said in a statement posted on Facebook that a last-minute aircraft change left too few seats for the group.

“Rather than separate the group and leave people behind, we made the difficult decision to end the group experience early. We know that this was very disappointing to many of our travellers and it was to us as well," the statement read.

The company also said its contract did not require refunds but that it chose to refund the unused portion of the trip and reimburse reasonable travel costs for those who returned home instead of continuing on their own.

"We chose to offer a refund for the unused portion of the trip and reimbursements for reasonable costs of travel home for those travelers who elected not to stay and continue on the trip on an individualized basis," the statement read, adding that the high number of chargebacks has delayed the company’s ability to issue refunds within its intended 60-day timeline.

Meanwhile, another traveler who said they paid nearly $30,000 for an Australia and Fiji trip scheduled to begin October 18 filed a police report last week after never receiving flight or hotel confirmations, she told WUSA9.

The Charles County Sheriff's Office confirmed to The Independent that it received the report with an allegation of possible fraud, and said they are investigating.

The traveler said Younique Ventures stopped responding to her calls and emails as the departure date approached.

“They have cut all communication via email and phone,” she said in a video obtained by WUSA9 showing her confronting Kendra Brown’s mother at the company's registered business address. “They have not provided any flight confirmation, any hotel confirmation.”

“We are working to provide the best options for them to use their travel credit,” the company said. “We will continue to keep affected travelers informed, with our next update by Friday, October 2.”

The Independent has contacted Younique Ventures for comment.

Florence Pugh is doubling down in accusing Instagram of censoring her message about Cornell University’s alleged gang rape scandal.

Appearing Wednesday on The View to promote her new Netflix show East of Eden, the 30-year-old actor called out Instagram for covering her posts with a “content warning” after she shared a statement about the former Cornell student who filed a civil lawsuit accusing seven Chi Phi fraternity members of sexually assaulting her in October 2024.

The View co-host Sara Haines asked Pugh at the Hot Topics table: “Even in modern times, women have to bear the consequences of sexual violence, like the allegations currently playing out with the so-called Cornell 7. The case is still pending, and some of the accused have denied any wrongdoing, but I saw what you wrote about this. This was really important for you. Can you explain why you felt the need to speak up?”

The Oscar-nominated actor responded that she had felt the need to speak out about the case on behalf of “all women,” adding that the fear of rape “lives in our bodies.”

“When stories like this come out and it’s really not picked up in the way that you hope it’s picked up, it makes me feel scared, it makes me feel anxious, it made me feel so much rage,” the Little Women star said. “I’m lucky enough to do what I do and I have a platform and I wanted to talk about it.”

Florence Pugh has accused Instagram of censoring her post about the Cornell University scandal ( The Independent )

Pugh has joined people all over in the world who have shared outrage after a woman identified only as “Jane Doe” alleged in a civil lawsuit that her alleged perpetrators were allowed to remain enrolled at Cornell University after she accused them of sexually assaulting her — and that they only needed to write essays as their punishments.

“I’m able to come here and talk about it in real life, even though, sadly, Instagram censored me when I said it, which is also just another shock that women are censored, even when they go through these things, they can’t talk about it,” Pugh said on the talk show.

The Marvel actor initially posted that she felt “enraged” about the situation, and called on men “to be as horrified and as sickened as us” at the allegations.

She then shared another post that appeared to show a screenshot of her Instagram Grid, which still has an advisory from the platform on it, reading: “This post contains content that some people may find upsetting.”

“Instagram decided to block my post from getting in front of the right people. Tut tut tut. Oh dear,” Pugh wrote in her follow-up response. “That doesn’t look great does it? Here’s another go at it in case you were one of those people that can no longer see my post.”

The actor said on The View: “I feel very lucky and honored that we get to talk about this today. Thank you for bringing it up. It’s an ongoing conversation and it will always be an ongoing conversation until we’re harder on those that do that to women.”

Her comments came a day after co-host Sunny Hostin ignited debate on the show by siding with the New York prosecutors who previously chose not to bring charges in Jane Doe’s case.

Hostin, who said she was “dealing with the facts” as she sympathized with the seven men accused in the lawsuit, was not at the table when Pugh appeared as a guest on the show.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Why the UK medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks
News.content:
The UK’s medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks, experts have warned, with the NHS dependent on a system where much of the world relies on a handful of countries for its drug supplies.

India and China are the backbone of the global medicines market, manufacturing around two-thirds of the world’s active pharmaceutical ingredients. This leaves countries exposed to factory shutdowns, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruption and sudden changes in the price or availability of raw materials, experts told The Telegraph.

“We rely now more than ever on other countries to make sure we can get access to the medicines that the vast majority of people take,” said Dr James Davies, director of research and insights at Community Pharmacy England.

Nearly all the active ingredients in the UK’s most widely used medicines are made overseas, around 80 per cent of them in China and India, leaving the NHS exposed to shocks thousands of miles beyond its control.

The resilience of Britain’s medicine supply has eroded gradually in recent years, as global instability has placed growing strain on the supply chains it depends on.

“We’ve seen more global turbulence in general,” said Dr Davies. “It’s not unique to the UK, but it’s affecting countries across Europe, across the Western world, with the Iran war, with difficulties flying things over Ukraine and Russia, and challenges with shipping in the Red Sea.”

In the UK, shortages have been reported across a wide range of products, including antibiotics, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines, epilepsy treatments, hormone replacement therapy, and some diabetes medicines.

The drugs most at risk are the cheapest and most widely used – statins, blood pressure pills and antibiotics – taken by millions of people and manufactured in China and India at huge scale and minimal cost.

“Some antibiotics are almost exclusively made in China,” said Dr Davies. “For some of the blood pressure medicines, they’re more likely to be made in India. But across the board, those two are where most of the raw ingredients for those active pharmaceutical ingredients come from.”

News.title: Fraudster jailed for 41 years over Pakistani nurse scam in Saudi
News.content:
A fraudster who sent 92 Pakistani nurses to Saudi Arabia on fake documents in an elaborate scam to provide workers for short-staffed Gulf hospitals has been jailed for 41 years.

Ghulam Zulfiqar Ali used forged experience certificates, created fake verification QR codes and phoney employment platform IDs.

Ali was being paid by the Saudi authorities to find staff, but also charged genuine Pakistani nurses who wanted a job overseas, in a racket that has caused major embarrassment to the Pakistan’s authorities.

Gulf nations including Saudi Arabia are experiencing a severe shortage of nurses, compounded by rapid population growth, a rising burden of chronic diseases, and heavy dependence on nurses from abroad.

The World Health Organization (WHO) forecasts a global shortfall of 4.5 million nurses by 2030, and recruiting nurses for developed countries is a lucrative trade.

The 91 women were all genuine nurses, but did not meet the criteria for the “Nurse Highly Qualified” visa category under which they were sent.

When the Saudi authorities realised the fraud they deported all the nurses.

Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari, director of Pakistan’s Federal Investigation Agency, told the Telegraph: “They lost both their money and their employment, and the incident caused serious embarrassment to Pakistan internationally.”

Investigators found that between October 2022 and September 2023, a Pakistani employment firm called M/S Sahou Manpower obtained permissions for the recruitment of 108 nurses for a Saudi-based manpower company, to work in hospitals under the visa category “Nurse Highly Qualified”.

The investigation found the Saudi employer bore all recruitment costs, including visa processing fees and air tickets.

It paid the Pakistani recruiting firm between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,100 (GBP 830) per candidate. However, Ali was also demanding between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,000 (GBP 750) from each nurse.

Investigators found the candidates were genuine nurses, but did not meet experience requirements and were given fake certificates.

Meanwhile Ali had not uploaded their details to Saudi systems designed to verify and check qualifications and give each applicant a QR code. Instead he provided them with faked QR codes and verification platform IDs.

Ali was convicted of cheating, two counts of forgery and emigration offences.

He was given 41 years imprisonment by the special court in Rawalpindi. He was also fined £1,904 and ordered to pay £25,031 compensation – £272 to each of the 92 nurses.

His accomplice, Ghulam Fareed, was given three years’ imprisonment and a £544 penalty.

Nasreen Begum, one of nurses, told the Telegraph: “We are thankful to FIA for compensation. Most of us have genuine qualifications as nurse-midwives, licenced practical nurses, clinical nursing assistants and a lady health visitor but our documents weren’t verified and that landed us in a difficult situation.”

Zeenat Khan, another victim of the fraud, said she had opted to take a job in Saudi Arabia because she was jobless despite having nursing qualifications.

She said: “I have three kids and wanted to give them a good education. Now, I hope to get back my money,” she said.

Swera Ali said she had been working in a private hospital in her native Lahore, Punjab province, but received only £50 a month and performed 16 hours duty.

She said: “My parents took a loan from relatives to facilitate me, but my hope of making money from an overseas job was short-lived when they deported us after less than a month.”

Mr Bukhari added: “The investigation established that their nursing diplomas were genuine. The fake QR codes and fake [employment platform] IDs were created by the accused, and the experience certificates were forged by the visa agent without the knowledge of the nurses.”

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

Sports.title: talkSPORT host picks GOAT Premier League XI but gets off to hardest possible start with Prem’s worst ever team
Sports.content:
Next

LAURA KIRK-FRANCIS was cursing her luck when she was forced to snap up a forgotten name from Derby’s record-breaking flops.

The talkSPORT host took on the supercomputer in the latest episode of The Sun’s brilliant new show Greatest Of All Teams, brought to you by Sun Vegas.



Kirk-Francis picked players from 11 different teams during the Premier League era.

But the Arsenal fan’s bid to select an XI capable of bagging the title was complicated straight away.



The supercomputer determined the first pick had to be from the Derby side that went down in history as the Premier League’s worst ever team after racking up a lowly 11 POINTS in 2007/08.

And Kirk-Francis, who ended up selecting Jay McEveley, could not believe her luck.

Joining StevoTheMadman and Tim Sherwood in the GOAT studio, she said: “It’s not good, is it?

“We’ll maybe go for a left-back here. Let’s go for Jay McEveley. It can’t get worse.”

Sherwood, 57, also revealed then-Derby skipper Robbie Savage, who is now edging towards becoming Peterborough’s new boss, was hard done by.

The one-time title winner said: “I feel sorry for Robbie Savage because whenever this team jumps up, it’s called Robbie Savage’s Derby.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“It’s unfair on Robbie because he is probably the best player within that group.

“There’s a few of them that went on to have decent careers or were having decent careers at the time.”

But Kirk-Francis’ fortunes improved after making former Everton youngster McEveley her first pick.

She selected Emiliano Martinez as her keeper after the supercomputer pinpointed the Aston Villa side which won the Europa League last season.



Vincent Kompany and Virgil van Dijk, from the Manchester City and Liverpool sides of 2012/13 and 2023/24 respectively, became Kirk-Francis’ centre-back partners.

Steve Chettle, who was part of Nottingham Forest’s squad for the 1998/99 campaign, completed the backline.

James Ward-Prowse and Tom Cleverley made the cut after the supercomputer randomly selected the Southampton and Watford sides of 2016/17.

Rob Lee was picked in the middle of the park when Kevin Keegan’s entertaining Newcastle outfit from 1994/95 was pushed forward.

But Kirk-Francis was pleasantly surprised when, after a full season was simulated, her XI bagged 64 points.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp responds to Man City guilty verdict after ex-Liverpool boss once joked he’d hold open-top bus parade
Sports.content:
Next

JURGEN KLOPP is not preparing for any late title parties amid the Manchester City scandal.

The Germany boss, whose side face Serbia on Friday, had previously joked he would join an open-top bus parade to celebrate should Liverpool be awarded any championship honours due to the Cityzens being stripped of any.



The Premier League have found City guilty in 114 of the 115 accusations of financial rule breaches over a nine-year period, which started in 2009.

During Klopp’s time in charge at Anfield, his Liverpool team finished runners-up to Pep Guardiola’s City on three occasions, albeit only one of those came within the period under investigation.



But while others are calling for the honours won during that time to be taken away from City, the ex-Reds chief appears to have no interest in being rewarded retrospectively.

Klopp, who ended Liverpool’s 30-year wait for the title in 2020, said: “I haven’t given it much thought.



“I can wait and see how it plays out quite calmly.

“My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football City played during the time we competed against each other — and the level of opposition they provided at the highest stage — is far too great for me to simply say now that they ought to face some kind of punishment.

“Naturally, I have nothing to do with that matter anyway.

“But when you talk about a legal process that has already dragged on for so long, you can imagine — and I suspect there will be appeals or other complications — that it’s going to take ages yet.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So, I am a long way off from preparing for any outcome, and I don’t really have a strong feeling about it one way or the other.

“It’s not as if I need to have won the Premier League a few more times.

“I am completely at peace with what happened and what we achieved.

“We battled it out on the pitch, and I can’t comment on anything else because I don’t know the exact details of the case.



What are Man City charged with? THE Premier League claim Man City hid £900m in 'sham' deals across a nine-year period. They were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges – which fit into six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

“To be honest, it doesn’t really interest me, either.”

Klopp’s latest comments are a major U-turn to his response in January 2025.

He said: “We had this discussion when I left.

Sports.title: ‘Star in the making’ – Chelsea wonderkid scores late winner for England u18s as fans think he’s going right to the top
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA youngster Ryan Kavuma-McQueen scored a 91st-minute winner as England Under-18s clinched a 2-1 victory against Korea Republic on Wednesday.

The 17-year-old came off the bench on the hour mark, shortly after the Young Lions had taken the lead thanks to a strike from Newcastle ace Sam Alabi.

Ji-Seong Lim then equalised for Korea Republic in the 70th minute, but Kavuma-McQueen won it late with a deflected shot into the top-right corner.



Excited Chelsea fans were quick to comment on the goal, with one person writing: “Absolute star in the making.”



Another said: “What a player!”

A third commented: “Kavuma-McQueen leaving it that late, my heart did not need that. Give me academy lads doing this over another random signing any day.”

While a fourth wrote: “Who else can do it better than him?”

The win saw England U18s progress to the UEFA Friendship Cup semi-finals.

Kavuma-McQueen has been enjoying his first taste of regular first team football this season.

He is currently on loan at Portsmouth in the Championship and has made seven first-team appearances.

During that time, the teenager has scored one goal and provided one assist.



Kavuma-McQueen has made just one senior appearance for Chelsea, in last season’s FA Cup quarter-final against Port Vale.

Sports.title: Man City’s sponsor threatens legal action against Premier League after guilty verdict over financial breaches
Sports.content:
Next

ETIHAD Airways – the chief sponsor of Manchester City – has threatened legal action against the Premier League after the club was found guilty of financial breaches.

In a long statement on Wednesday night, the sponsor said it was going to “seek the relevant legal counsel… to protect its interests”.



It is claimed £900m was hidden in “sham” deals across a nine-year period, after City were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges.

Now the airline has hit out at the Prem saying it “categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.”



It slammed the Premier League for having “created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.”

They said the Premier League had not been in touch nor given the airline “accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions.”



“Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly.”

The airline said the selective release of information and a lack of clarity and transparency had been damaging to Etihad.



“The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.”

Etihad Airways is one of the flag carriers of the UAE with the football club being owned by the country’s vice president and member of the royal family Sheikh Mansour.

The threat comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham weighed in saying he would be “really concerned” to lose Manchester City’s billionaire owners.

He told the BBC: “They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester.

“Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. I can’t intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that.”



Legendary manager Pep Guardiola has also broken his silence saying he was “here” for the club – “more than ever”.

He said: “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

“Let me be clear: we will get through this together.”

The Prem’s statement on the charges said an Independent Commission had found City “guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation”.

Those charges relate to the period between 2009 and 2018, with Guardiola joining the club in 2016.



One punishment for the club could be the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) forcing Sheikh Mansour, the vice-president of the United Arab Emirates, to sell the club.

City have won a total of eight Prem titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups and one Champions League under his ownership.

The Premier League did not comment when approached by The Sun.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo LEAVES Portugal camp amid feud with manager Jorge Jesus as thousands track his private jet
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO sensationally QUIT the Portugal camp after being an unused sub against Norway and then refusing to train amid a major bust-up with the new manager.

The legendary superstar, 41, spent the full 90 minutes watching from the sidelines as his team-mates ran out 2-1 winners in Oslo.



A seething Ronaldo demanded showdown talks with new boss Jorge Jesus on Wednesday.

Now, though, the Al-Nassr forward has walked out on the training camp later today.



Ronaldo, 41, wrote on Instagram to his 679million followers: “After the press conference of the national team coach, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team camp.

“In due time, I will tell the truth to all Portuguese people about the reasons that motivated my departure from the national team, to which I have always devoted myself.

“Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my team-mates good luck, without exception.”

And fans wasted no time trying to track his private jet – and saw it was on the move.

According to FlightRadar24, his Bombardier Global Express aircraft was flying from Madrid to Copenhagen this evening – with nearly 5,000 people keeping tabs.

It took off from the Spanish capital at 7.49pm local time and was due to land in the Danish capital at 10.18pm.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Portugal play Denmark in the Nations League tomorrow night before rounding off the bumper international break at home to Norway on Sunday.

The first Norway game last weekend was the first time in 18 years that Ronaldo was named in Portugal’s matchday squad but did not get on the pitch.

Jesus planned to bring him on for 30 minutes – but opted against the plan.

And when he did replace starting striker Goncalo Ramos on 81 minutes, it was Francisco Trincao who came on.

Record stated an emergency meeting between Ronaldo, Jesus and Portuguese FA chief Pedro Proenca was called for earlier today where they thrashed out their differences.



But it seems the icon was not happy with the outcome and on Wednesday evening was waiting for his plane to take him back to Madrid – after allegedly not taking to the field for training either yesterday or today.

Instead, he was spotted leaving Parken Stadium in a van with two members of backroom staff.

Jesus doubled down on his decision not to play Ronaldo against Norway – but insisted there was no issue between the pair.



The manager, who replaced Roberto Martinez after the World Cup, said: “There was no incident whatsoever.

“Any player – and I was a player myself – when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on, no-one is happy about that.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about.



“If everything goes according to plan [against Denmark], it will be Goncalo who plays.

“If I need [Ronaldo], he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”

The feud comes just a week after Ronaldo committed his future to playing for his country – as he chases down 1,000 career goals – and admitted he will step away when he is no longer wanted by the national team.

Ronaldo revealed: “I had a conversation with our president, with our coach.



“I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I’m not doing anything here.

“I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

“This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.”

Jesus, who won the league title with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season, added: “As long as he’s playing and is in a condition to be selected, I will pick him, within certain limits and under the conditions that I consider best for the national team.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel warns England will NEVER get another Harry Kane and fears it could take 10 years to replace him
Sports.content:
Next

THOMAS TUCHEL expects Harry Kane to smash the 100-goal barrier within the next 13 matches.

The England captain struck for the 87th time in his country’s 2-0 win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League on Tuesday and is the eighth highest scorer in the history of international football.



Only three other players have reached three figures – Portugal’s Cristiano Ronaldo (146), Argentina’s Lionel Messi (125) and Iran’s Ali Daei (108).

Manager Tuchel said: “He is closing in. He scored again. 13 goals left.”



And asked whether he expects Kane to reach 100, the German added: “Thirteen matches. You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all. He is the highest level of goalscorer.

“There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”



Kane, 33, is also set to pick up his 124th cap against Croatia on Saturday so is on course to equal Peter Shilton’s 125 record at home to the Czechs at Wembley next Tuesday.

The Bayern Munich striker broke Wayne Rooney’s England scoring record of 53 goals three years ago but asked about reaching the 100-goal club, he said: “I don’t like to think too far ahead, but of course, it’s getting closer.

“You know, 100 goals for the national team would be something special without a doubt.

“It still feels like yesterday I just broke the record and I was away in Italy getting that one.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The seasons come and they go quickly, so I just enjoy being out there with the boys on the pitch, wearing the Three Lions shirt and that won’t change.

“The striker’s job is to score goals first and foremost, and I know that, and I love doing that.”

It is also remarkable that Kane is the eighth-highest scorer in international football in history. He is now three goals ahead of Hungarian legend Ferenc Puskas and two goals behind Robert Lewandowski.

Kane scored 73 times for Bayern last season and is hoping to win the Ballon d’Or next month.

Asked about his goal on Tuesday, he said: “It’s still the best feeling there is and it was nice to get it just before coming off, I know that, otherwise I’d have been itching to still be out there.



“But from my point of view, some games I’ll touch the ball a lot and be the difference in maybe build-up or passing or switching play.”

England were not at their best in the Nations League game but Kane added: “The final product has to be perfect and I don’t think it was quite there. I still think we can improve in that sense, with the final cross or the final through ball.

“But in the end, a win’s a win. I’ve been around long enough in the team where sometimes you just have to win the game and move on and tonight was one of those.”

Sports.title: Burnham would be ‘really concerned’ to lose Man City billionaire owners after guilty verdict but ‘can’t intervene more’
Sports.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham says he would be “really concerned” to lose Manchester City’s billionaire owners after the club’s financial breaches.

The former Manchester mayor added that he “can’t intervene more” as City face a potential points deduction and subsequent relegation.



It is claimed £900m was hidden in “sham” deals across a nine-year period, after City were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges

The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) could now force Sheikh Mansour, the vice-president of the United Arab Emirates, to sell the club.



City have won a total of eight Prem titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups and one Champions League under his ownership.

But Mr Burnham said he would be “really concerned” to lose the club’s owners, who have invested heavily in the Manchester area.



He told the BBC: “They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester.

“Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. I can’t intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that.



“It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail.

“But obviously it’s ongoing, and because it’s still contested by Manchester City, then I think it’s right that I don’t say much more.”

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Prem’s financial rules over a nine-season period.

The majority of charges related to the club’s failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation.

In a statement alongside the commission’s findings, the Prem alleged City “systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade”.



And culture secretary Lisa Nandy warned City could face the “ultimate sanction” of expulsion, though City have said they will appeal the decision.

The club’s former manager Pep Guardiola – who left over the summer – today broke his silence amid the guilty verdict.

Guardiola guided City to the never-seen-before four league titles in a row and 100 points, as well as the Champions League and Treble.

Guardiola, 55, said: “I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here – more than ever.

“I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.



“Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

The club responded to the shock statement by continuing to insist their innocence.

They said they were “disappointed and surprised” by the commission’s findings and would be “relentless” in fighting the case.

Club CEO Ferran Soriano released a video explaining the club’s position and claiming that the Prem’s case “is based on a single false accusation”.

The Spaniard said: “[The allegation] that the owner’s personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.



“Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the commission that shows it could not happen and it did not happen.

“This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everthing necesary to categorically demonstrate the money did not come from the owner.”

It is not known what punishments City will face, but a hefty points deduction and even expulsion from the league have been suggested.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The investigation start in 2018 after German newspaper Der Spiegel published leaked financial documents from City.

During the period of the charges, the club won three Premier Leagues, the FA Cup twice, the League Cup four times and the Community Shield.

Sports.title: World’s biggest football stadium set to host 135,000 fans taking shape as new photos emerge of 80-METRE tall towers
Sports.content:
Next

THE world’s biggest stadium is continuing to take shape after pictures showed off the incredible arena after nine months of construction.

The VinFast Trong Dong Stadium is being built in Hanoi, Vietnam and is set to host 135,000 spectators.



Workers are operating around the clock in a bid to complete the project by July 2027.

The initial completion date was the summer of 2028.



The stadium, which is named after a traditional Vietnamese bronze drum, will feature the biggest fully retractable roof.

Designs suggest it will have a stunning circular gold dome that will be shaped like a trong dong drum.

And now new images have shown huge 80-metre towers dotted around the site as constructions moves towards the next step.

A series of cranes are visible as the incredible vision of the ground begins to become a reality.

The project is said to be part of a £26million development to create an Olympic Sports City that will host global events.

The development will cover around 22,200 acres on the outskirts of Hanoi, according to Reuters.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The 135,000 capacity will comfortably make it the largest football stadium globally.

That will make it more than twice the size of Arsenal’s Emirates Stadium.



The current biggest ground in the world is the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, which can host around 114,000.

The second largest is the Nou Camp at 99,354 – though it will expand to 105,000 after its ongoing renovations are completed.

The Soccer City Stadium in Johannesburg – which hosted the 2010 World Cup final – comes in third at 94,736.

Rounding off the top five are the New Administrative Capital Stadium in Egypt at 93,940 and Wembley Stadium at 90,000.

The Grand Stade Hassan II in Morocco – which is currently under construction ahead of the 2030 World Cup – will have a 115,000 capacity when it’s ready.

Gill notched his best ODI score and a record-high individual tally in an ODI run-chase. It was his 11th hundred in the format, one of five on the day, as India amassed 406-2 in 43.3 overs to take a winning 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
