Sports.title: Man City sponsor Etihad Airways considering legal action against PL
Sports.content:
Manchester City's principal sponsor, Etihad Airways, has said it is considering taking legal action against the Premier League.

City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol answers your questions after Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches

The club continue to deny the breaches, with chief executive Ferran Soriano calling the process a "Premier League conspiracy theory" in a video message to players and staff.

And now the Abu Dhabi state airline Etihad Airways, which has sponsored City since 2009, says it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".

In a statement, they say the Premier League did not engage with them and they were not given a chance to provide relevant information.

They are now seeking legal advice to protect their interests.

Etihad were not named in Tuesday's published judgment but say it has "created damaging implications" for them.

Sky Sports News has contacted the Premier League for comment.

Meanwhile, several Man City sponsors are standing by the club in the wake of the guilty verdict.

Lucozade, Kellogg's and Revolut have all told Sky Sports News they are not commenting on the independent commission's findings while the process remains ongoing.

Etihad Airways statement in full

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dave Reed takes a look the independent commission's key findings on the 'Disguised Funding Scheme' used by Manchester City. The club continue to deny the breaches

A statement said: "Etihad Airways has reviewed the Premier League commission's published opinion relating to the disciplinary proceedings involving Manchester City, together with the Premier League's public communication of its findings.

"Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.

"The Premier League's public communication of the commission's findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

"At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the commission's opinion. Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.

"Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.

"Etihad is immensely proud of its longstanding relationship with Manchester City. The Etihad name has been proudly carried by the club and its stadium for many years, as part of a partnership that has connected us with millions of supporters around the world. Our commitment to Manchester City, its supporters and our shared partnership remains strong.

"We stand with the club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the commission's conclusions through the processes available to it.

"Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests."

The Etihad statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

'Etihad statement shows how Man City will fight back'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News senior reporter Rob Dorsett outlines the possible punishment that could be handed to Man City

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"In 2011, Etihad Airways signed a 10-year deal which was worth £400 million, which they have since extended.

"They have released a very strongly worded statement, and in it they say they are seeking legal advice to protect their interests.

"Now, why would they be doing that? The reason behind it is that the judgment from the independent commission on Tuesday said that Manchester City's owners had been inflating their sponsorship income, and that some of City's sponsorship deals were 'sham' deals that weren't real contracts.

"They acknowledged that they weren't named in the published decision, but they say it has 'created damaging implications for Etihad Airways'.

"This just proves that Manchester City are not going to take this lying down. They are absolutely convinced that they have done nothing wrong.

"They don't believe that this has been a fair and impartial process, and we've got the situation now where their principal sponsor has come out and threatened the Premier League with legal action and said that what the commission have done and the published decision yesterday has very damaging implications for them.

"Etihad Airways are a big airline and a big business. They're one of the biggest airlines in the world, worth around £4 billion

"I think this is a very big development as it gives you a sense of how City are going to be fighting back."

What did the independent commission find?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher says he's 'not surprised' that Man City have been found guilty

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven.

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

City: Process was not impartial

A Manchester City statement released on Tuesday read: "Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

Sports.title: Ronaldo walks out of Portugal camp and vows to reveal 'the truth'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal's camp in Denmark and vowed to reveal "the truth" behind his departure in due course.

Reports of a rift between Ronaldo and Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus emerged after the six-time Ballon d'Or winner was left as an unused substitute in Sunday's Nations League win over Norway.

Jesus, who was Ronaldo's coach at Al Nassr, insisted "there was no incident whatsoever" in his press conference on Wednesday, claiming the star was set to return to training with his team-mates ahead of Thursday's Nations League game against Denmark in Copenhagen.

However, Ronaldo announced he had walked out on Portugal's camp later on Wednesday in a cryptic post on Instagram.

The 41-year-old wrote: "Following the national team manager's press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I decided to leave the national team's training camp.

"In due course, I will tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

"Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception."

Spanish ​outlet Marca reported earlier on Wednesday that Ronaldo, who is Portugal's record goalscorer and most-capped player of all time, took a private ‌jet to Madrid.

Ronaldo has not participated in Portugal training since Sunday's Norway win, which saw his replacement, Goncalo Ramos, score.

Image: Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo reacts to a missed chance during the UEFA Nations League, League A match at the Jose Alvalade Stadium in Lisbon

The Al Nassr forward started in Portugal's Nations League-opening home win over Wales last Thursday on a frustrating night for Ronaldo.

He missed a slew of chances and had a second-half effort ruled out by a VAR intervention before being taken off in the 67th minute.

His appearance against Wales was cap number 234 for Portugal, but his decision to leave the camp ahead of Thursday's Denmark game raises huge doubts over whether he will add to that tally in the future.

Ronaldo admitted during this camp with Portugal that he considered international retirement after his disappointing World Cup performance drew widespread criticism.

Across a 23-year international career, Ronaldo has scored 146 times in 234 appearances for Portugal. He has made no secret of wanting to reach 1,000 career goals - his current tally is 979 - but may have to achieve that feat in club football.

Analysis: Ronaldo's latest move leaves 'bad taste'

Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"Another day, another big Cristiano Ronaldo story. He is a man who has been making headlines for 23 years with Portugal. This latest story, though, leaves a bit of a bad taste in the mouth.

"Ronaldo was a substitue in Portugal's game against Norway on Sunday night, which they won 2-1, and he was expecting to come on as a substitute.

"But the Portugal manager Jorge Jesus decided not to use him. He said, 'I planned to use him, but the circumstances weren't right for him to be introduced during that game'.

"Ronaldo appears not to have taken this snub very well because he has not trained with his teammates since that game, he had been training in the gym, and he has now confirmed he has left the camp."

Sports.title: What if Man City's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped?
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has called for Manchester City to be stripped of their titles after the club was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules – so what would change?

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, during which the club won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield.

Sanctions will be addressed in a further hearing with the independent commission and Man City, who continue to deny the breaches, have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday, October 2 to do so.

Possible sanctions include points deductions, fines, transfer bans and expulsion from the Premier League - but what if City are stripped of their titles and trophies?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes stripping Manchester City of their titles should be part of their punishment after they were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules

If City are stripped of Premier League titles…

Man City won three Premier League titles between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

They pipped Manchester United on the final day of the season in 2012 through Sergio Aguero's famous winner, then they won the league by two points over Liverpool in 2014 before setting a new record in 2018 by amassing 100 points to deny United again.

So if the titles were awarded simply to the runners-up, Man Utd would be handed two, one each for Sir Alex Ferguson and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, taking the club's Premier League total to 15, and Liverpool one - their second under Jurgen Klopp.

However, stripping City of their titles would not necessarily mean rewriting the league tables and promoting every club below them by one place. Instead, the titles could remain vacant, like when Juventus were stripped of the 2004/05 Serie A title for their involvement in the Calciopoli doping scandal, and it was left unassigned.

What if Man City's record was expunged?

Another option could be to expunge Man City's league record - removing their results - between 2009/10 and 2017/18, which would impact teams' points total and even their finishing positions, although Man Utd and Liverpool would still replace them as title winners.

Blackpool, in the 2010/11 season, are the only club across the nine seasons that would technically have avoided relegation if Man City's results were removed, at Wolves' expense.

What about European qualification?

In four of the nine seasons that Man City have been found guilty of financial breaches, Everton missed out on European football because City finished above them in the Premier League.

In a fifth season, 2013/14, Everton finished fifth and qualified for the Europa League, when the top four - including champions City - qualified for the Champions League.

Tottenham, meanwhile, didn't qualify for the Champions League in four seasons during the period because City finished above them in the table. In each of those seasons, they played in the Europa League instead.

Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea missed out on Champions League football because City finished above them during the seasons in focus.

Liverpool, Man Utd, Swansea and Southampton were denied European qualification because City finished above them.

Tony Pulis was managing Stoke City when Man City beat them in the 2011 FA Cup final, winning their first major trophy in 35 years, and said he feels "cheated".

City also won three League Cups, beating Sunderland in 2014, Liverpool in 2016 and Arsenal in 2018 as well as Chelsea in the 2012 Community Shield.

Sunderland haven't won a trophy since the 1973 FA Cup, while Klopp was denied his first piece of silverware when City won on penalties at Wembley and Arsene Wenger was prevented from bowing out in style in his final season at Arsenal.

Sports.title: Burgess and Powell know weight of expectation for Warrington and Wakefield in Grand Final
Sports.content:
Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell have the same task in the Grand Final and that is to win the trophy for the first time for their clubs; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm

Super League Grand Final: Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell know weight of expectation as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity make history

It's Grand Final time with Warrington Wolves set to face Wakefield Trinity in the chase to become the sixth team to be Super League champions

Hull KR made history in 2025 when they became the fifth team ever to win Super League, but 2026 is entirely different.

Hull KR beat Wigan Warriors, who are one of the big clubs that have won the Grand Final over and over.

For Warrington and Wakefield, the task is very different - neither have won this trophy and history is guaranteed.

Of course, that adds an extra layer of pressure as Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell look to do something that their respective town and city have dreamt of since their introduction to Super League.

With Warrington, he would end a 71-year drought and he admits it is a major motivator.

Powell: It could be a phenomenal story

Not only that, they did it in some style with a 33-6 victory over Wigan in the semi-final. Wigan were the clear favourites having already picked up a domestic double in 2026.

Now, it is for Powell to make even more history with the biggest win in Wakefield's existence but he is more focused on playing good rugby and from that, the result will follow.

He does concede, though, that it would be the cherry on top of what has been a remarkable narrative.

"These boys are impeccable human beings, I think. We're in a great place, we're tuned in," Powell said.

"That never helps you, all it can do is create anxiety and I don't see any point in that. Clearly it would be unbelievable if we win the game.

"We're on a great journey, the club's on a great journey, and this is the next step, this is a step for us into a great arena with an opportunity to do something unbelievably special.

"It'll be a phenomenal story, and I think we're good enough to do it. It's all about Saturday and the boys just doing what they do best and making sure that we play the game we want to play.

"If we get that right, the result will take care of itself."

Sports.title: Why F1's return to 'intense' Sepang offers 'chaotic' race potential
Sports.content:
Ask a Formula 1 driver or fan anytime over the last nine years what track they would most like to see return to the sport's calendar, and there was a good chance that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit would get mentioned.

So those who have been hoping that Sepang would one day return get their wish this weekend as, for the first time since 2017, Formula 1 cars will race on the fast, flowing 3.44-mile track on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur.

We take a look at how that has unexpectedly come about and what to expect from the race weekend...

Why is Malaysia hosting the Bahrain Grand Prix?

The first thing to explain is how Malaysia has ended up as the host of Bahrain's Grand Prix.

The Bahrain Grand Prix at the Gulf country's own Sakhir track had been scheduled to take place on April 12 but the war in the Middle East saw both their race and Saudi Arabia's, which was scheduled for the week after, called off.

But a subsequent agreement in July between the Bahrain and Malaysian governments, plus F1 and the FIA, paved the way for the Bahrain GP to still take place, albeit over 3,000 miles from its usual location, at Sepang.

It has been slotted into what was a free weekend in the schedule between last week's race in Azerbaijan and next week's in Singapore, which neighbours Malaysia.

With Bahrain covering most of the cost, the event runs under the official title of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season.

"It makes sense because the relationship between Bahrain and Malaysia has been strong. Malaysia's fantastic, Sepang's fantastic," said Sheikh Salman bin Isa Al Khalifa, chief executive of the Bahrain International Circuit to Sky Sports F1.

"For us and F1 it's important that we are on the calendar. We went from 24 races to 22 then there were concern about other races so it's important for everyone, not just for F1 but the sponsors and the teams."

What is the Sepang International Circuit like?

The track - located in the town of Sepang to the south of Kuala Lumpur and close to the capital's international airport - proved a gamechanger for modern Formula 1 venues when it staged the inaugural Malaysian Grand Prix in October 1999.

It was the first F1 layout to be designed in full by Hermann Tilke, who has subsequently gone on to pen most of the sport's many new tracks, and is perhaps still his best in terms of absolute driving challenge.

The 15-turn track features a combination of medium-high speed corners, two long straights and wide braking zones, offering both a stern challenge for car and driver, plus the possibility of overtaking.

Image: Sepang's iconic main grandstand offering views of both the back and main straight

"The track itself has got a really nice flow to it," explains Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick, who raced at Sepang in the F3 Asian Championship.

"I think the track itself is kind of one that I think all the drivers are going to enjoy. It's got a little bit of China in it, a little bit of Budapest I think in a couple of places.

"You've got two decently long straights kind of into each other so the way that they'll manage the energy deployment for the racing I think will be good.

"A lot of the drivers will know it and remember it well from when F1 previously went there. Although the younger ones maybe not, a lot of the drivers will know it and feel familiar quite quickly."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater with the latest update on the 2026 F1 calendar season-ending races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

What 'shock' factor does racing in Malaysia provide?

Then there is the aspect that often made F1's annual visits to Sepang memorable: the weather.

Malaysia's tropical, humid climate means conditions can quickly shift from searing sunshine to torrential rain.

High track temperatures in dry conditions provide an intense workout for drivers, tyres and engines, while in 2009 the race was red-flagged with 25 laps remaining and never restarted after a huge downpour left cars undriveable and saw several aquaplane off the track.

"Physically it will be a bit of a shock. The humidity is pretty intense!" said Chadwick.

"Obviously they've got Singapore in and around the same time, so it's going to kind of hit them all at once, that kind of temperature and physicality of the race.

"I don't think it's going to be an easy race by any means. Like I say, the physicality, the tyres, everything is all going to be a factor."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton had to retire from the race lead after an engine failure as his title hopes were damaged at the 2016 Malaysian Grand Prix.

What are the F1 drivers expecting?

It's fair to say that Formula 1's drivers are excited for the sport's return in Malaysia, irrespective of whether they have driven at Sepang before or not.

Lewis Hamilton has raced there 11 times in F1, claiming a joint-record five poles and winning once in 2014, and the Ferrari driver is looking forward to re-familiarising himself with both the country and track.

"I always loved going to KL," said Hamilton.

"Had lots of great experiences there with my previous team [who are title sponsored by Malaysian oil firm Petronas] and the track is awesome. It is a circuit that does give good racing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In 2014, Mercedes driver Lewis Hamilton claimed his one and only win at the Malaysian Grand Prix.

"When it comes to deciding what tracks to go to in the year, that should be a part of the decision making. We want good races for fans, not ones that that you don't see any overtaking in, so I'm very much looking forward to it.

"It's a super hot circuit, one that's physically massively demanding, so I look forward to that challenge."

Red Bull's Max Verstappen was the last winner in 2017 and agrees it presents a demanding track for driver and car.

"It's a great track," said the Dutchman. "I really enjoy being there.

"It's very tough, I think just from the heat already, but also degradation will be really tough on the tyres."

Image: Malaysia 2017 was Max Verstappen's second win in F1

Ten of the 2026's 22 F1 drivers were on the grid the last time F1 raced at Sepang (with Charles Leclerc driving for Sauber in Friday practice), while Alex Albon and Liam Lawson experienced the circuit in junior series.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris is among those whose Sepang experience is limited to the simulator.

"I'm excited for it," said the McLaren driver.

"I've seen many races when I was younger and I was growing up. I remember doing simulator support for Fernando [Alonso] and Stoffel [Vandoorne] when they raced there.

"I remember going into the factory at midnight and driving until 7am in the morning, so it's not completely new to me, but it'll be a first time going to the circuit itself, which is exciting.

"The only thing that's not exciting is because you have no battery, the two high-speed corners that should be high-speed, you run out of battery and it's flat, so that takes away a little bit of the character that I think you should have on such an incredible track.

"Otherwise, it's a new place, and I'm looking forward to another new challenge for us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastian Vettel and Lance Stroll crashed into one another following the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix!

The same inexperience is true for world championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who was only 11 years old the last time F1 raced there.

"It's always very nice as a driver to discover a new track," said the Mercedes driver, whose title lead over team-mate George Russell, another Sepang rookie, was cut to 66 points last week in Azerbaijan.

"I've done it on the sim and it looks like a pretty cool track - very fast flowing, long corners, not easy, especially to put it all together.

"I think it's going to be very interesting as well with tyre degradation. We might see two or three stops because tyre degradation is going to be big."

So what will the racing be like in Sunday's 56-lap Grand Prix, which starts at 8am live on Sky Sports F1?

"Malaysia will be pretty chaotic in terms of racing because of the straights and corner setup that you have there," predicted Norris.

"In some ways, a similar vibe to Monza."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix lead in several epic team-mate battles.

The track will reward those teams who find the right set-up compromise between cornering performance and straight-line speed. Although, should it rain, all bets would be off.

"Another question mark is going to be the weather," added Antonelli.

"I've seen the forecast and it seems to rain pretty heavily at a certain time, at a specific time of the day, so there's going to be a lot of unknowns."

Sports.title: Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ball
Sports.content:
“Do you know the question that you are asking me? Today, do you honestly think it is my job to make this kind of question happen …” Cut to the long, painful pause. Chuck in a deep, shaming stare, eyes that have suddenly become death rays of betrayal and disgust and Pep Guardiola himself transformed from a man cheerfully toasting his own FA Cup final victory to a grizzled chief detective addressing a room full of convicted perverts.

Guardiola had the wind entirely at his back at this point, sitting in the Wembley press room an hour after Manchester City’s 6-0 defeat of Watford in May 2019. Success drowns out every other noise in football. To be good is also to be good, noble, virtuous. History is written by the domestic treble winners. Right up until the moment it isn’t.

The question in question was asked by Rob Harris of the Associated Press. It was basically this: information is now in the public domain that suggests Roberto Mancini received a second salary from Abu Dhabi when he was City manager. Mancini was one of Guardiola’s immediate predecessors. So had he, Pep, ever received two salaries?

Even as Harris was asking this he was interrupted by City’s press officer, saying: “We’re not going here, we’re really just not going there.” A simple “no” would have done the job. Instead the exchange ended with another beautifully executed mad-dog stare from Guardiola; not angry, just sad and disappointed. But also, let’s be honest, really angry as well.

Fast forward to this week and a clip has been doing the rounds of the same Rob Harris, now of Sky News, and still the same perky, questing figure. Harris is approaching Ferran Soriano this time, Pep’s key man through that era, and asking the same entirely legitimate things, with a very different outcome. “The Premier League maintains you cheated for nearly a decade … is all this success, as the Premier League says, based on sham contracts?”

There is no glare in return now, no outrage, no flushed moral high ground. “Thank you, thank you,” Soriano mutters, with the look of a man caught shoplifting a Twix at the local primary school fete, followed by a mute, fumbling exit.

Sunlight. Scrutiny. Awkward questions from awkward people. It turns out these are still the best disinfectant. Just as it turns out “the question” was the only one worth asking in that room in 2019. Not that anyone agreed at the time. Predictably enough the comments on social media were about scum, bias, the press as a national embarrassment. Even other journalists held a perfumed kerchief to their noses, suggesting this was all a non-issue because, er, the club had just won a treble.

It turns out the exact opposite was true. It was entirely the right moment to ask this question. That Cup final win came at the end of the main period of shammery. It was in many ways its unholy coronation. There was an industrial-scale embarrassment in that room. But it wasn’t the person asking the questions.

View image in fullscreen The sports correspondent Rob Harris confronts Manchester City’s chief executive, Ferran Soriano, in Copenhagen. Photograph: Sky News

There is an obvious problem with the City story at this stage. It’s just too big. There is too much to say, an entire Dickensian multiverse interlayered with oddities and moments of jaw-drop. This is not, repeat not, a media story. And yet it kind of is a media story. After all, it was media scrutiny and the efforts of the hacker Rui Pinto that first winkled it out. As such, Harris deserves his moment of grace, living proof that it’s culturally vital to keep on asking questions, the same Rob Harris I have seen grilling Vladimir Putin about corruption on the hoof in Zurich, and also walking into a pillar at the World Cup in São Paulo while running off with his laptop to ask someone else something else, a man so deeply locked into the news cycle even reinforced stadium infrastructure doesn’t register.

It is also worth mentioning at moments like this Nick Harris, AKA Sporting Intelligence, who has kept going at this story relentlessly despite an unusual degree of abuse, harassment and threats, and who has every right to feel vindicated, part of a world where we can still hold power to account, where a cat can look at a king. But for now the real object of interest in this exchange is, of course, the person on the other end of it. Welcome to the stage once again Pep Guardiola, the public face of the club for the past decade.

What did Pep know? This is more than just football legacy chat. It relates to pretty much everything here, the true nature of the club, of elite football itself, and more basic things like truth, spectacle and human nature. Is believing the assurances of others any kind of defence, given Guardiola was in the perfect position to ask questions of his own? Is any kind of deniability plausible here?

The other significant statement from Guardiola in that time came after City’s two-year ban from the Champions League for a serious breach of Uefa’s financial fair play rules was overturned by the court of arbitration for sport. “We didn’t break the rules. We played the same rules as all the clubs in the Premier League,” was Guardiola’s conclusion, which seemed pretty silly at the time, given time-barring of offences was key to that decision. How does it look now?

To this day Guardiola’s stance remains slavish adherence to the promises of his paymasters, as evidenced by his first statement on the matter on Wednesday. Guardiola says he will be getting through the current unpleasantness with the club and its fans, sticking together as always. But were you together, really? Because City’s fans have some urgent questions of their own now. The majority believed what they were told, and put their faith in the “irrefutable body of evidence” schtick. That ring binder of truth really is going to have to do a lot of instant high-speed kung fu when it finally comes screeching into the appeal room on its trail bike. Not to mention explaining where it’s been over the past three years of information exchange.

Guardiola will face his own questions too, and on a level that will hurt him. The coach who only stays for three or four years stretched this out to a full decade at a club where 80% of that time was spent under a cloud of sham contracts and casual hubris. Through all this he had a deeply personal relationship with his chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak. The pair of them are seen whispering tenderly in the recent Prime documentary, in which Guardiola is presented as the most genuine and heartfelt of truth-seekers, a lone castaway on Integrity Island, Jedi-like in a tailored hoodie, eyes brimming with tears as he talks feelings and eternal truths, like a dad in the pub on Christmas Eve.

View image in fullscreen Kevin De Bruyne joined Manchester City from Wolfsburg for £51m in 2015. Photograph: Ash Allen/EPA

In his farewell hagiographies, Guardiola was routinely described as the greatest modern manager. He invented the Messi role for Messi. He reimagined the basic texture of the sport in this country. If this guy isn’t good, nobody’s good. On the other hand, the only logical conclusion on the facts as they stand is that all his City trophies were won with the benefit of concerted macro-cheating.

During the period embraced by the charges, City’s net spend on transfers was, according to Transfermarkt, almost £400m more than Manchester United in second place, and five times as much as Liverpool and Arsenal. From 2016 to 2018, the key period in building the Pep supremacy, they massively outspent every other team. After which they won the league on the final day or by a single point three times. There were little things throughout, like digging out an extra £25m for Kevin De Bruyne, stretching those fine details in your direction. How is it possible not to see that success as unrelated to stolen margins? This is an era that will now be defined by sham-ball, trophies hoisted with a hand behind your back and a thumb on the scale.

Pep can only double down now and ride this to the end. His life’s work, his vast and all-consuming reputation is at stake. “We will get through this together,” he says in Wednesday’s statement. Well, you have no choice now, Pep. Wherever that destination might be.

There are others who must now enter the matrix of who knew what. Soriano, subject of the second Harris grilling, is utterly bound up in this. He’s there right at the start, speaking to us in the leaked emails published by Der Spiegel. “We will need to fight this,” Soriano writes in one leaked memo, “and do it in a way that is not visible.” Hmm. How’s that part working out?

Soriano’s own pre-City past has already been sliced and diced by those who wish to see a pattern. For the record, and as a basic statement of fact, he was at Barcelona during the period when the alleged, unproved, time-barred refereeing scandal happened, but not implicated or punished. He was at Air Spain when it collapsed, but cleared of any wrongdoing. And now he’s been at City in the period of inflated income that has, in effect, left the club dangling over the edge of a cliff. It is certainly an unfortunate chain of coincidence.

Others who will be asked what they knew, or not asked because he’s not going to speak to you, include the owner, Sheikh Mansour. This has an added element. It speaks to the ultimate test, some way down the line, of fitness to run a football club. How is it possible to spend so much family money on this thing, to dole out what are in effect government contracts, and not know the actual process here?

But let’s face it, we all knew really. Weren’t the sham dealings obvious? It was there even in the absence of furious statements of support from the independent directors at First Abu Dhabi Bank, Etihad Airways, Experience Abu Dhabi, Emirates Palace Hotel in Abu Dhabi, Aldar Properties of Abu Dhabi, Masdar Energy of Abu Dhabi, e& telecoms of Abu Dhabi. Come on, chaps. Stand up for the investment. No word either from Dude Wipes, the club’s official male-oriented toilet-paper partner. Although who knows, we may now be entering full Dude Wipes territory.

We knew about the sportswashing aspect, knew that City was a soft-power vehicle for the state of Abu Dhabi, which has a record of alleged – and of course denied – human rights abuses and so on. And of course City’s fans must have known this too, or felt it on some level. It was there cooked into the blueprint, the sense of something brutally high-end but strangely cold.

JG Ballard coined the phrase “the death of affect” to describe the institutionalising of public feeling, rage and triumph commodified as a spectator event. Some champion teams have a strut. City’s basic vibe was always closer to an unceasing V-sign. Perhaps there was even a buried unease here. No one really enjoys being treated as a glove puppet, even when it is done gently and with a hand held discreetly under the desk. On which note, Pep? Any other questions now? Is this a good time?

Sports.title: Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enough
Sports.content:
The Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight after the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges of financial rule-breaking.

Executives at a number of Premier League clubs have told the Guardian that a points deduction that would relegate City to the Championship for a single season would be insufficient given the scale of what an independent commission described as the club’s “disguised funding scheme” and “sham commercial deals”, which enabled them to artificially inflate their income by £900m between 2009 and 2018.

While the clubs have no involvement in the sanctioning process, the extent of their ill-feeling towards City illustrates the difficulties facing the Premier League as it seeks to conclude a case it began investigating almost eight years ago.

The same independent commission that found City guilty of the vast majority of 115 rule breaches will determine their fate at a sanctions hearing pending the outcome of the club’s appeal, which will be heard by a newly convened independent panel.

Under new Premier League rules introduced this season, the appeal hearing must be concluded within 12 weeks of the deadline on Friday for it to be submitted, with the panel given a further 30 days to deliver its judgment, meaning a decision should be reached by the end of January next year.

While not confirmed, the sanctions hearing could take place concurrently during the same time period, although it will not be published pending the outcome of the appeal. City could also subsequently appeal against the sanctions imposed by the commission.

It is also possible that the club could delay the process further by arguing that the Premier League’s new expedited timescales should not apply given they were only introduced this season, whereas the charges against them are historic.

The club has already succeeded in delaying the publication of the commission’s “core decision”, which was finally released on Tuesday following an appeal procedure.

As prosecutor, the Premier League is permitted to petition for its preferred punishment at the sanctions hearing, with City also pleading their case, before a decision is taken by the commission.

The Premier League’s position on sanctioning will be taken independently of the clubs by the board of directors comprising the chair, Alison Brittain, the chief executive, Richard Masters, and three independent non-executive directors: Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder KC.

View image in fullscreen Sheikh Mansour (centre) and Khaldoon al-Mubarak (right) have been Manchester City’s owner and chair respectively for the whole period covered by the rule breaches. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The commission has a wide range of sanctions at its disposal including points deductions, transfer embargos and expulsion from the Premier League. Given the scale of City’s offences, according to the independent panel, there are no comparable precedents. City say they are “innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case”.

In the first successful profitability and sustainability rules prosecution, of Everton three years ago for a £19.5m overspend, the Premier League pushed for the club to be docked 12 points in the sanctioning hearing, with the independent commission ultimately docking them 10 points, which was reduced to six on appeal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Many of the clubs are calling for a far more severe punishment for City given the commission’s conclusion that without the hugely inflated income they would have breached Premier League and Uefa spending limits in multiple seasons, and will also lobby to ensure that the whole process is concluded before the end of the season.

“Relegation to the Championship for one season would be insufficient,” a club source told the Guardian. “The commission has to arrive at a punishment that is proportionate for years of sustained and deliberate cheating, as well as providing a strong deterrent to it happening again.”

The Premier League is in a difficult position, as it is also eager to prevent further mass litigation against City by rivals seeking financial recompense. Burnley were awarded £35m at an arbitration hearing earlier this year after suing Everton on the back of their PSR breach, which they claimed led to their relegation at the end of the 2021-22 season, a decision that has set a precedent for clubs claiming compensation following regulatory offences.

Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Liverpool all reserved their rights to sue City in the event of a guilty verdict two years ago, and have already held informal conversations about whether to pursue a claim now the judgment has been published. While those clubs will all arrive at individual decisions, the extent of City’s punishment could prove critical to their thinking.

Many of the top-flight clubs remain unhappy with the Premier League’s decision to reach an agreed sanction this year with Chelsea of a £10m fine after they self-reported the previous owners making unlawful payments to players and agents during the Roman Abramovich era.

Sports.title: ‘I am here more than ever’: Guardiola backs Manchester City owners over guilty verdicts
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has thrown his support behind Manchester City after the club were found guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, telling fans: “We will get through this together.”

Guardiola left City in the summer after a trophy-laden decade in charge, with his first two seasons falling within the period investigated by the independent commission. The Spaniard remains a close ally of the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, who brought him to England, the pair having previously worked together at Barcelona. City maintain their innocence and are set to appeal against the decision before Friday’s deadline.

“I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,” Guardiola posted on social media. “I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Twenty trophies were won in the 10 years Guardiola managed City and he was frequently asked about the charges that hung over the club for much of his tenure. The 55-year-old has consistently reiterated his faith in what he was told by the club’s Abu Dhabi ownership while the investigation was ongoing, with charges first brought against the club in February 2023. “I trust them,” Guardiola said in May. “I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did.”

Upon Guardiola’s departure, it was confirmed that he would continue as a global ambassador for City Football Group, which involves him giving “technical advice to the clubs in the group, working on specific projects and collaborations”.

Meanwhile the former City chair David Bernstein has described the situation at the club as “beyond awful” and called for the board to stand down. “I can’t think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible,” said Bernstein, who was chair between 1998 and 2003.

“I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors ‌of the club, including the chief executive, who’s been there for years and went ‌through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.

“If this was a public company of some sort, the directors would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this, appeal or no appeal. I don’t ‌think the present management can credibly continue.”

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City Women’s head coach, insisted that it had been a case of “business as usual” for his team as they prepare to host Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League on Thursday. Asked if he echoed Guardiola’s position and if he would back the club in spite of the Premier League’s guilty verdict, Jeglertz said: “Definitely. I’m working [at] this club now, and that’s definitely what I’m hired for, for sure.”

The Swede declined to comment further when asked if he had been given any assurances that the women’s team would not be affected by the matter.

Jeglertz insisted his side, who won the Women’s Super League title last season, were focused only on football, saying: “We haven’t changed anything, we just keep on doing everything we normally do.”

Sports.title: Leah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continue
Sports.content:
Renée Slegers did not attend the post‑match press conference, the manager understood to have been too furious after Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead in their draw with Paris FC on Wednesday night.

The assistant coach Aaron D’Antino stepped in to speak to the media instead of Slegers, after a disastrous mix-up between the goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez and the centre-back Leah Williamson gifted Paris FC a penalty that Maeline Mendy converted to deny Arsenal all three points in the Champions League.

“The most frustrating part is how much we are working behind the scenes to try and turn this around, and it is just not going our way at the moment,” D’Antino said.

Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway had given the Gunners a two-goal lead but Clara Mateo pulled one back before Williamson handled the ball after the referee deemed play to have restarted from a goal-kick when Rodríguez passed it to her.

D’Antino said: “If we’re looking at what we can control, it’s just passing the ball to Leah. From what I remember seeing, the ball was still rolling and she was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do. So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don’t put ourselves in that situation. But as far as we’re concerned, that’s not a penalty … we haven’t taken a goal-kick, there’s no advantage gained by Leah stopping the ball.”

It has been a tough start to the season for Arsenal, who are up against it in the title race with only five points from their opening four games, and the closing stages of the match in Paris delivered another gut punch.

Paris FC had promised another tricky test, with teams that are happy to concede possession frustrating an Arsenal side that just cannot seem to find their way through low blocks. Chelsea had read that script on Sunday: they were organised at the back and punished Arsenal’s profligacy and failure to make their early dominance count.

At the Stade Jean-Bouin, which sits in the shadow of Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, the story was familiar. As a result, it was less a wave of relief that swept through the pocket of travelling Arsenal fans and the players when their first goal went in and more a tsunami. It had looked as if Arsenal’s hesitancy had cost them a possible opening again when Stanway prodded the ball towards Russo but the England forward took several touches to create the space to shoot before firing her low effort in.

With the home team forced to come out more, that it took only five minutes after the restart for Arsenal to double their lead was no surprise. It was a stylish finish from Stanway that gave Arsenal breathing space, the midfielder pushed Emily Fox’s cross forward a little with her chest before lashing a volley in from close range.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway celebrates scoring Arsenal’s second goal with teammates before their evening took a turn for the worse. Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/Reuters

However, only 22 minutes of comfort followed, before the team that inflicted a shock win on penalties to knock Arsenal out of qualifying in 2023 pulled the goal back that would test the Gunners’ resolve.

It was a mix-up between the centre-backs Lotte Wubben-Moy and Williamson that delivered the goal. The pair both moved to close down Evelyne Viens and the Canadian forward slipped the ball wide to Clara Mateo who raced free, rounded Rodríguez and slotted into the empty net.

It was tense as the clock ticked down. Paris posed a threat throughout, but the leveller followed the most calamitous of mistakes by Arsenal. Rodríguez collected the ball for a goal-kick, rolled it on to the pitch and then passed it to Williamson who bent and stopped the ball with her hand. The referee’s whistle went and she pointed to the spot, with Rodríguez deemed to have taken the goal-kick while Williamson clearly assumed she was being given the ball to take it. VAR did not intervene and Mendy converted from the spot, driving powerfully into the bottom corner.

It was a bruising end to another bruising game for Arsenal, who really need some luck to go their way to lift the increasing pressure. Meanwhile, Slegers’s decision to avoid talking after the game will have only ramped that pressure up further ahead of a must-win game against league leaders Manchester City on Sunday.

Sports.title: ‘I like him as a No 9’: Bellingham a striking alternative for England, says Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England. Kane continued his remarkable scoring record in the 2-0 win against Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday, moving to 87 goals in 123 international appearances with a late strike in Prague, but he has little cover up front.

There is no prospect yet of Tuchel having to consider life without Kane. The England head coach backed the 33-year-old striker to last another decade at the highest level, tipped him to reach a century of international goals soon, and said England cannot expect to produce a replica of their greatest forward. However, there is concern over whether England have enough depth in attack.

Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been overlooked for this camp. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who came on for Kane during the defeat by Spain on Saturday, is 29 and has four goals in 13 caps. Liam Delap, the 23-year-old Nottingham Forest forward, is yet to earn a senior call-up and it was noted that Bellingham led the line after coming on for Kane in the closing stages against Czechia.

“You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all,” Tuchel said. “We look for different solutions. We finished the game with Jude as a No 9. There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”

Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench in Prague on Tuesday. “I like him as a [No] 9,” Tuchel said. “Then he can contribute to both sides and overloads the sides and doesn’t affect so much of the balance. We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central [No] 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides.

“We are working on that. Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and be able to end up in the box. He is a natural goalscorer and has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to have the decisive action so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a [No] 9 or a [No] 10.”

England moved second in Nations League Group A3 after seeing off Czechia, who were reduced to 10 men midway through the first half. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring and Kane finished well late on.

“The ball falls down and you see Harry taking the shot and that is exactly the player you want it to drop down to,” Tuchel said. “He does it in every single match. The highest level of finishing.”

Tuchel was the manager who took Kane to Bayern Munich in 2023. Uli Hoeness, Bayern’s honorary president, has since said the former Tottenham striker is the club’s greatest signing. “That is so beautiful as it tells me everyone can see his true value and his personality,” Tuchel said. “It is not easy to change and to come to Bayern Munich when you win, win, win and it is a big club. You are under the spotlight and he won everyone over.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

England’s next assignment is a trip to Rijeka to face Croatia on Saturday. It remains to be seen if Tuchel sticks with Trent Alexander-Arnold after the right-back marked his first international appearance since June 2025 by creating Gordon’s goal.

“Trent’s outstanding,” Kane said. “The delivery, the passing range, the crossing but also today defensively he was outstanding. He’s a fantastic player. Trent just has to keep his head down, keep working hard. He’s been great in camp so far. He’s showing to the boss that he wants to be here.”

Sports.title: Craig Bellamy urges Wales improvement but wary of Norway’s threat
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy has said Wales must improve against Norway on Thursday after appearing unrecognisable in their defeat against Denmark, and highlighted their next opponents’ run to the World Cup quarter-finals as proof of their talent.

Wales host Norway in Cardiff hoping to record their first win since last November and their first since promotion to Nations League A. “This team has been on a surge,” he said of Ståle Solbakken’s side. “They are progressing and they will keep going as well – they ain’t going away, especially with the youngsters they’ve got coming through. We’ve all been waiting [for them to flourish]. But it was coming and it’s come with a bang.”

Bellamy said Norway having two teams in the Champions League – Bodø/Glimt and Viking – would have been a “miracle a number of years ago”. Addressing the Norwegian media at his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, Bellamy said: “I think you’re all sneakily hoping we don’t talk about you as much but the World Cup exposes you. But I’m on to yous. I know what you’re up to and I know your younger age groups are getting even stronger.

“Sander [Berge], [Martin] Ødegaard and [Erling] Haaland, they are really close friends and their three sons are all the same age, born within a few months of each other. They’re already preparing the next generation, so we’re all in trouble.”

Addressing Wales’s 2-0 defeat in Copenhagen on Sunday, Bellamy said: “I didn’t recognise anything about us in the game and that was hard. We didn’t look clear in what we were doing, we were ‘in between’ and that comes from myself. I want us to improve as a team and I want to improve.”

Meanwhile, the Brentford defender Kristoffer Ajer insisted Haaland has displayed the same personality as normal amid the noise surrounding Manchester City after the club were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-year period. “Ever since I met him he’s been a guy that brings a lot of energy and joy to the group and that’s the biggest compliment I always give Erling,” Ajer said.

“When people ask about him, he hasn’t changed one bit since the first time I met him, even though he’s the biggest star on the planet right now. He’s been exactly the same the last few days as well, which is not a surprise for me.”

Solbakken, Norway’s head coach for the past six years, said “everything’s fine” with Haaland, who has scored three goals in his past two matches, and played down the idea that the City verdict has been a distraction. “[He’s been] very good, scoring goals,” Solbakken said.

“He missed one chance against Portugal that he usually doesn’t miss and that’s the only thing I can say negative, because he’s on fire.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellamy said he did not expect Haaland to be bothered by his club’s situation at Cardiff City Stadium. The Wales head coach said: “I don’t think he’ll be distracted, the guy’s a machine. Have you seen his record at international level? He’s brilliant. If you love football, you have to appreciate him … You see certain moments in certain sports. Remember the Jonah Lomu factor [in rugby union]? We’re coming through the Haaland factor at this present moment.”

Ødegaard is a doubt for the game on Thursday after a poor challenge by Bernardo Silva in the 2-1 defeat by Portugal on Sunday. “He will probably test himself a bit today,” Solbakken said of the Arsenal and Norway captain before training in the Welsh capital. “If he had no chance [of playing], he wouldn’t be here.”

Sports.title: ‘A lot of lies’: Ireland manager hits out over coverage of Bazunu exit from Israel game
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland manager, Heimir Hallgrímsson, has claimed “a lot of lies” were told over the goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s decision to withdraw from the Nations League ​game against Israel last weekend, and he does not anticipate any problems with the second match against them going ahead on Sunday.

Ireland are one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s war in Gaza, and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to pull out of both games between the two countries.

The match last Sunday, which Ireland won 3-0, went ahead after a majority of their squad voted to play on the eve of the away fixture in Hungary. Media reports indicated that the squad was fractured after the meeting and vote, and that Bazunu had been insulted by teammates over his decision.

The goalkeeper is available for the home game with Austria on Thursday, but will not take part on Sunday in the rematch with Israel, which the Football Association ‌of Ireland has moved to Serbia behind closed doors.

“Gavin is a great lad, I’ve always had a good relationship with him and it’s probably tougher for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,” Hallgrímsson told a press conference on Wednesday.

“There’s been a lot of lies said around all of this, but we welcomed him back and he’s taking part. Amazing, I think it shows his character, as well, to be with ‌us. So I want to give him praise for that. I want to give the players praise for how welcome they have been with him,” he added. Life goes on. He’s a part of this group and I think that shows how strong the bond is between these players that even a thing like this is not breaking us.”

The Ireland midfielder Finn Azaz has also been the centre of attention given his Israeli heritage, and remained on the bench for the win against Israel. Hallgrímsson was asked if Azaz would be involved in the fixture on Sunday. “We are focusing on this one [against Austria], you can probably ask me that question later on,” the manager said.

“Finn has shown incredible emotional control and awareness. He probably is one of the people I admire the most in how he conducted himself in all of this.”

The ‌game against Austria in Dublin on Thursday is expected to bring further protests over Ireland’s decision to play Israel. Hallgrímsson said: “I am focused on football, I’ll let others think about security. The FAI has said we are playing both games and we will fulfil that. It has been really, really tough, but I surely think that in time we will have seen that we took more right decisions than wrong ones.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo walks out on Portugal after being dropped from starting lineup
Sports.content:
The Portugal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after head coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the iconic striker would not start their next match.

Ronaldo had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference. The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark either.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram. “In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception.”

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his teammates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands. “There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters.

“Any player – and I was a player myself … when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on … no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting lineup, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted. The former Benfica manager also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.

Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday. However, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his teammates on the pitch. Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving Parken alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s press conference. Reports also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen. Just before Ronaldo’s social media post, the Portuguese federation had released a brief statement merely confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had not trained.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start the Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos, who scored the winner against Norway.

“If everything goes according to plan, it will be Gonçalo who plays,” he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”

At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would “probably [be] my last year in football”. He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

Sports.title: Golf star Phil Mickelson checked into addiction treatment facility because of 'family trauma'
Sports.content:
Phil Mickelson entered an addiction treatment center amid ongoing personal issues, according to a report.

The professional golfer, 56, is said to have checked into the undisclosed facility recently to seek 'treatment for family trauma and addiction,' a spokesperson for Mickelson told TMZ.

The six-time major champion, who has previously opened up on his struggles with a gambling addiction, is believed to have already left the center.

The Daily Mail has contacted Mickelson's representatives for comment.

The news comes after Mickelson stepped away from professional golf on the LIV Golf circuit and at this year's major championships.

He missed the start of the LIV Golf season, returned for one tournament in South Africa in March, but then stepped away again, even pulling out of the Masters and the Open Championship.

Phil Mickelson entered an addiction treatment center amid ongoing personal issues

Mickelson is pictured with his wife, Amy, at the 2012 Ryder Cup gala in Illinois

At the time, Mickelson cited an unspecified private family matter involving his wife, Amy, for his absence.

Mickelson has been married to Amy, 54, for almost 30 years after tying the knot back in November 1996. The couple share three children together in Evan, Sophie and Amanda.

The left-handed legend has been candid about his struggles with gambling, previously opening up on his addiction in 2023.

He said at the time that he had 'crossed the line from moderation into addiction which isn't fun at all.'

'The money wasn't ever the issue since our financial security has never been threatened, but I was so distracted I wasn't able to be present with the ones I love and caused a lot of harm,' he said.

He also described how this 'lack of presence' has been 'so hurtful' for his family, saying he's been 'often' told throughout his addiction, 'You're here, but you're not with us.'

'It affected those I care about in ways I wasn't aware or could fully understand,' Mickelson said. 'It's like a hurricane is going on outside and I'm isolated in a shelter oblivious to what was happening.'

'When I came out there was so much damage to clean up that I just wanted to back inside and not deal with it,' he added.

The golf icon has been married to wife Amy for close to 30 years. They share three children

Mickelson and Amy are pictured with their children, Evan, Sophie and Amanda, after his victory at the 2013 Open Championship

Mickelson has also made headlines this year for a series of alleged scandals and bombshell sexual misconduct accusations.

In June, Golf Digest reported that Mickelson had been removed as a member of The Farms Golf Club in Rancho Santa Fe, California, amid allegations of inappropriate physical contact with a female staff member.

According to multiple sources, Mickelson approached the employee in the clubhouse, made non-consensual and inappropriate physical contact with her, and he was confronted by club officials mid-round before being told to vacate the premises.

A representative confirmed he had resigned from the club.

A separate report from Skratch later painted the incidents as part of a deeply entrenched pattern of behavior. Mickelson had previously departed two other high-end clubs - the Madison Club and The Bridges, also in Rancho Santa Fe - with sources at both allegedly saying personal conduct was a primary factor.

Mickelson hit back at the allegations through his attorney, Tom Clare, at the time.

'There is a great deal of misinformation circulating and, while Phil's full attention is devoted to a private family health matter, he has retained defamation counsel and is determined to hold accountable any publication or individual trafficking in speculation or false rumors,' Clare said in a statement.

Mickelson's spokespeople also claimed that he has 'never been expelled from a golf club' and that the decision to leave said clubs was 'his alone.'

The golfer and his wife are seen taking in the action on the Sunday of the 2021 Ryder Cup

Mickelson was accused of showing a photo of himself naked and erect to Ashley Perez (left) in 2015, then-wife of fellow golfer Pat Perez

Just over a week later, however, Mickelson was accused of showing a nude photo to a fellow professional's wife in a bombshell report on his private life published by Skratch - written by legendary golf writer Alan Shipnuck.

In the piece, Mickelson is accused of allegedly showing a naked photograph of himself with an erect penis to the then-wife of fellow Tour professional Pat Perez during a tournament in 2015.

Ashley Perez, who was married to Pat from 2014 to 2023, told the outlet the incident occurred during the Barclays tournament in New Jersey, when Mickelson arranged for the couple to join him at his villa at Liberty National Golf Course.

While Pat had excused himself to use the restroom, leaving Ashley and Mickelson alone on the patio, she claims the six-time major champion produced his phone and showed her a full-body image of himself naked and aroused.

'Phil says to me, 'I'm going to leave my bedroom door open tonight. When Pat falls asleep I want you to come see me',' Ashley told Shipnuck.

According to the outlet, she said she declined his advances and did not immediately tell her husband, saying she had not wanted to create a scene mid-tournament.

When Perez was eventually told, he confronted Mickelson - who the outlet reports ultimately apologized during a corporate outing at the Madison Club in La Quinta, California.

The allegation became central to Perez's now-notorious comments on Claude Harmon's podcast in November 2022, when he said: 'I have a different hate for Phil than most people.

Ashley Perez told Skratch that Mickelson apologized during an awkward 26-minute call

'Phil crossed the line with me that is just uncrossable and unforgivable. He knows that he screwed up. He apologized for the action, but I cannot forgive him for it.'

Ashley Perez says she has a recording of a subsequent 26-minute phone call between Pat and Mickelson. During it, she claims, Mickelson alternated between contrition and saying he could not remember the details of the evening. Shipnuck also reports he has listened to the recording.

When Pat told him he had shown Ashley 'a naked photo', Mickelson is alleged to have responded: 'You mean topless?'

Without fully admitting what had happened, Mickelson is said to have told the couple: 'I can't tell you how disgusted and embarrassed I am in myself.'

A spokesperson for the golfer told the Daily Mail earlier this year: 'Some of the allegations circulating about Mr. Mickelson are false, and others revisit mistakes he has already acknowledged, publicly or privately. Stacking the disputed claims next to the ones he has owned does not make them credible. It instead contributes to a false and misleading narrative.

'No person, no article, and no book can present an accurate, complete, or personal story of the life Mr. Mickelson and his family have lived. His story, struggles, and recovery belong to him and to the people who have shared it closely alongside him.

'Recovery is not a straight line. Throughout their 35-year relationship, his wife, Amy Mickelson, has supported Mr. Mickelson and their family with extraordinary grace, unwavering love, and the belief that people are measured not only by their failures, but by what they do to make them right.

'Mr. Mickelson's priority is to become the husband, father, and man his family deserves. Right now, that means giving his full attention to a private family health matter. He understands that parts of his life are public, but his family's private matters are not.'

Sports.title: Man City's major sponsor Etihad considers legal action against Premier League after claims the airline was at the centre of 'sham' sponsorship deals
Sports.content:
Etihad Airways – the principal sponsor of Manchester City – is considering legal action against the Premier League after it was implicated in its bombshell ruling that the club breached its financial rules.

In an explosive statement, obtained by Daily Mail Sport, that further escalates the war dominating English football, the Abu Dhabi-based airline ruled to be at the centre of a series of ‘sham’ inflated sponsorship deals actually funded by City’s owners, says it ‘categorically rejects’ the findings of the competition’s commission and warns it is now seeking legal advice on next steps.

On Tuesday, the Premier League published the long-awaited, seismic verdict of an independent panel which stated that the club had disguised funding of more than £830million via a series of commercial deals between 2009 and 2018, when it won eight trophies. It found that of the £949.94m City claimed to have brought in, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the rest coming from owners the Abu Dhabi United Group and that in total it cooked the books to the tune of £900m.

While Etihad were not named in the judgement, it is the longstanding sponsor of City’s stadium, kit and training centre in a relationship with the club that stretches back to 2009. In 2011 it penned a £400m, 10-year deal that has since been extended.

City will appeal the devastating findings, in which they were found guilty on all substantive charges, and which could result in points deductions, relegation transfer bans. They have until Friday to do so.

But in another seismic development, state-owned Etihad – worth around $5billion – has now gone into battle.

The Abu Dhabi-based airline ruled to be at the centre of a series of ‘sham’ inflated sponsorship deals actually funded by City’s owners, says it ‘categorically rejects’ the verdict

They say that ‘at no time’ did the Premier League engage with them during the process and point out that they were never given a right of reply or an opportunity to ‘provide relevant information’.

They add that the ruling has ‘created damaging implications for Etihad’ and warn that the Premier League ‘must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented’.

The development came hours after Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Manchester, said he would be ‘really concerned to lose’ City’s owners, who have heavily invested in transforming areas of east Manchester close to the club’s stadium.

Football’s independent regulator, which has the power to kick out owners it deems unfit, said yesterday that the decision ‘raises serious issues’ and restated its powers to ‘assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives’, adding that it would ‘use these powers where appropriate’, while Burnham warned subsequently that it would be wrong to jump to conclusions.

An Etihad spokesperson said: ‘Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements. The Premier League’s public communication of the Commission’s findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

They added: ‘At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the Commission’s opinion. Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.’

In what is clearly a warning to competition bosses, the statement went on: ‘Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.’

The spokesperson reaffirmed the airline’s commitment to City which ‘remains strong’.

‘We stand with the Club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the Commission’s conclusions through the processes available to it,’ it added, before concluding: ‘Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.’

Earlier, Burnham had hailed City’s owners, who arrived in 2008.

‘They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester,’ he added. ‘‘I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn’t just put into the Etihad and the campus around it, but also into the city.’

‘I can’t intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it’s ongoing, and because it’s still contested by Manchester City, then I think it’s right that I don’t say much more.’

Burnham, an avid Everton supporter, campaigned for his club when they fell foul of the Premier League’s spending rules in 2023-24.

‘I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time,’ he said, ‘and with hindsight, I think more people would say that wasn’t fair the way that was handled. So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I’d had before becoming prime minister.’

The Premier League has been contacted for comment.
