World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: Colombia pulls out of international LGBT coalition
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella pulled Colombia out of the international Equal Rights Coalition, which promotes the rights of sexual and gender minorities around the world.

The Foreign Ministry announced its departure from the coalition in a letter addressed to the organization of which Colombia was co-president until February next year.

According to Caribe Afirmativa, a gay rights NGO that was part of the international initiative, warned that the decision was “a serious setback in foreign policy and commitments to LGBTIQ+ rights.”

We also view this action as a snub to the international community, a break from the leadership role Colombia had established, and an unequivocal political signal regarding the place the current government is willing to grant to the rights of LGBTIQ+ people. Caribe Afirmativa

De la Espriella has appointed multiple prominent far-right figures in his government and has vowed to wage a “Culture War” against what it considers “gender ideology.”

On top of this, De la Espriella and multiple of his cabinet members oppose the right of gay couples to adopt children and reportedly sacked the newly appointed planning chief because he and his gay partner had adopted a child.

World.title: Trump and six tech companies sign a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord
World.content:
Trump and six tech companies sign a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 19:10 UTC Full article

The document, titled “White House Accord on Super Intelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities”, was posted by the president after a lunch with industry executives

US President Donald Trump and the heads of six technology companies signed a voluntary accord at the White House on Tuesday under which the companies commit to ensuring the safety of their own artificial intelligence systems. Trump called it “morally binding” and said it was “almost like a constitution”.

The document, titled “White House Accord on Super Intelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities”, was posted by the president on his Truth Social network after a lunch with industry executives. It was signed by Sundar Pichai of Google, Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, Greg Brockman of OpenAI, Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Elon Musk.

According to the text, the companies are responsible for the safety of their own technology, will implement safeguards so models operate as intended, will quickly detect and fix problems and will work with independent auditors to verify their systems do not access other technical systems in unintended ways. The accord sets no consequences for breaches. Trump also announced a board to oversee the area, without naming its members, and the appointment of a government official to lead on the issue in the coming days.

Zuckerberg described it as “a start”; Pichai as “historic and consequential”; and Amodei as a way “to win safely”. Specialists consulted by the BBC were critical. Kimberlee Weatherall, a law professor at the University of Sydney, said the accord lets companies “define what counts as safety” and called it “deeply unimpressive”. Jeannie Paterson of the University of Melbourne warned that self-regulation could mean “only minimal safeguards”.

The accord comes amid calls from parts of the industry and from experts for tighter oversight of the technology. According to the BBC, OpenAI cancelled the release of one of its models on Monday over safety concerns.

The same day, Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to replace “artificial intelligence” with “Super Intelligence” or “SI” in official correspondence, websites and reports, and tasking his science and technology adviser with proposing a legal definition within 60 days. In his address to the UN General Assembly last week, the president said the word “artificial” made the technology “sound fake”.

Trump reiterated his support for the expansion of data centres, whose construction has become a sensitive issue ahead of November's midterm elections: a Marist poll for NPR and PBS found 65% of registered voters oppose having them built in their area.

The accord puts into practice the position Washington set out in New York against calls for common rules. There, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for “a single set of global principles and standards”, while Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei rejected any pre-emptive regulation.

World.title: Pilot stabs another on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight and passengers subdue him
World.content:
Pilot stabs another on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight and passengers subdue him

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 18:10 UTC Full article

The pilot identified as the attacker has been arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to Netanyahu

A pilot on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv stabbed another pilot in the cockpit on Wednesday and, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, “apparently tried to crash the plane”. Passengers and crew members subdued him, and the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia, with all 174 passengers safe, 166 of them Israelis.

Flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 MAX, had taken off from Dubai at 03:05 GMT. Near the Israel–Jordan border it first declared a general emergency and, minutes later, transmitted the unlawful interference code used in hijackings. According to Netanyahu, the aircraft lost about 5,200 metres of altitude in under two minutes before diverting. It landed in Tabuk at 06:58 GMT. The Israeli Air Force sent fighter jets towards the aircraft.

Netanyahu said he had spoken with a passenger who, together with a crew member, broke into the cockpit and overpowered the pilot “while he was attempting to sabotage the aircraft's systems”; another crew member stabilised the plane. Flydubai said the aircraft was secured by on-duty crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed it. The pilot identified as the attacker has been arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to the prime minister. Israel's ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, identified the injured pilot as Emirati.

Imagens de passageiros capturam o pânico a bordo de um voo da Flydubai após o co-piloto esfaquear o piloto, levando a aeronave a uma descida rápida de 17.000 pés. Passageiros correram em direção à cabine de pilotagem enquanto o co-piloto omanense começou a esfaquear o piloto.… — FREE BUBBLE (@FreeBubble40637) September 30, 2026

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz called the incident an “attempted jihadist terror attack”. The airline said the motives “are unknown” and subject to a formal investigation, and urged people to “refrain from premature speculation”. No authority has announced charges.

Several passengers said the plane began to drop and that screams came from the cockpit before three to five men went in to subdue the attacker. All were flown out on a replacement aircraft sent by Flydubai, which landed in Tel Aviv in the afternoon.

The incident comes weeks before Israel's elections. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called it a terror attack; opposition leaders Yair Lapid and Avigdor Liberman accused the government's camp of seeking political advantage. Transport Minister Miri Regev called for Flydubai flights to be suspended. Former Israeli ambassador to the United Arab Emirates Amir Hayek urged instead that the airline be allowed to investigate, and President Isaac Herzog said Israel would keep acting “together with our Emirati partners”.

Flydubai operates ten daily flights in each direction between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route opened after the 2020 Abraham Accords, under which the UAE recognised Israel.

World.title: Foundering of Argos Georgia with the loss of 13 lives, MAIB report points to hatch failure
World.content:
Foundering of Argos Georgia with the loss of 13 lives, MAIB report points to hatch failure

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 07:29 UTC Full article

Image of Argos Georgia. (Courtesy of Argos Froyanes Limited)

Argos Georgia sinking, air photo from MOD

The marine accident investigation report refers to the loss of Argos Georgia, 23 July 2024, which occurred approximately 190 nautical miles east of Port Stanley. The Accident Investigation report 19/2026 includes what happened, subsequent actions taken and recommendations.

Argos Georgia was a longline fishing vessel registered in St Helena. The vessel foundered while on passage from Port Stanley in the Falkland Islands to fishing grounds near the island of South Georgia. Of the 27 people on board, 13 lost their lives.

The investigation found that the line hauling hatch in the starboard side of Argos Georgia opened unexpectedly. This allowed significant quantities of water to enter the vessel, causing it to list to starboard and founder.

Safety issues



• Cause of loss: The manual securing mechanism for the line hauling hatch had likely not been applied and the hatch could not be closed by the crew. This led to the vessel progressively flooding, loss of stability and foundering.

• Technical and operational failures: The hatch’s drive mechanism had an unidentified design weakness, while open weathertight doors, vulnerable electrical systems and inaccessible manual controls allowed flooding to spread.

• On board emergency response: The crew’s response was unstructured, and delays in declaring distress and abandoning ship reduced rescue time. Poor evacuation control, extreme conditions and liferaft damage increased cold water exposure and loss of life.

• Shoreside management deficiencies: The company lacked effective systems for controlling safety-critical risks and for assessing, escalating and responding to flooding, abandonment and distress emergencies in severe weather and remote waters.

Recommendations

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency is recommended to amend Merchant Shipping Notice 1873 (F) – The Code of Practice for the Construction and Safe Operation of Fishing Vessels of 24m Registered Length and Over – to include design requirements for shell door arrangements that, as a minimum, require automatic locking arrangements capable of securing doors in the closed position.

Argos Froyanes Limited is recommended to implement a documented safety management system across its fishing vessels.

The Falkland Islands Government, Directorate of Emergency Services and Islands Security is recommended to enhance the Falkland Islands maritime search and rescue communications capability so that direct and reliable contact can be established with vessels in distress within the Falkland Islands maritime search and rescue area of responsibility.

World.title: Milei opens Argentina Week at the OECD and will meet Macron at the Élysée
World.content:
Milei opens Argentina Week at the OECD and will meet Macron at the Élysée

29th Tuesday, September 2026 - 21:50 UTC Full article

Friday will feature panels on energy and critical minerals, technology, artificial intelligence, international trade and fisheries. Milei will also receive an award from the Paris Economic Forum.

Argentine President Javier Milei will lead Argentina Week in Paris from Wednesday, a gathering aimed at attracting European investment, with its main day on Thursday at the headquarters of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, ending that evening with a private meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace.

The schedule released by the Argentine presidency opens on Wednesday with a welcome reception at the embassy. On Thursday, at the Château de la Muette, Milei will deliver the keynote address under the theme “Forces driving Argentina's growth: milestones and investment opportunities”, following a panel on the country's macroeconomic transformation led by Economy Minister Luis Caputo and Central Bank Governor Santiago Bausili. He will then meet provincial leaders and a group of business executives. The meeting with Macron is scheduled for 6:50 p.m., followed at 8 p.m. by a reception hosted by the French president for the delegation. The two leaders met in Paris, Buenos Aires and Nice between 2024 and 2025.

Friday will feature panels on energy and critical minerals, technology, artificial intelligence, international trade and fisheries. Milei will also receive an award from the Paris Economic Forum.

Twelve governors are travelling — from Neuquén, Mendoza, Corrientes, Chubut, Río Negro, Santa Cruz, Salta, Jujuy, San Juan, Catamarca, Entre Ríos and Chaco — along with Buenos Aires city head of government Jorge Macri. Santa Fe's Maximiliano Pullaro is not attending. The national delegation includes Presidential General Secretary Karina Milei, Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno and ministers Federico Sturzenegger, Mario Lugones and Juan Bautista Mahiques.

Participants include TotalEnergies chief executive Patrick Pouyanné; ENI's Claudio Descalzi; Glencore's Gary Nagle; Santander's Héctor Grisi; Louis Dreyfus Company chair Margarita Louis-Dreyfus; YPF's Horacio Marín; and International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol. Vaca Muerta, liquefied natural gas, lithium and mining are at the centre of Argentina's pitch.

Before the trip, Milei told the weekly Le Point that French investors were welcome “to come and fill their pockets in Argentina” and said his government “sanctifies property rights and the sanctity of contracts”. In a separate interview with the channel LCI, he said “Europe is sinking”.

The trip comes as financial indicators deteriorate: country risk rose above 640 points on Monday, its highest level of the year, in the same week the president questioned official activity and poverty statistics.

World.title: Lula remark on medical exams sparks controversy five days before the vote
World.content:
Lula remark on medical exams sparks controversy five days before the vote

29th Tuesday, September 2026 - 21:37 UTC Full article

“Men don't like to have the prostate test. They don't like the touch. Women learn to receive touch from a young age. Men don't, they're full of hang-ups,” he said

A remark by Brazilian President and re-election candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva about men's reluctance to undergo prostate examinations has sparked a controversy in the final stretch of the campaign, after opposition figures linked it to child sexual abuse. Lula's campaign has taken the matter to the Superior Electoral Court.

Lula spoke on Monday at an event in Belém, capital of Pará state, after the first robotic prostate surgery carried out by the public health system in the country's north. “Men don't like to have the prostate test. They don't like the touch. Women learn to receive touch from a young age. Men don't, they're full of hang-ups. They don't know that when they get prostate cancer, they'll be touched a lot,” he said. In the same speech he recalled that his mother died of cancer.

Liberal Party deputy Nikolas Ferreira responded on X: “A little girl doesn't learn to receive any touch, Lula!” Other figures from the party, whose candidate is Flávio Bolsonaro, joined the criticism, and messages linking the remark to the abuse of minors spread on the platform.

Lula's coalition filed an action on Tuesday with the Superior Electoral Court against Ferreira's posts, accusing him of attributing a sexual connotation to the statement. According to the campaign, the president was speaking about public health and comparing male reluctance over prostate exams with the gynaecological check-ups women undergo from puberty.

The first round of Brazil's election takes place on Sunday, October 4.

World.title: A falsehood about Brazil's patron saint pits Supreme Court justices against each other mid-campaign
World.content:
A falsehood about Brazil's patron saint pits Supreme Court justices against each other mid-campaign

29th Tuesday, September 2026 - 21:00 UTC Full article

Bolsonaro accused members of the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil of helping the Workers' Party spread the falsehood

A false report that presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro backed stripping Our Lady of Aparecida of her title as Brazil's patron saint has produced contradictory rulings from three Supreme Federal Court justices, a clash with the Catholic bishops' conference and a dispute dominating the final week of campaigning before Sunday's vote.

The claim has no basis. It rests on a bill introduced in 2007 by an evangelical deputy, which was shelved the following year. Bolsonaro, a Liberal Party senator and an evangelical, denied supporting any such initiative and released several videos to that effect. “It is the biggest fake news of this campaign,” he said.

The episode was amplified by a post from comedian Antonio Tabet which, without naming the candidate, associated his family with a supposed attack on the patron saint. At Bolsonaro's request, Justice André Mendonça ordered it removed; on Sunday, Justice Flávio Dino suspended that order and restored the content; Justice Luiz Fux again ordered its removal, and the case went to the full court. The Superior Electoral Court had also ordered posts on the subject taken down.

Bolsonaro accused members of the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil of helping the Workers' Party spread the falsehood. The body denied it in a note stating that “a lie is not fought with another lie”. The candidate later said the text confirmed the report was false and thanked the bishops.

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking re-election, said on Monday at a rally in Belém: “As long as I am president of the Republic, no one will dishonour Our Lady of Aparecida,” and called for respect for all religions, including those of African origin. His running mate, Geraldo Alckmin, and other allied candidates released messages aimed at Catholic voters.

The use of religious falsehoods is not new in Brazilian campaigns. Folha de S.Paulo columnist Hélio Schwartsman recalled that in 2018 a claim circulated that Workers' Party candidate Fernando Haddad would distribute material on sexual diversity in schools, and in 2022 that Lula would close churches; in both cases the party went to the electoral courts to have them removed. “Campaigns do not hesitate to embrace the fake news that favours them,” he wrote.

The Quaest poll published on Monday gave Lula 39% and Bolsonaro 34% in the first round, and a 42% tie in a prospective October 25 runoff. The only debate planned with both candidates would take place on Thursday on TV Globo; Bolsonaro confirmed his attendance and Lula had not formally responded.

World.title: Chile's defence minister backs trade between Punta Arenas and the Falklands
World.content:
Chile's defence minister backs trade between Punta Arenas and the Falklands

29th Tuesday, September 2026 - 09:02 UTC Full article

Asked how closer trade ties would fit with regional commitments, Barros said the “potentially most contentious” point is oil and mining exploration

Chile's Defence Minister Fernando Barros Tocornal has backed the development of commercial activity between the Magallanes region and the Falklands, saying his country's support for Argentina's sovereignty claim does not imply restrictions on trade with the archipelago. He made the remarks in an interview with Radio Polar in Punta Arenas during a visit to the region on September 24 and 25.

According to his comments, reported on Sunday by the Argentine daily La Nación, the Magallanes community has “the right to trade” and the minister sees “no impediments to those activities going ahead” within the legal framework.

Barros reiterated Chile's support for Buenos Aires, though with a nuance. “Chile has expressed its support for the Argentine claim, its sovereignty claim over the Malvinas or Falklands, but there is a fact: a friendly country has exercised sovereignty over the islands for 200 years,” he said, referring to the United Kingdom, which has administered the archipelago since 1833, with the 1982 interruption. He added that such support must be expressed in line with international law, “respecting the will and interest of the people involved and by peaceful means”. Argentina's position holds that the will of the archipelago's residents is not decisive in resolving the dispute. La Nación described the remarks as “at the very least confusing”.

The minister's words do not formally alter Chile's diplomatic position. On September 3, Presidents José Antonio Kast and Javier Milei signed a joint declaration in Santiago in which Chile reiterated its support for the sovereign rights Argentina claims over the islands, South Georgia, the South Sandwich Islands and their corresponding maritime areas.

Asked how closer trade ties would fit with regional commitments, Barros said the “potentially most contentious” point is oil and mining exploration, “which will have to be assessed in due course”, and noted that Chile's commitments in Mercosur and Unasur are “political and not legally binding”. In 2011, Mercosur members and associate states, including Chile, agreed measures concerning vessels flying the archipelago's flag.

The remarks come as a project for a sea link between Punta Arenas and Stanley advances. The Falkland Islands Development Corporation, the archipelago's economic development agency, has signed a contract with Easter Island Naviera, a Chilean company operating mainly between Valparaíso and Easter Island. According to Chilean media, the first voyage is planned for November. Some Argentine outlets present the route as an alternative to the supplies that currently reach the islands from Montevideo, some 2,000 kilometres away.

Argentina has 60 administrative proceedings open, with no penalty applied, and three criminal complaints covering ten companies and their directors over hydrocarbon exploration in waters near the archipelago. None of the allegations has been proven. In the 2013 referendum, 99.8% of voters chose, on a 92% turnout, to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Mexican Senate passes bill holding pet owners accountable for abuse or negligence
World.content:
The Mexican Senate approved on Tuesday wide-ranging legislation that recognizes animals as sentient beings and prohibits their mistreatment and cruelty as it holds owners or caregivers accountable for their health, nutrition, living conditions and mental well-being.

Though most notably aimed at the 69% of Mexican households that include pets (totaling some 80 million animals, according to the national statistics agency INEGI), the law would apply to all animals under human care, including those used in sports and entertainment; those on exhibition in zoos, aquariums or educational farms; those used in marketing; and even animals being raised for human consumption

The bill, formally the General Law on Animal Welfare, Care, and Protection, passed the Senate on a 115-1 vote. It amends provisions of the Federal Laws on Animal Health and on Film and Audiovisual Media, as well as the General Laws on Wildlife, Ecological Balance and Environmental Protection and Civil Protection. It is now being debated in the Chamber of Deputies.

Mexico ranks first in Latin America and third worldwide in terms of animal abuse, with more than 10,000 formal complaints of animal abuse registered between 2024 and 2026.

The Mexican Constitution prohibits animal abuse. But in recognizing animals as sentient beings with rights, the new law would go further by establishing obligations for people who have animals in their care, such as providing them food, water, veterinary care and a suitable place to live.

Failing to do so — or taking any action or making any omission that causes pain or suffering, or endangers the life and well-being of animals — will be considered a punishable offense subject to a fine,, administrative arrests of up to 36 hours, confiscation of the animals, closure of establishments, or the revocation of permits or concessions.

Furthermore, the bill establishes that anyone who mistreats or abandons an animal will be responsible for its veterinary care, rehabilitation and shelter costs. In addition, it supports the creation of abuse reporting mechanisms and a national registry of animal welfare violators.

PAN Sen.Gina Gerardina Campuzano González from Mexico’s PAN political party said that the bill seeks to open a new chapter for animal protection, especially in Mexico, where she says seven out of 10 animals suffer abuse, “so we are not talking about an isolated problem.”

With reports from Grupo Animal and Publimetro México

World.title: Flooding and landslides in Xalapa leave 2 dead, dozens of homes damaged
World.content:
The heavy rains that battered Xalapa, Veracruz, between Monday night and the early hours of Tuesday morning resulted in the death of two individuals, as well as severe flooding, landslides and damage across dozens of neighborhoods in the capital city.

In a radio interview cited by news outlet Quadratín Veracruz, Mayor Daniela Griego Ceballos said that the fatalities included a man in the Independencia neighborhood who was killed by a landslide, and a young woman who lost her life after becoming trapped in a flooded building in the area of San Bruno.

At the time of the interview, Griego said there were no other reports of people seriously injured, trapped or in similar situations.

The intense rainfall left damage across Xalapa. Initial reports from municipal authorities recorded 31 instances of rising water and 64 cases of flooding or pooling water at various locations in the city. As damage assessments progressed, the government of Veracruz reported that the emergency had caused damage in 43 neighborhoods and affected at least 60 homes.

Griego explained that one of the highest rainfall totals was recorded in Lomas del Seminario, which saw 135 millimeters of rain.

According to forecasters, more rain is expected in Xalapa throughout the rest of the week. Griego urged residents to avoid exposing themselves to danger, particularly those living in high-altitude areas, on slopes or in high-risk zones.

She warned that conditions remain hazardous because the ground is still waterlogged and water continues to accumulate in some areas, which could lead to further damage.

“The best course of action would be to go to a relative’s home or to a shelter to avoid putting yourselves at risk,” she advised.

Meanwhile, the Economic and Port Development Ministry (Sedecop), in coordination with local governments, announced it would conduct a census of businesses affected by rains, flooding and overflowing waterways in Xalapa and nearby municipalities to quantify the damage and losses suffered by small businesses and merchants.

Head of Sedecop Ernesto Pérez Astorga said that once the assessment is complete, a proposal for financial support for the affected businesses will be presented to Governor Rocío Nahle García.

With reports from Imagen del Golfo and La Silla Rota

World.title: El Jalapeño: Ensenada fisherman says latest catch, a US Navy torpedo, is ‘a keeper’
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

ENSENADA, Baja California — A local fisherman has formally declined three separate diplomatic requests and an increasing financial settlement from the United States Department of Defense to return an inert MK 54 practice torpedo he hauled aboard his vessel last week, insisting that under international maritime traditions, the weapon is legally his.

Tomás Aguilar, 58, netted the 9-foot, 600-pound U.S. Navy training device 20 nautical miles southwest of Ensenada after initially mistaking it for an unusually heavy dorado. Since towing the ordnance back to port, Aguilar has tethered the torpedo to his dock, outfitted it with a blue tarp to protect its painted finish, and repeatedly informed visiting Navy representatives that he intends to keep it.

“They lost it off San Clemente Island two weeks ago, its battery died, and it drifted into Mexican waters,” Aguilar said while polishing the torpedo’s bronze propeller assembly with an old towel. “In the bay, if you leave a lobster pot unattended for two weeks, it belongs to the sea. The same principle applies here.”

The impasse has drawn escalating attention from defense officials in Washington, who initially offered Aguilar a standard finders’ fee of US $500 and a ceremonial U.S. Navy cap. By Monday afternoon, negotiations had involved officials from both the U.S. Department of State and Mexico’s Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (SRE), with the American counteroffer rising to US $45,000, a diesel engine overhaul and lifelong entry privileges to the San Diego Naval Base commissary.

Mexican diplomatic personnel have attempted to mediate the standoff, noting that while federal maritime protocol generally encourages the swift return of foreign military equipment, Aguilar’s legal defense — supported by three retired local harbor captains — remains surprisingly robust under 19th-century salvage precedent.

“We have gently explained to Mr. Aguilar that maintaining personal ownership of foreign naval ordnance creates an unusual precedent for regional bilateral relations,” said a spokesperson for the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs, speaking on condition of anonymity. “However, he has presented a signed receipt from the Ensenada harbor master labeling the object as ‘unclaimed aluminum float,’ which is kind of accurate, I guess.”

Pentagon officials have privately expressed frustration over the delay, emphasizing that while the MK 54 REXTORP contains no active explosive warhead, it remains classified training hardware containing proprietary sonar technology. Aguilar, however, remains unmoved by security concerns, noting that the device’s painted nose cone makes it an ideal centerpiece for his niece’s upcoming quinceañera.

At press time, delegates from the U.S. Naval Attaché were reportedly assembling on the Ensenada pier alongside Mexican Navy representatives, preparing to offer Aguilar a refurbished commercial panga boat and full salvage indemnity in exchange for the weapon.

World.title: ‘The presidents of Mexico can only have one flag,’ Sheinbaum says: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🇲🇽 Sheinbaum backs ban on dual nationals running for president or governor: Responding to the Senate’s approval of a constitutional reform bill, the president said that “the presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one homeland, one people to defend.” She stressed that Mexican citizens can hold multiple nationalities, but said that anyone who wants to be a governor or president “must have only one nationality.”

Responding to the Senate’s approval of a constitutional reform bill, the president said that “the presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one homeland, one people to defend.” She stressed that Mexican citizens can hold multiple nationalities, but said that anyone who wants to be a governor or president “must have only one nationality.” 📰 Sheinbaum downplays NYT report on López Beltrán: Asked about a Sept. 29 New York Times report stating that two U.S. law enforcement agencies are looking into accusations of ties between Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, the son of former President López Obrador, and organized crime and fuel smuggling, Sheinbaum noted that the report said no formal investigations had been launched.

Asked about a Sept. 29 New York Times report stating that two U.S. law enforcement agencies are looking into accusations of ties between Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, the son of former President López Obrador, and organized crime and fuel smuggling, Sheinbaum noted that the report said no formal investigations had been launched. 📁 FGR has files on some of the people sanctioned by the U.S.: Asked about Tuesday’s U.S. Treasury Department sanctions against Sinaloa Cartel “leaders” and “facilitators,” Sheinbaum said that “some of these people” are already subject to Federal Attorney General’s Office investigations. Among those sanctioned are Ismael Zambada Sicairos, son of detained kingpin “El Mayo” Zambada, and Carlos Alberto Torres Torres, the ex-husband of Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila.

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Claudia Sheinbaum responded to a significant national development and a significant international development at her Wednesday morning press conference.

The former was the Senate’s approval on Tuesday of a constitutional reform bill that seeks to bar presidential and gubernatorial aspirants from running for office if they hold dual nationality. The bill must be ratified by at least 17 of Mexico’s 32 state Congresses in order for the constitution to be changed.

The significant international development was the U.S. Treasury Department’s announcement on Tuesday of sanctions against 21 alleged Sinaloa Cartel “leaders” and “facilitators,” including the former husband of the Morena party governor of the northern border state of Baja California.

Also of note at today’s mañanera was Sheinbaum’s response to a New York Times report about Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, son of former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador. López Beltrán, known as “Andy,” formerly served as Morena’s secretary of organization and is now aiming to be elected as a federal deputy in next year’s elections. He has denied allegations of corruption leveled against him.

For her part, Sheinbaum, on Wednesday morning, made it clear — once again — that she is no fan of The New York Times.

Sheinbaum: ‘The presidents of Mexico can only have one flag’

A reporter asked the president about the Senate’s approval of the “dual nationality” constitutional reform bill.

“The presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one homeland, one people to defend,” Sheinbaum said.

She stressed that Mexican citizens can hold dual nationality, triple nationality or even quadruple nationality.

However, “any person who wants to be a governor or wants to be president must have only one nationality,” Sheinbaum said.

Sheinbaum responds to NYT report on Andrés Manuel López Beltrán

A reporter asked Sheinbaum about a New York Times report headlined, “A Former President’s Son Poses a Test for Mexico’s Governing Party.”

The Sept. 29 report states: “Two U.S. law enforcement agencies are looking into accusations of Mr. López Beltrán’s supposed ties to organized crime and fuel smuggling, but they have not launched formal investigations, according to five people with direct knowledge of the agencies’ inquiries who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters.”

López Beltrán revealed in August that his U.S. visa had been revoked. He said at the time that there was “no reason whatsoever” for the “crude and perverse act of villainy” against him.

Asked whether the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) will have to open an investigation into López Beltrán in light of the New York Times report, Sheinbaum first pointed out that the article was written by “the same reporter” who wrote a story on fentanyl production in a kitchen in Culiacán while “there was hot sauce to one side.”

She was referring to Paulina Villegas, one of four journalists listed in the byline of the report on López Beltrán. In late 2024, Sheinbaum described the NYT report on fentanyl production as “not very credible.”

On Wednesday morning, she downplayed the report published by the Times on Tuesday.

“It says: It’s not confirmed, there is no formal investigation, but it seems they told me some agencies are investigating,” Sheinbaum said, purporting to paraphrase the Times report.

“Just imagine! [This is] the New York Times,” she said.

“That’s what the article says. Read it,” Sheinbaum added.

Sheinbaum descalifica el reporte del @nytimes sobre posibles investigaciones a Andy en EU Ataca directamente a la periodista que escribió la nota Sigue el blindaje total al hijo del expresidente López Obrador pic.twitter.com/6acvOKfOGH — Manuel Lopez San Martin (@MLopezSanMartin) September 30, 2026

“It’s not confirmed; there is no formal investigation, but they told me that perhaps, maybe, U.S. agencies are investigating. That’s the New York Times article by the same reporter who said that fentanyl was cooked in a normal kitchen in Culiacán. It’s impossible,” she said.

Sheinbaum said she wasn’t aware of any investigation into López Beltrán by the FGR.

“The Attorney General’s Office would have to inform, but we don’t have knowledge [of an investigation],” she said.

Sheinbaum: ‘Some’ OFAC-sanction individuals are already under investigation in Mexico

A reporter asked the president whether the Baja California state government led by Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila Olmeda should be investigated by the FGR given that the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced sanctions on Tuesday against Ávila’s ex-husband, Carlos Alberto Torres Torres.

In a press release titled “Treasury Sanctions Sinaloa Cartel Leadership and Corruption Networks,” the Treasury Department said that “Sinaloa Cartel-enabled narco-corruption has reached the highest levels of the Baja California state government” and alleged that “[a]t the center of this narco-corruption scheme is the ex-husband of the Governor of Baja California, Carlos Alberto Torres Torres (Carlos Torres) and his brother Luis Alfonso Torres Torres (Luis Torres).”

The Treasury Department said that Carlos Torres, a former federal and state deputy, “uses his political influence to facilitate cartel activities and protect the Sinaloa Cartel from government and law enforcement intervention in Baja California.”

“The U.S. Department of State revoked Carlos Torres’s U.S. visa in May 2025 due to his cartel affiliation and work on behalf of the Sinaloa Cartel,” Treasury said.

Torres denies the allegations leveled against him.

Sheinbaum said that some of the people OFAC sanctioned on Tuesday — among whom are Ismael Zambada Sicairos, son of detained Sinaloa Cartel kingpin Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada García — were already under investigation by the FGR.

“Some of these people whose accounts were frozen yesterday already had investigation files in the Attorney General’s Office, but not all of them,” she said.

Governor Ávila said in January that Torres was the subject of an FGR probe that stemmed from an anonymous complaint implicating her ex-husband in a plot to allow a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel to operate in Baja California.

The governor’s U.S. visa was also revoked last year, but she denied any criminal wrongdoing. However, in a telephone conversation with one man identified as an “external” FBI adviser and another man identified as an FBI “special agent,” Ávila said she was willing to cooperate with U.S. authorities, apparently in order to avoid possible criminal charges in the United States and extradition to that country.

An audio recording of the conversation was published by the newspaper El Universal in July.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Reform barring future presidents, governors from holding dual nationality passes Senate
World.content:
The Mexican Senate has approved a constitutional reform establishing a requirement of exclusive Mexican nationality for those aspiring to the presidency, a state governorship or the head of government of Mexico City.

The bill, championed by President Claudia Sheinbaum, was approved by the Senate with 86 votes in favor — from the ruling party Morena, the PT and the PVEM — and 42 against, cast by members of the PAN, the PRI and Movimiento Ciudadano (MC).

Approved in both general and specific terms by a qualified majority, the bill now needs to be ratified by at least 17 state legislatures, where Morena also holds parliamentary majorities.

If approved, the law would come into force starting in 2028 to avoid affecting those seeking a governorship in next year’s elections. Nor will it affect those already holding such positions at the time the law enters into force.

Morena Senator Óscar Cantón stated that the reform does not eliminate any political rights or cancel any nationality. Rather, it seeks to prevent “temptations, ambitions and betrayals” against the people of Mexico, as occurred in the regimes of Antonio López de Santa Anna (1853-1855) and Porfirio Díaz, who stayed in power for over 30 years (1877-1880 and 1884-191).

PAN Senator Laura Esquivel Torres said that this amendment to the Constitution sends the message that “migrants are less Mexican and do not have the same rights.”

Echoing her statement, PRI Senator Alejandro Moreno said that holding another nationality does not make anyone an enemy of the nation, and that claiming a document determines loyalty is “a dangerous notion and an insult to our fellow citizens.”

Meanwhile, PT Senator Lizeth Sánchez said that the reform seeks to defend Mexico’s sovereignty, because external pressures influence decisions that belong to the Mexican people.

Sheinbaum has said that no president should have “two flags” or “two peoples” to respond to. For her, the heads of the executive power must maintain an exclusive legal and political loyalty to the Mexican state.

Surprisingly, two Morena Senators born in the United States voted in favor of the reform.

Senator Ricardo Sheffield acknowledged having been born in Los Angeles, California, and confirmed that his father was American, though he denied holding that citizenship himself — despite the fact that his siblings do.

Senator Javier Corral was born in El Paso, Texas, while Senator Cecilia Guadiana (also with Morena), who has been alleged to hold U.S. citizenship, requested a leave of absence for Sept. 29 and 30 and did not participate in the vote.

With reports from Expansión, Latinus and EFE

World.title: The MND Economy Index™ for July 2026
World.content:
Listen to this article

THE MND ECONOMY INDEX™

Providing broad insight into the Mexican economy

MND Intelligence · Fifth edition

Welcome to the fifth edition of the MND Economy Index™, part of the MND Intelligence™ suite of data products from Mexico News Daily.

The MND Economy Index™ is a 10-pillar, 19-indicator composite index that compiles a broad range of economic data into a single score between 0 and 100, giving Mexico News Daily readers a clear, accessible picture of how the Mexican economy is performing across multiple dimensions.

In the inaugural MND Economy Index™ article, published in late May, we not only analyzed the index score — 63.4 out of 100 — but also explained what the index is, why we developed it and how it works. Click here to read (or re-read) those explanations.

In this September edition of the MND Economy Index™ — which uses economic data primarily from the month of July — the index score is 73.1, a notable increase of 6.2 points compared to the previous score.

The score for July is easily the highest since we began publishing the MND Economy Index™, reflecting improvements in several of its component pillars.

Before we look more closely at the latest index result, here is a short guide to what the overall index score means.

85–100: Exceptional — the economy performing at a high level across nearly all indicators.

— the economy performing at a high level across nearly all indicators. 75–84: Strong — strong broad-based performance with only minor areas of concern.

— strong broad-based performance with only minor areas of concern. 60–74: Above neutral — meaningful strengths, but with notable room for improvement.

— meaningful strengths, but with notable room for improvement. 50–59: Mixed — passing marks overall, more indicators above benchmark than below.

— passing marks overall, more indicators above benchmark than below. Below 50: Broad underperformance — more indicators below benchmark than above.

The September edition of the MND Economy Index™ (based mainly on July data)

As noted above, the MND Economy Index™ score for this September edition is 73.1, an increase of 6.2 percentage points compared to the previous score. Below you will see the score for each of the ten pillars that make up the index, expressed out of 10 to reflect each pillar’s exact contribution to the final composite score.

Pillars are color-coded using a traffic light system: green (a score above 7.5) indicates strong performance; yellow (5.0–7.5) signals decent performance but with room for improvement; and red (below 5.0) flags a pillar that is falling short of its benchmark. Where a pillar score has improved compared to the previous month, an upward arrow appears alongside its corresponding traffic light; a downward arrow indicates a deterioration; and a pause symbol denotes no change.

As you’ll see below, scores for five of the ten MND Economy Index™ pillars increased in July compared to the previous month. Scores for the other five pillars declined. Collectively, the increases were more significant than the decreases, allowing the index score to rise.

It is noteworthy that, for the first time since we began publishing the MND Economy Index™ on a monthly basis, none of the pillars registered a red-light score.

🟢 ⬆️ INFLATION (9.68)

The score for this pillar increased to 9.68 in July from 9.33 in June. The inflation pillar thus replaced the monetary policy pillar as the largest contributor to the overall index score.

Annual headline inflation eased to 3.12% in July from 3.37% in June, causing an increase in the score for the current inflation component of the pillar. At 3.12%, the inflation rate was just 0.12 percentage points above the Bank of Mexico’s 3% target.

The score for the pillar component that considers the 12-month forward inflation forecast also increased as the Bank of Mexico anticipates an annual rate of 3.2% in the third quarter of 2027, which, of course, includes the month of July. The central bank is predicting a slightly higher inflation rate of 3.3% in the second quarter of next year. We used the Bank of Mexico’s Q2 2027 forecast for the previous edition of the MND Economy Index™ as it corresponded to the month of June.

The inflation pillar score is set to decline in the next edition of the MND Economy Index™ as inflation increased in August to reach an annual headline rate of 3.26%.

🟢 ⬇️ MONETARY POLICY (9.32)

The score for this pillar declined to 9.32 in July from 9.57 in June.

The Bank of Mexico’s benchmark interest rate remained at 6.50% in July after the central bank’s board voted to keep it at that level at a monetary policy meeting in late June. Therefore, there was no change in the interest rate component of the pillar score.

The deterioration in the pillar score was due to an increase in Mexico’s real interest rate in June — i.e., the Bank of Mexico’s benchmark interest rate minus the annual headline inflation rate. The real interest rate in July was 3.38%, a reading 0.68 points above the 2.7% neutral midpoint. The real interest rate in June, at 3.13%, was closer to the neutral midpoint than the reading in July.

🟢 ⬆️ MANUFACTURING SECTOR HEALTH (7.9)

The score for this pillar increased in July, rising to 7.9 from 6.9 in June.

The exports component of the pillar remained at the maximum score due to a 43.7% annual increase in export revenue in July, well above the 16.7% threshold needed for a perfect ten. Official data shows that almost 94% of Mexico’s export revenue in July came from the shipment abroad of manufactured goods.

The increase in the overall pillar score was due to 1.6% annual growth in manufacturing output in July. The year-over-year gain represented a significant improvement from the 2.4% decline in June.

🟢 ⬆️ ECONOMIC GROWTH (7.6)

The score for this pillar increased to 7.6 in July from 4.4 in June. The large increase in the score allowed economic growth to move from being a red light pillar to a green light pillar in the space of a single month.

The increase was due to a significantly higher annual economic growth rate in July. The annual growth rate in July was 3.3%, according to final data published by INEGI last week, whereas the rate in June was 1.7%.

The solid economic growth performance in July (month-over-month growth was 1.4%) came after Mexico’s economy expanded 1.9% in annual terms in the second quarter of the year. Annual growth in Q1 was just 0.4%.

🟡 ⬇️ SOVEREIGN RISK (7.41)

The score for this pillar was 7.41 in June, down slightly from 7.43 in June.

The score for the sovereign credit ratings component of the pillar remained unchanged in July, as there were no month-over-month changes to the Mexico ratings of Moody’s (Baa3/stable); S&P (BBB/negative); and Fitch (BBB-/stable).

The slight decline in the overall pillar score was due to a modest widening in Mexico’s 5-year credit default swap spread. The credit default swap spread was 87.19 basis points at the end of July, up from 86.87 basis points at the end of June. The increase reflected a slight rise in the market-implied cost of insuring against a Mexican sovereign default.

🟡 ⬇️ CURRENCY STABILITY: (6.79)

The score for this pillar declined slightly to 6.79 in July from 6.8 in June.

The standard deviation of daily exchange rate movements decreased to 0.40% in July from 0.49% in June, leading to a slight increase in the score for that component of the pillar.

The decrease in the pillar score in July was due to a lower spot rate score. The score for that component declined because the peso strengthened against the US dollar in July to trade at 17.32 to the greenback at the end of the month, an appreciation of 1% compared to the end of June.

The exchange rate was thus more distant from the index’s 19.00 USD:MXN baseline, which is based on the 2025 average rate. This pillar penalizes significant deviation from the 19.00 USD:MXN baseline in either direction, recognizing that a peso that has strengthened too far from this benchmark can erode export competitiveness and reduce the purchasing power of remittances, just as a weakening peso raises import costs.

🟡 ⬆️ INVESTMENT CLIMATE (6.58)

The score for this pillar increased slightly to 6.58 in July from 6.56 in June.

The increase was due to higher annual growth on the S&P/BMV FIBRAS Total Return Index, which tracks the performance of Mexico’s listed real estate investment trusts. The index grew 27.4% annually to the end of July, up from a 27.1% year-over-year increase at the end of June.

The score for the foreign direct investment component of the pillar remained steady as the latest available data is still that published by the Economy Ministry in late August. That data shows that foreign direct investment in Mexico increased 2.1% annually in the first six months of 2026 to reach a record high $34.96 billion. Annual FDI growth of 25% is required for a perfect score in that component of the investment climate pillar.

🟡 ⬆️ PRODUCTIVITY (6.4)

The score for this pillar increased to 6.4 in July from 3.8 in June.

Data published by the national statistics agency INEGI on Sept. 10 showed that the IGPLE — INEGI’s quarterly productivity measure — increased 1.7% annually in the second quarter of 2026. That level of productivity growth was significantly stronger than the +0.1% reading in the first quarter of 2026.

Thus, the pillar score increased 2.6 points in the space of a month.

INEGI will publish productivity data for the third quarter of 2026 in early December. Therefore, the score for the productivity pillar won’t change in the October and November editions of the MND Economy Index™.

🟡 ⬇️ LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT (6.18)

The score for this pillar decreased to 6.18 in July from 6.21 in June. Scores for two of the pillar’s three components increased, but the overall labor and employment score still edged down because the decline in the formal-employment component outweighed the combined gains in wage growth and informality.

In July, there was a 1.5% annual increase in the number of people in formal sector jobs, down from 2% growth in June. Therefore, there was a decrease in the score for that component of the pillar.

Nominal wages rose 6.7% year-on-year in June — up from 6.4% in June.

Year-over-year growth in Mexico’s informality rate was 0.1 points, down from an annual increase of 0.2 points in June. In July, 56.2% of all Mexican workers worked in the informal economy. Lowering the informality rate is a major challenge for the Mexican government.

🟡 ⬇️ EXTERNAL INCOME (5.26)

The score for this pillar declined in July, falling to 5.26 from 6.52 in June.

Incoming remittances increased 3% year-on-year — a decrease compared to the 4.2% annual growth in June.

Thus, the score for the remittances component of the pillar declined and moved further away from the 16.67% increase required for a perfect score.

A 1.3% year-over-year decline in tourism revenue in July was also a factor in the lower pillar score. The year-over-year decline in spending came after tourism revenue increased 5.9% annually in June, the month Mexico hosted most of its FIFA men’s World Cup matches.

The MND Economy Index™ trend

In the graph below you can see how the MND Economy Index™ score has changed over time.

We have now calculated a total of nine index scores in the period between March 2025 and July 2026. The difference between the lowest score (56.9 in March 2025 — predating the publication of the first MND Economy Index™ article) and the highest (73.1 in July 2026) is 16.1 points.

The much higher score in this edition of the the MND Economy Index™ indicates that Mexico’s economy is performing much better now than it was early in President Sheinbaum’s six-year term.

The improvement in the index score this year has also been notable, increasing almost 10 points between March and July.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: MND Local San Miguel de Allende: Investments, golf, midwives and a decline in violent crime
World.content:
Plenty of San Miguel de Allende news has been circulating lately, including possible federal funding to fix a water contamination problem, state investment in local infrastructure projects, growing opposition to a golf course proposal and the inauguration of the country’s first midwifery center.

Presa Allende cleanup included in 2027 federal budget

Mexico’s proposed 2027 federal budget allocates 100 million pesos (about US $5.6 million) to clean up the Ignacio Allende Dam southwest of San Miguel, which impounds the Presa Allende reservoir, and tributaries including the Río Laja, which flows into the reservoir.

The cleanup would involve “a comprehensive sanitation of the basin, the sustained elimination of water hyacinth, the improvement of water quality and control of sources of pollution.”

For several years, about three-quarters of Presa Allende has been covered by thick mats of water hyacinth (lirio acuático in Spanish). The infestation is triggered by untreated municipal sewage and fertilizer runoff flowing from the Río Laja into the reservoir.

This fast-growing invasive plant harms fish, birds and other wildlife by blocking sunlight and oxygen. It also creates a breeding ground for mosquitoes, restricts water levels, and obstructs fishermen and recreational boaters.

Amigos de la Presa, Audubon de México, Rescatemos la Presa Allende, Rotary Club of San Miguel de Allende-Midday, Caminos de Agua, and other local organizations and volunteers have sponsored cleanup projects and raised money and awareness in recent years. However, this marks the first time a significant amount of federal funding has been proposed for a long-term solution.

Action on the issue could come soon. President Claudia Sheinbaum’s finance minister delivered the proposed budget to the Chamber of Deputies in early September, and Congress typically adopts the final budget in November or December.

Update on proposed golf course near El Charco

Growing opposition to the construction of a golf course north of the El Charco del Ingenio Botanical Garden on the northeastern edge of San Miguel has bolstered an online petition drive. The petition has since garnered more than 84,000 signatures and more than 300 comments, all opposing the project. Signers expressed concern about threats to the environment and water supply while advocating for the preservation of wildlife habitat and green spaces.

State and local officials have spoken out about the proposal. Mayor Mauricio Trejo Pureco and Guanajuato Governor Libia Dennise García Muñoz Ledo were recently approached in San Miguel by a demonstrator holding an anti-golf course sign. Trejo said such projects must comply with the law. The governor later clarified during Sheinbaum’s Sept. 18 mañanera press conference in Irapuato that no authorization has been granted for a new golf course in San Miguel.

The proposal emerged about a year ago with the backing of Lorena Ochoa, a World Golf Hall of Famer described as Mexico’s most accomplished golfer. El Charco representatives stated the golf course would be in “the worst imaginable location” on a large rural tract of land directly bordering the botanical garden.

Opposition to the course mobilizes

In its September newsletter, El Charco stated it “celebrates the determined community mobilization opposing the golf course, hoping the developers behind this ill-advised initiative will heed the growing public opposition and acknowledge the project’s lack of water and ecological viability. Furthermore, it calls upon the municipal government not to authorize the project under any circumstances, given the heritage value and characteristics of our local landscape.”

San Miguel currently has three golf courses: two 18-hole courses (Malanquín and Las Ventanas) and one nine-hole course (Zirándaro).

Mexico’s first Excellence Center for Midwifery and Wellbeing opens in San Miguel

Mexico’s first midwifery center has opened in San Miguel, offering free maternal healthcare that combines traditional and professional midwifery with specialized medical services, including a midwifery school. The center, part of the national IMSS-Bienestar system, is located at Indalecio Allende 4 in the San Rafael neighborhood.

Sheinbaum inaugurated the facility Sept. 18 via video conference, noting the center was established following an approval process involving traditional midwives and obstetrician-gynecologists.

“It’s truly something special,” Sheinbaum said. “I was there when it was just about to be built, and now it’s a reality. And I hope we can build them in other places.”

Guanajuato governor announces investments in San Miguel

During her recent visit to San Miguel, Gov. García said the state will invest in local infrastructure and public works projects to drive economic growth and strengthen collaboration between state and local officials.

These investments will focus on transportation infrastructure improvements, healthcare services and social programs.

“San Miguel de Allende is a cornerstone of Guanajuato’s identity, tourism and economic vitality,” the governor said.

One proposed project includes a parking garage to relieve traffic in the city’s Centro district. Trejo proposed the project to reduce vehicle idling, enhance pedestrian safety and protect historic buildings from traffic-related wear and tear.

Centro suffers from a severe parking shortage, with reports indicating only about 5,000 spaces are available for the more than 100,000 visitors who travel to San Miguel during holidays and major events.

Officials report homicides down, arrests up in Guanajuato state

Homicides have dropped 43% this year in the state of Guanajuato, according to federal officials who shared statistics at Sheinbaum’s Sept. 18 mañanera in Irapuato.

Marcela Figueroa, head of the Executive Secretariat of the National Public Security System, reported an average of 3.2 homicides daily in Guanajuato in August. The daily average from January through August of this year was four, representing a 43% decrease compared with the same period in 2025.

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said 10,699 people were arrested in Guanajuato state between Oct. 1, 2024, and Aug. 31 of this year, with 172 “priority targets” taken into custody. He added that authorities seized more than 6 metric tons of drugs and 2,000 firearms during that timeframe, and dismantled two methamphetamine laboratories.

While questions remain regarding how some of these statistics are categorized and tracked, a new federal security strategy targeting key perpetrators of violence appears to be contributing to the decline.

Cathy Siegner is an independent journalist based in San Miguel and Montana. She has journalism degrees from the University of Oregon and Northwestern University.

World.title: Hurricane Polo hits the Sonora coast after making landfall and crossing the Baja Peninsula
World.content:
After lying threateningly off Mexico’s west coast for the better part of a week, a weakened Hurricane Polo finally made landfall in Baja California Sur at 10 p.m. Monday night, dumping 15-30 cm of rain but causing little harm before making its way across the Peninsula and the Gulf of California to the Sonora coast, where it still packed enough power Tuesday morning to lash the beach city of Guaymas.

Guaymas and nearby Empalme suffered flooding, power outages and damage from fallen trees Tuesday, with storm-generated waves crashing over the Guaymas malecón, flooding streets.

The Sonoran state government had announced on Monday the suspension of all “nonessential” activities, including schools, sports and certain work, in the state capital and more than a dozen municipalities

The Mexican Navy said it had personnel ready along the northern Pacific coast and, as a precaution, deployed three vessels to deliver aid to coastal communities isolated by the storm, while local authorities along the Baja California Peninsula said they had shelters at the ready.

Travel was also suspended where the hurricane was expected to make landfall, and ports across the region were closed.

Polo was expected to weaken later on Tuesday afternoon as it moves inland, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center. Before it does, however, Mexican authorities urged residents to remain safe indoors either ‌at their homes or in temporary shelters in high-risk areas. Hundreds of people across the region have been evacuated.

Polo has been an oddly behaving hurricane from its formation and continued to be so after landfall. It hit the Sonora coast hard after it weakened to a Category 1 storm. But after it made landfall in Baja California Sur (far north of Los Cabos, almost in the middle of the Peninsula at the level of the Comondú municipality) as a much stronger Category 3, state authorities were breathing a sigh of relief.

A “saldo blanco” for Baja California Sur was preliminarily reported Tuesday morning — no deaths, no injuries. “There was more water than wind,” Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío said. “So there was only minor damage, well within our capacity to deal with it.”

But it was still a hurricane. Mexico’s National Meteorological Service (SMN) reported that the hurricane brought to the Peninsula sustained winds of 150 to 170 km/h with gusts of 180 to 200 km/h and waves 7 to ⁠9 meters high.

With reports from CNBC, AP News, La Jornada and Once Noticias

World.title: Mexico: Jorge Kahwagi, Boxer-Turned-Congressman and Businessman, Dies at 58
World.content:
Mexico · Obituary · Politics

Latest — 30 September 2026 (evening) Where the cause-of-death report came from. The cerebral haemorrhage version was first aired by journalist Gustavo Adolfo Infante during Wednesday’s live broadcast of Sale el Sol (Imagen Televisión): “Jorge Kahwagi has just passed away at 58 years of age from a cerebral haemorrhage here in Mexico City.” By evening, the family had still issued no official statement confirming the cause — Luz Noticias stresses the version remains unconfirmed. Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time. Known medical history. In 2019 Kahwagi himself disclosed an emergency hospitalisation for a perforated gastric ulcer that led to a bacterial infection; he recovered. No link between that episode and his death has been established. The ring record, specified. Infobae dates his professional career to eleven fights between 2001 and 2005 — all won by knockout — including the Mexican cruiserweight title in 2002. In 2015 he returned for one more bout in Cebu, Philippines, stopping Ramón Olivas in 40 seconds. The politics, specified. Infobae and CRHoy date his first stint in the Chamber of Deputies from 2001. In 2004 he took leave from his seat to join Big Brother VIP while still drawing his congressional salary — a decision criticised at the time. He later led Nueva Alianza as secretary general and then national president between 2007 and 2011, during the party’s Elba Esther Gordillo era. His mother is Sonja Macari Chalhub. Sources: Infobae, Infobae (family), Luz Noticias, CRHoy.

Key Facts —The death. Jorge Kahwagi Macari — businessman, undefeated professional boxer and three-term federal deputy — died on Wednesday, 30 September 2026, in Mexico City. He was 58. —The confirmation. The news spread through public condolences from actor Roberto Palazuelos and Senator Manuel Velasco, who served alongside Kahwagi in the Chamber of Deputies. —The cause. Not officially confirmed. Infobae reports a presumed cerebral haemorrhage; the family has issued no statement. —The ring. An undefeated professional record — a dozen wins, every one by knockout — that was shadowed for years by persistent fight-fixing accusations. —The politics. Three stints in the Chamber of Deputies for the PVEM between 2003 and 2012, and later national president of the Nueva Alianza party.

Few Mexican public figures packed as many reinventions — ring, Congress, reality TV, boardroom — into one life as Jorge Kahwagi, and few attracted as much controversy along the way.

Jorge Kahwagi Macari died in Mexico City on Wednesday; he had lived out of the public eye for years. (File photo: The Rio Times archive)
