A Death Confirmed by Friends

News of the death emerged on Wednesday morning and was confirmed publicly by those close to the family. “Fly high, dear Jorge, just as you lived,” wrote Roberto Palazuelos — the actor and businessman known as the “Black Diamond” — in an Instagram message addressed to Kahwagi’s mother Sonja and his sisters Sonja and Layla. Senator Manuel Velasco, coordinator of the PVEM bloc in the Senate, mourned “my friend Jorge Kahwagi Macari”, with whom he had coincided as a federal deputy in the LIX Legislature.

No official cause of death has been released. Infobae reported that Kahwagi died in Mexico City, presumably of a cerebral haemorrhage, after years of serious health problems; other outlets, including Marca and Animal Político, stressed that no specific illness or circumstance had been confirmed. His death comes barely six months after that of his father, the Lebanese-Mexican businessman and newspaper publisher Jorge Kahwagi Gastine, who died in March at the age of 85.

The Undefeated Record Nobody Believed

Kahwagi’s sporting record reads like a boast: a professional boxing career without a single defeat, every victory by knockout — reported as twelve wins in twelve by Animal Político, while other accounts count eleven professional fights. He held Latin American titles sanctioned by both the WBC and the WBO. Yet almost from the start, the record was dogged by accusations of fixed fights and hand-picked opponents — a controversy that followed him for two decades and made him one of the most argued-about figures Mexican boxing ever produced.

Born in Mexico City on 28 May 1968, Kahwagi turned his sporting fame into a broader celebrity career that few boxers anywhere have matched. He feuded publicly with the wrestler Cibernético, took part in a season of Big Brother VIP — then Mexico’s most-watched reality format — and moved fluidly between the worlds of entertainment, business and eventually party politics.

From the Ring to San Lázaro

Between 2003 and 2012, Kahwagi sat three times in the Chamber of Deputies at San Lázaro, always through proportional representation for the Green Ecologist Party (PVEM) — including the LIX Legislature in which he overlapped with Velasco. He later served as national president of the Nueva Alianza party, cementing a political career that ran in parallel to his family’s business interests: the Grupo Crónica, which published the La Crónica de Hoy newspaper, and Cosmocolor, a firm long associated with the issuance of official identifications in Mexico.

That mixture of glamour, political access and family business made Kahwagi a fixture of Mexico’s early-2000s public life — and a standing invitation to scrutiny. Admirers saw a sportsman who reinvented himself; critics saw the archetype of a system in which fame, money and politics traded seamlessly among themselves.

Reality TV, Surgery and the Long Retreat

In later years the spotlight dimmed. Extensive cosmetic surgery visibly altered his face and physique, generating concern and commentary each time older footage resurfaced. His health became a recurring topic on social media, and by the 2020s he had largely withdrawn from public view, surfacing in the news mainly when his father’s death in March briefly revived interest in the family story.

Wednesday’s condolences suggest that the old networks — political, artistic, sporting — remained intact beneath the retreat. Velasco’s message spoke of friendship forged in Congress; Palazuelos’s of a bond with the whole family. Further details, including funeral arrangements, had not been announced by Wednesday evening.

What We Could Not Confirm

The cause of death has not been officially communicated; the cerebral haemorrhage reported by Infobae remains unconfirmed by the family. Accounts differ on whether his professional boxing record stood at eleven or twelve fights — all agree it was undefeated, every win by knockout. No funeral or memorial details had been published at the time of writing, and there has been no statement from the Grupo Crónica or the PVEM leadership beyond personal condolences.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was Jorge Kahwagi Macari?

A Mexican businessman, lawyer, professional boxer and politician who died on 30 September 2026 aged 58. He was an undefeated boxer with every win by knockout, a three-time federal deputy for the PVEM between 2003 and 2012, later national president of the Nueva Alianza party, and a Big Brother VIP participant.

What did Jorge Kahwagi die of?

No official cause has been announced. Infobae reported a presumed cerebral haemorrhage in Mexico City after years of health problems, but his family has not confirmed this. The death was made public through condolences from Roberto Palazuelos and Senator Manuel Velasco.

What was Jorge Kahwagi’s boxing record?

Undefeated, with every victory by knockout — reported variously as eleven or twelve professional wins. He held WBC and WBO Latin American titles, but his career was persistently shadowed by accusations of fixed fights and hand-picked opponents.





What could not be confirmed about Jorge Kahwagi?





The cause of death has not been officially communicated; the cerebral haemorrhage reported by Infobae remains unconfirmed by the family. Accounts differ on whether his professional boxing record stood at eleven or twelve fights — all agree it was undefeated, every win by knockout.

MARKETS · BRAZIL

Key Facts — The country Brazil votes in the first round of its presidential election on Sunday 4 October. The Ibovespa is the main index of B3, the São Paulo stock exchange.

— What happened At about 14:05 Brasília time on 30 September the Ibovespa stood at 186,618 points, up 1.52%, g1 market data showed. The official close comes after 17:00.

— The numbers The dollar traded at R$5.179 per dollar at about 14:05, down 0.74% (g1), after R$5.185 at 13:17 (InfoMoney). It closed Tuesday at R$5.217 per dollar.

— What it means for you A firmer real makes imports and travel abroad slightly cheaper for Brazilians. Visitors paying in dollars get a little less. One session changes little.

— Still open Whether the gain holds into the close after 17:00 on 30 September, and how markets price Sunday’s vote.

The Brazil Ibovespa rose more than 1% on Wednesday 30 September, four days before the first round of the presidential election. Banks and Petrobras led, while the dollar slipped towards R$5.18 per dollar.

At about 14:05 Brasília time (17:05 UTC) the index stood at 186,618 points, up 1.52%, according to g1 market data. InfoMoney reported the index up about 1% at 13:40. The official close comes after 17:00 and was not available at the time of writing.

Banks and Petrobras carry the index

Valor put the index at 185,738 points around 13:00, up 1.04%, after a range of 183,880 to 186,809. Projected turnover was R$24.6 billion (about US$4.7 billion).

Itaú preferred shares were up 3.90% and Bradesco preferred shares 2.76% at that point, Valor reported. Banco do Brasil gained 2.31% and BTG Pactual units 1.25%.

Petrobras added to the rise in the morning, with its preferred shares up 0.47% around 10:42, Exame reported. US crude was 2.29% higher at US$91.43 a barrel that morning.

Not every stock joined in. Homebuilder Tenda fell 5.23% after J.P. Morgan said its management sounded more cautious about the third quarter, citing tighter lending by state bank Caixa.

Wednesday’s move follows a four-session slide. The index closed at 187,423 points on 22 September and fell to 182,991 by 28 September. It rebounded 0.46% on Tuesday, as Brazil Ibovespa Ends Four-Day Slide at 183,828 Points Before the Election reported.

A softer US inflation reading did much of the work

The main trigger came from Washington. The PCE price index, the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.4% in the year to August, below the 3.7% expected.

That raised bets that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its meeting at the end of October, Valor and InfoMoney reported. Wall Street’s Nasdaq was up about 1% at midday.

The real followed. The dollar traded at R$5.185 per dollar around 13:00, down 0.59%, after touching R$5.163, InfoMoney reported.

g1 showed R$5.179 per dollar, down 0.74%, at about 14:05. The central bank’s PTAX reference rate closed at R$5.1809. On Tuesday the currency closed at R$5.217, and on Monday at R$5.225 per dollar.

The election trade cuts both ways

Some traders tied part of the rally to polls showing an edge for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro over President Lula, Valor reported. The polls themselves remain tight and point in different directions.

A Quaest survey published on Monday had Lula at 39% and Bolsonaro at 34% in the first round, g1 reported. They tied at 42% in a runoff. Regional polls such as Rio Grande do Sul Poll Puts Flávio Bolsonaro Three Points Ahead of Lula add to the uncertainty.

HSBC sees up to 35% upside for Brazilian shares if the result strengthens expectations of fiscal consolidation, Valor reported. Without that prospect, the bank sees room for a 12% fall.

The fiscal backdrop is part of the debate. The consolidated public sector ran a primary deficit of R$10 billion (about US$1.9 billion) in August, central bank data showed.

Gross public debt rose to 82.9% of GDP from 82.6%, InfoMoney reported. High borrowing costs also weigh on companies, as Brazil Corporate Debt Costs Near 24% as Moody’s Warns of a 2027 Squeeze showed.

The official Brazil Ibovespa close for 30 September was not available at publication. Intraday gains can shrink or widen in the final hours of trading.

It is also unclear how far prices already reflect Sunday’s outcome. HSBC expects any first reaction to fade until the next government’s cabinet and fiscal plans become clearer.

World.title: St Kitts and Nevis PM Drew Meets Deputy Hanley in Miami While Recovering From Stroke
World.content:

One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life.

POLITICS · ST KITTS AND NEVIS

Key Facts — The country St Kitts and Nevis is a two-island federation in the eastern Caribbean with about 50,000 people. Its Labour Party has governed alone since winning six of 11 seats in August 2022.

— What happened On Monday 28 September Deputy Prime Minister Geoffrey Hanley briefed Prime Minister Terrance Drew in Miami, the Prime Minister’s Office said. Drew has been recovering in Florida since a stroke in late August.

— Who is involved Drew and Hanley of the Labour government. Minister Konris Maynard acted as prime minister while Hanley was at the UN. Opposition leader Mark Brantley heads the Nevis-based CCM.

— What it means for you Government business, including citizenship-by-investment policy, continues under acting arrangements. Drew says he will return to full duties “in due course”.

— Still open No return date has been announced. Medical details beyond Drew’s own statements have not been published.

St Kitts PM Terrance Drew met his deputy, Geoffrey Hanley, in Miami on Monday 28 September. Drew has been recovering in Florida since suffering a stroke in late August.

The Prime Minister’s Office said Hanley flew in to brief him after leading the federation’s delegation to the UN General Assembly. Drew used the meeting to thank his Cabinet for “steady and dedicated leadership during this period”.

What the two men discussed

According to the statement, Hanley gave a full update on government business and on the federation’s work at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. The two also discussed current government priorities.

Drew also thanked Cabinet minister Konris Maynard, who served as acting prime minister while Hanley was in New York. The statement was carried by SKNVibes on 29 September and by Nevis Pages and WIC News on 30 September.

“My commitment to you, and to the vision we share for our Federation, remains unwavering,” Drew said. He added that he looks forward to returning to his full duties “in due course”.

A month of acting arrangements

Drew fell ill at home in late August, and Hanley addressed the nation on his hospitalisation on 31 August, WINN FM reported. According to Caribbean Life, he was first stabilised in nearby Martinique and then moved to a hospital in Florida.

Hanley became acting prime minister and took over the finance and health ministries, Virgin Islands News Online reported on 2 September. Justice Minister Garth Wilkin took national security, citizenship and immigration.

In a video in mid-September, the St Kitts PM confirmed the stroke and said he had left hospital. He said a dissected artery at the back of his brain caused it, and that therapy was progressing well.

Why “confidence” is the message

Local reports framed the Miami meeting as a show of unity inside the Labour government. The facts point to continuity rather than a coalition under strain.

Labour, led by Drew, won six of the 11 elected seats in August 2022, according to the government information service. That is a majority on its own, with no partner party needed.

Labour won six of 11 elected seats on 5 August 2022 and governs without a coalition partner; the CCM holds all three Nevis seats. Source: SKN Information Service, 6 Aug 2022.

The Concerned Citizens’ Movement (CCM) took all three Nevis seats and sits in opposition. Its leader, Mark Brantley, is both federal opposition leader and Premier of Nevis, heading the island’s own administration.

Labour and the CCM are rivals at the ballot box. Yet on 3 September Brantley urged people not to politicise Drew’s illness, WINN FM reported.

“Before Terence Drew was Prime Minister, he was human,” Brantley said. No public dispute between Labour and the CCM over the acting arrangements has been reported.

What it means for the federation

A small state run for weeks by an acting leader faces questions about decisions on budgets and investment. Citizenship-by-investment rules, under EU pressure, are one such file, as we reported earlier this month.

The regional central bank also recently cut its economic outlook for St Kitts and Nevis. Continuity at the top helps keep policy steady while those issues are handled.

What Is Not Yet Known

No date has been announced for the St Kitts PM’s return home. The government has not said when the acting portfolio assignments will end.

Beyond Drew’s own account, no medical update has been published. It is also not known whether any major Cabinet decisions await his return.

World.content:

URBAN RENEWAL · BARBADOS

Key Facts — The country Barbados, an island republic in the eastern Caribbean that uses a Barbados dollar pegged at two per US dollar. Temple Yard is an artisans’ quarter in Cheapside, central Bridgetown.

— What happened On Tuesday 29 September, Housing Minister Chris Gibbs told Barbados Today that phase one of the Temple Yard rebuild will be finished before 30 November.

— Who is involved The Housing and Lands ministry, state-owned Barbados Tourism Investment Inc. (BTI), and the roughly two dozen artisans, many linked to the Rastafarian community, who left the site in December 2024.

— What it means for you Visitors to Bridgetown should see leather, craft and food stalls return to Cheapside, possibly by the holiday season. Phase one mainly rehouses existing tenants.

— Still open No move-in date for tenants and no completion date for phase two, according to the minister on 29 September. Earlier targets for January 2026 slipped.

The first phase of the Temple Yard redevelopment in Bridgetown, Barbados, will be finished before Independence Day on 30 November. Housing Minister Chris Gibbs gave that pledge to Barbados Today on Tuesday 29 September.

He spoke during a break in the House of Assembly, the elected lower chamber of parliament. Phase one is meant to bring back most of the artisans who worked there before construction began.

What the minister promised

Gibbs said the site is in final quality checks and “snagging”, the builders’ term for fixing small defects before handover. Phase one, he said, “does almost 100 per cent match” the space the artisans had before.

He could not give a completion date for phase two, which is meant to add room for new craftspeople and creative shops. Barbados Today noted that no date has been set for tenants to move in.

A cultural hub with a long wait

Temple Yard in Cheapside has long been a centre of leatherwork, crafts and food for Bridgetown’s Rastafarian community. Many stalls had fallen into disrepair over the years.

Prime Minister Mia Mottley announced the rebuild in 2019, saying she wanted to “remove every stain of discrimination against Barbadians”, especially Rastafarians. Work only began after the artisans were moved out in December 2024.

According to Barbados Tourism Investment Inc. (BTI), the state company running the project, a survey had found about 24 legitimate artisans on the site. About 15 moved temporarily to the Pelican craft centre, Barbados Today reported in January 2025.

Deadlines that have slipped before

This is not the first target date. In January 2026, a BTI spokeswoman told Barbados Today that phase one would be finished by the end of that month.

She added that phase two would take four to five months, finishing the project in the first half of 2026. She expected just under 40 artisans once the site was fully running.

Relocated traders told the paper that sales at Pelican had dropped sharply because customers could not find them. For them, the timing of the move back matters more than the official finish date.

Part of a wider push for creative space

Gibbs linked the project to a national plan for permanent workspaces for artists and micro-businesses. At the same sitting, the House approved a 25-year lease for a long-promised National Art Gallery.

The gallery will occupy Block A at the Garrison, a World Heritage site, with about 4,000 square metres of land and buildings. The nominal rent is Bds$6,000 a year (about US$3,000 at the fixed peg of two Barbados dollars per US dollar).

For more background on the island, see Barbados Explained: The Island, the Economy, the Republic and What to Watch. Those considering a longer stay can read Moving to Barbados: Visas, Costs, Work Permits and Daily Life.

What Is Not Yet Known

The government has not said when tenants get keys, what fees they will pay, or how stalls will be allocated. Earlier, a vendors’ group had asked for written guarantees of first choice.

The minister’s timeline has so far been reported only by Barbados Today and has not been independently confirmed. No official schedule for phase two has been published.

Sources: Barbados Today, “Temple Yard redevelopment phase to be ready ‘before November 30’”, 29 September 2026; Barbados Today, “Artisans to return to ‘reimagined’ Temple Yard ‘in coming months’”, 6 January 2026; Barbados Today, “Temple Yard redevelopment to begin this year, officials vow”, 23 January 2025.

POLITICS · EL SALVADOR

Key Facts — The country El Salvador chooses its president, all 60 members of parliament and its municipal councils on one day, Sunday 28 February 2027, in a single round.

— What happened On Wednesday 30 September the Supreme Electoral Tribunal formally called the 2027 general elections, La Página reported. The call opens candidate registration on Thursday 1 October.

— Who is involved Five parties plan presidential tickets: Nuevas Ideas, the FMLN, ARENA, the PCN and the FPS. Four more run only for parliament and councils, El Mundo reported on 30 September.

— What it means for you Presidential and parliamentary candidates file from 1 October to 19 November. The voter register closes on 29 December 2026, according to the tribunal’s calendar.

— Still open Publication of the formal decree in the official gazette, and how many tickets survive the tribunal’s review, were not yet confirmed on 30 September.

El Salvador electoral court magistrates formally called the general elections of 28 February 2027 on Wednesday 30 September. The Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE), which organises and referees elections, made the call official, the Salvadoran outlet La Página reported.

The step opens the 50-day window for presidential and parliamentary candidates, starting on Thursday 1 October. It follows the preview in El Salvador Election: Bukele and His Rivals Can Register From 1 October.

What the formal call sets in motion

Candidates for president, vice-president and the 60 seats of the Legislative Assembly, the parliament, file with the tribunal until 19 November. Candidates for municipal councils file between 9 and 19 November.

Filing is not the same as being on the ballot, the newspaper elsalvador.com noted on 29 September. The calendar provides for review, correction of defects and then final registration or rejection.

Each candidate also needs a certificate from the Court of Accounts, the public audit body, showing no unpaid final judgments. Its president, Walter Sosa, promised certificates within eight days through a new online system, El Mundo reported.

The court accepts requests from 1 October to 11 November. The Electoral Code allows it up to 15 days per request.

Three campaign clocks

Legal campaign windows before the 28 February 2027 vote: 121 days for president, 60 for parliament, 29 for municipal councils, all ending 24 February (Rio Times count, inclusive). Source: TSE electoral calendar via El Mundo and elsalvador.com, 29-30 Sep 2026.

Campaigning is not allowed at once. Presidential candidates may campaign from 27 October, parliamentary candidates from 27 December and council candidates from 27 January.

All three windows close on 24 February 2027, four days before the vote. The voter register closes on 29 December 2026, according to the TSE calendar updated in July.

Who is expected on the ballot

No more than ten parties are expected to take part, El Mundo reported on 30 September. Five plan presidential tickets: Nuevas Ideas, the FMLN, ARENA, the National Coalition Party (PCN) and the Salvadoran Patriotic Fraternity (FPS).

Vamos, the Christian Democrats, GANA and Fuerza Solidaria will run only for parliament and councils. Democracia Salvadoreña held a primary call but published no results, the paper added.

President Nayib Bukele of Nuevas Ideas seeks a third consecutive term, for 2027 to 2033. A constitutional reform in July 2025 allowed indefinite re-election, scrapped the runoff and set six-year terms.

That reform also moved the presidential vote forward from 2029. His record is set out in Who Is Nayib Bukele? El Salvador’s President Explained.

How the challengers view the referee

The FMLN’s Rafael Aguirre told El Mundo he does not fully trust the tribunal, but did not back claims of fraud. He asked the TSE to admit observers from “any organisation” so suspicions can be dispelled or proven.

Orlando Delcid of the FPS said he trusts the tribunal, which he said fairly rejected his earlier attempt to found a party. ARENA’s Mayteé Iraheta said the elections follow current law but that “the process is the questionable part”.

What Is Not Yet Known

El Mundo reported that the call becomes formal only once a decree appears in the Diario Oficial, the official gazette. That publication could not be independently confirmed on 30 September, and the El Salvador electoral court website was down for maintenance.

It is also unclear how many tickets will clear review, and whether the tribunal will accredit independent observer missions.

Sources: Diario La Página, 30 September 2026; Diario El Mundo, 30 September 2026; Diario El Mundo on Court of Accounts certificates, 30 September 2026; elsalvador.com, 29 September 2026; Supreme Electoral Tribunal, Calendario Electoral 2027.

ENERGY · CURAÇAO

Key Facts — The country Curaçao, a Dutch Caribbean island off Venezuela. One state-owned utility, Aqualectra, produces its electricity and drinking water, largely from wind, solar and fuel-fired machines.

— What happened The firm Eco Capital Curaçao asked parliament to push for a 90-to-120-day government taskforce on a rooftop “virtual power network”, Curacao.nu reported on 30 September 2026.

— The numbers From 1 October the cheapest household power band rises from about 63 to 70 guilder cents per kWh (about US$0.35 to US$0.39), the regulator said on 24 September.

— What it means for you Nothing changes on bills yet. Residents face higher October tariffs and possible rotating cuts of up to two hours, Aqualectra warned on 30 September.

What Eco Capital is asking for

The firm is not asking the Staten, Curaçao’s parliament, to approve its own project. It wants the Staten to urge the government to create an “Executive Virtual Power Network Taskforce” for 90 to 120 days.

That group would deliver a framework covering investment costs, technical rules, responsibilities and risks. It would also set the criteria for deciding whether a pilot goes ahead.

Eco Capital proposes the Koraal Specht and Cornelisbaai area as a test case. New commercial and industrial activity at Cornelisbaai adds demand, which the firm says rooftop solar and batteries in nearby Koraal Specht homes could help meet.

Curacao.nu reported earlier on the firm’s wider plan to link nearly 7,000 homes into one centrally controlled plant. Eco Capital fears the utility’s new Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) leaves no clear route for such pooled private producers.

Who would sit at the table

The proposed members include Aqualectra, the Regulatory Authority Curaçao (RAC) and two ministries. The state fuel distributor Curoil, the Central Bank of Curaçao and Sint Maarten, banks, pension funds and insurers are also named.

The work list is technical. It covers steering thousands of small units as one controllable source, data exchange, grid safety, cybersecurity, financing and consumer protection.

The idea is not new. Eco Capital first filed it in September 2023, and the planning ministry (VVRP) replied in February 2024 asking for further detail, according to Curacao.nu.

Rising bills and a stretched grid

Household electricity tariffs in Curaçao by monthly usage band, September versus October 2026, in guilder cents per kWh (rounded). Source: Regulatory Authority Curaçao via Curacao.nu and nu.CW, 24 September 2026.

From 1 October the cheapest household band, up to 250 kWh a month, rises from about 63 to 70 guilder cents per kWh (about US$0.35 to US$0.39). Curaçao’s guilder is pegged at 1.79 per US dollar.

The regulator blamed higher fuel costs and weaker expected wind, Curacao.nu and nu.CW reported on 24 September. A 10 percent monthly cap pushes part of the increase into November.

Supply is tight too. On 30 September Aqualectra said several machines and a 13-megawatt gas turbine were still unavailable, leaving it heavily reliant on wind, nu.CW reported.

On 15 August the utility expected evening demand of 128 megawatts against 98 megawatts of machine capacity, and rotated cuts across districts. An island-wide blackout on 27 August 2025 lasted almost a full day.

The case for and the risks

There is a stabiliser in the record. Aqualectra says tariffs fell about 6 percent in 2024 and nearly 11 percent in 2025, and it expects over 70 percent renewable power by 2027.

The government also announced a national energy policy on 8 September, with the RAC coordinating. A virtual power plant could fit that effort. Pooling home systems still raises questions about grid control, cost and who carries the risk.

Power costs are a regional theme. Governments are trying storage and price relief alike, from Brazil Puts a Battery Inside a Transmission Auction to tariff relief in Honduras Electricity Tariff Frozen for Six Months as Asfura Signs Law.

What Is Not Yet Known

It is not known whether parliament will adopt the request or when it might debate it. Aqualectra, the RAC and the government had not responded publicly by 30 September.

No cost estimate for a pilot has been published. How much of the delayed tariff increase lands in November is also still to be set.

Sources: Curacao.nu, 30 September 2026; Curacao.nu, 13 September 2026; Curacao.nu, 24 September 2026; nu.CW, 24 September 2026 (RAC tariffs); nu.CW, 30 September 2026 (Aqualectra); nu.CW, 15 August 2026; nu.CW, 3 September 2025; nu.CW, 15 January 2026 (Aqualectra year in review); nu.CW, 10 September 2026.

World.content:

POLITICS · HAITI

Key Facts — The country Haiti, a Caribbean nation of about 12 million, has had no elected president since 2021. Its planned vote would be the first national election in a decade.

— What happened In a note dated Monday 28 September 2026, the Haiti electoral council told parties and candidates not to campaign before it sets the official period, Juno7 and AlterPresse reported.

— The numbers As of 21 September, 7 presidential, 162 Senate and 419 lower-house candidates had registered, and 628,755 voters were on the roll, the council said.

— What it means for you The first round is still set for 13 December 2026, with a runoff on 21 February 2027. Campaigning is allowed only once the council opens the period.

— Still open When the campaign starts. The July calendar set 5 October, but candidate registration was extended on 16 September to 9 October.

The Haiti electoral council has told parties and candidates to stop any activity that looks like campaigning. It says the official campaign period has not begun and has not yet been set.

The warning came in a note dated Monday 28 September, reported by Juno7, AlterPresse and Le Nouvelliste. It lands as political platforms hold rallies ahead of a first round planned for 13 December.

What the electoral council said

The Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) is the body that organises Haitian elections. It cites article 193 of the electoral decree of 2 June 2026, which gives it sole power to fix the campaign period.

The council asks parties, political groupings and candidates to avoid any activity “assimilable” to campaigning before that period opens. It also calls for a “serene, fair” climate, AlterPresse reported.

The note does not name any party or list penalties. The council said it would run the process with independence, integrity and transparency, according to Juno7.

A calendar under pressure

Registered voters in Haiti on 6 and 21 September 2026 against the electoral council's goal of 4 million; registration closes on 13 October. Source: Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) figures via Juno7 and The Haitian Times, September 2026.

The calendar published on 27 July set the first-round campaign from 5 October to 12 December, The Haitian Times reported. Final results were due by 7 March 2027, with winners taking office by 12 March.

Deadlines have since moved twice. On 16 September the council extended online candidate registration and document filing to 9 October, while keeping 13 December, Juno7 reported.

Voter registration is the slower part. The roll stood at 506,953 on 6 September against a goal of 4 million, Juno7 reported, citing council data.

By 21 September it had reached 628,755, the council said. Registration closes on 13 October, and 1,285 registration centres were operating, including 148 in the violence-hit West.

There are stabilising signs. The UN Security Council extended the Gang Suppression Force for six months on 29 September, Juno7 reported.

The council and the foreign ministry are also preparing a pilot vote for Haitians abroad. A note dated 29 September again named 13 December as the election date, AlterPresse reported.

Parties already on the road

Some platforms have been touring for weeks. VIKTWA, which says it groups 52 parties, rallied in Pétion-Ville on Sunday 27 September for presidential candidate Wilner Joseph, Juno7 reported.

The platform had earlier held events in Cap-Haïtien, Gonaïves and Delmas. The council’s note does not refer to VIKTWA or any other group.

Civic groups are pressing on other fronts. The Collectif Kenbe Kapòw in the North wrote to council president Peterson Pierre-Louis asking for more registration agents and simpler procedures.

The Haiti electoral council also faces doubts from parties that call the timetable unrealistic, The Haitian Times reported. Background on the vote is in Haiti December Election Set as First Vote in a Decade.

What Is Not Yet Known

The council has not published a new campaign start date. With filing open to 9 October, the 5 October opening in the July calendar looks set to move.

It is also unclear what sanctions, if any, apply to early campaigning. Juno7 reported that the council is discussing possible changes to the electoral decree with parties and government.

Sources: Provisional Electoral Council (CEP), note of 28 September 2026, as reported by Juno7, AlterPresse and Le Nouvelliste; Juno7 on the 9 October filing deadline, voter registration, the VIKTWA rally and Kenbe Kapòw; AlterPresse on the diaspora pilot; The Haitian Times on the July calendar and registration figures.

World.content:

One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life.

TOURISM · BAHAMAS

Key Facts — The country The Bahamas, an island nation off Florida that lives on visitors. A US Commerce Department guide, updated April 2026, credits tourism with about 70% of GDP and over half of all jobs.

— What happened On 29 September 2026 the Bahamas Hotel and Tourism Association (BHTA) named Robert “Sandy” Sands interim president. He replaces Jackson Weech, who becomes Director General of Tourism on 1 October.

— The numbers 12.5 million visitors in 2025, up 11.4% (Ministry of Tourism, January 2026). Arrivals for January to July 2026 rose 14.8% to 8.5 million (Central Bank of The Bahamas, August review).

— What it means for you The hotels’ main lobby and the ministry’s senior technical post are now linked by one career. Closer work on airlift, staff training and overnight stays is the stated aim.

— Still open Sands serves only until the BHTA annual general meeting on 2 December 2026, when officers and directors are elected. Whether he will stand for a full term has not been reported.

The main Bahamas tourism association, which speaks for the country’s hotels, has put a familiar figure back in charge. The Bahamas Hotel and Tourism Association (BHTA) named Robert “Sandy” Sands interim president, state broadcaster ZNS reported on 29 September.

Sands replaces Jackson Weech, who leaves to become Director General of the Ministry of Tourism from 1 October. The Nassau outlet Eyewitness News also reported the handover on 30 September.

A Veteran Returns for Two Months

Sands is the association’s immediate past president. According to ZNS, he has already led the BHTA for five terms, or ten years, dating back to 1990.

He will hold office until the annual general meeting on 2 December 2026. Elections of officers and directors take place that day.

Sands praised Weech for leading with “competence, consideration, resolution”. He called the ministry’s choice “an astute decision” that should strengthen ties between the industry and government.

“We look forward to working with him collaboratively in his new capacity,” Sands said. For this Bahamas tourism association, the move places a former president inside the ministry it lobbies.

Record Arrivals, but Cruise-Heavy

Total visitor arrivals (air and sea) to the Bahamas: 9.65 million in 2023, 11.22 million in 2024 and 12.5 million in 2025. Source: Bahamas Ministry of Tourism, Feb 2025 and Jan 2026.

The handover comes during the strongest run in Bahamian tourism history. The country received 12.5 million visitors in 2025, up 11.4%, then-minister Chester Cooper told Parliament in January.

Sea arrivals, mostly cruise passengers, passed 10.6 million, up 14%. Foreign air arrivals were nearly 1.7 million, 1.6% below 2024.

Air visitors fill the rooms that BHTA members sell. Stopovers reached 1.821 million in 2025, only just above the 1.806 million of 2019.

This year the pace has held. Arrivals from January to July rose 14.8% to 8.5 million, the Central Bank of The Bahamas reported in its August review.

Sea visitors made up 7.2 million of that total. Air arrivals grew 5.8% to 1.2 million, a slower but still positive trend for hotels.

The sector’s weight is hard to overstate. A US Commerce Department guide, updated in April 2026, says tourism generates about 70% of GDP and employs over half the workforce.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) found stayover growth “relatively flat” in its 2025 review. It flagged a global slowdown as a threat to tourism demand.

Around 80% of visitors come from the United States, the IMF noted, according to The Nassau Guardian. See our guide to the Bahamian economy for background.

From Hotel Lobby to the Ministry

The Ministry of Tourism named Weech Director General effective 1 October, TravelPress reported. He had been BHTA president since December 2024.

Weech most recently served as vice president and general manager of the Royal Towers at Atlantis Paradise Island. His career spans more than 35 years in the Bahamas, the Caribbean and Britain.

Tourism Minister Glenys Hanna-Martin, who in May became the first woman in the post, said he “understands this industry from the ground up”. The ministry cited “several record-setting months” in 2026.

In June the BHTA set out its priorities for the new minister. They included workforce training, stopover growth, Family Island airlift and better infrastructure, Eyewitness News reported.

Weech led that delegation, with Sands beside him as immediate past president. The Bahamas tourism boom of 2026 gives those demands extra weight.

What Is Not Yet Known

It has not been reported whether Sands will seek a full term on 2 December. No other candidates have been named either.

The ministry has not said which BHTA priorities Weech will take up first. Full-year arrival figures for 2026 will only be published in early 2027.
