PM Narendra Modi held a phone call with US President Donald Trump Wednesday to review bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, critical technologies and energy, amid increasing friction in the relationship driven primarily by Indiaâs purchase of Russian oil.Modi is learnt to have touched upon Indiaâs concerns related to the USâ latest Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) that allows the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries like India and China for their procurement of Russian oil.In the run up to the Modi-Trump conversation â their first since they met in France in June â both external affairs minister S Jaishankar and foreign secretary Vikram Misri had flagged the same concerns with American authorities, emphasising the recently enacted SRIA would have consequences for India-US ties. India continues to maintain that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure reliable and affordable supplies for 1.4 billion people.Modi said in a post on X that he had productive conversation with Trump. âWe reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward,â said the PM, adding that they also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security.An Indian readout said they agreed to maintain close engagement to deepen cooperation for the benefit of the people of both countries, and also to remain in touch. There was no White House readout till late in the evening.According to diplomatic sources, the conversation helped reinforce the strategic partnership amid the friction over the US passage of the Russia-related legislation, and also differences over trade that have prevented the 2 countries from concluding a bilateral trade agreement. Modi will travel to the US in December for the G20 summit in Florida where he is likely to also have a bilateral meeting with Trump. However, potential US tariffs or penalties could disrupt the diplomatic buildup to the visit.Jaishankar had raised Indiaâs concerns related to the SRIA with his counterpart Marco Rubio in a meeting on the margins of the UNGA last week. Earlier this week, foreign secretary Vikram Misri told a visiting Congressional delegation that the new law will have a negative impact on not just bilateral relations but also the energy situation in global markets.Trade and energy, however, are not the only issues that India and the US need to address to get the relationship back on track. While still in the US, Jaishankar warned the Trump administration this week that the lack of empathy or understanding about Indiaâs cross-border terrorism concerns â as evident from the US courting of Pakistan â will also hurt the relationship.

Machchhar, an Indian national based in Dubai, was reportedly stabbed and severely wounded during the incident. According to Israeli reports, he intervened after an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft.

NEW DELHI: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has praised Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery after he was stabbed and seriously injured while trying to stop an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv, saying he helped save the lives of 174 people on board.âMy salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery.Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker â preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster.He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery.He is a true hero,â Netanyahu said in a post.The flydubai rescue flight carrying passengers from the diverted flight landed at Ben Gurion International Airport in Israel, The Times of Israel reported. About 180 passengers, most of them Israelis, were on the rescue flight.The original flight, flydubai FZ1073 travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, made an emergency landing at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia after an altercation in the cockpit.Machchhar, an Indian national based in Dubai, was reportedly stabbed and severely wounded during the incident. According to Israeli reports, he intervened after an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft.Netanyahu said the evidence indicated that the pilot had stabbed his fellow pilot and claimed there was an intention to crash the plane.In a video statement, Netanyahu described the incident as âan extremely serious security incidentâ. He said an Israeli passenger and a crew member managed to stop the pilot as he was allegedly attempting to damage the aircraft's systems.Another crew member then entered the cockpit and managed to stabilise the plane, Netanyahu said. He added that Saudi authorities were interrogating the suspect.An Israeli official said a âsevere disasterâ had been averted.The aircraft was diverted to Tabuk, where it made the emergency landing. The passengers were later flown back to Israel on the rescue flight.

World.title: Kathua fratricide: Plaint over bringing child to project site enraged killer
World.content:
JAMMU: The CISF jawan who shot dead four colleagues, including an assistant commandant, at an NHPC hydel plant in J&Kâs Kathua district had allegedly got into a heated argument with one of the victims over bringing his child to the project site, police said Wednesday.

The accused head constable, Abhidesh Kumar Singh of Bihar, was remanded in seven-day police custody. DG (CISF) Parveen Ranjan visited the project site to oversee the situation and get a first-hand report from officers on the previous eveningâs fratricide.

Police said Abhidesh and his wife Pooja, both head constables with CISF, were posted at the same Sewa-III project of the central PSU at Basohliânear the Himachal Pradesh borderâbut assigned different shifts.

The unit administration had not allowed Pooja to enter or stay in the Quarter Guard area with her young child, aged about two-and-a-half.

âWhile joining their respective shift at the site, either spouse would bring the toddler along to hand him over to the one heading home, despite being repeatedly warned against bringing the child to the project site. Even on Tuesday, one of them had brought the child to the site to hand over to the spouse, and someone complained about it to the Company Commander,â an officer said.

In a fit of rage, Abhidesh walked into the Operations section office near the main gate and opened indiscriminate fire, killing Pandey, sub-inspector Lakshman Singh, and constables Sanjeev Kumar and Mohammed Rafiq,â the officer said.

World.title: J&K parties, barring BJP, blast top officials for letter to assembly against statehood resolution
World.content:
Congress chief whip Nizamuddin Bhat the officers had challenged the authority of the Speaker by writing to the Assembly. 'It is absolutely unconstitutional. J&K Assembly is not a Panchayati board,' he said.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Two top officials of the J&K administration came under fire Wednesday from political parties in the union territory for writing to the Assembly and asking it not to proceed with the resolution for the restoration of statehood, which also contained a reference to autonomy and was passed by the House on Monday.Peoples Conference, PDP and Congress sought action against chief secretary Atal Dulloo and the law secretary.Speaking on Wednesday, the last day of the Assemblyâs autumn session, Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone said the two officials had undermined the House and sought action against them. âThe act of the chief secretary of writing a letter to the Assembly is a disdainful act of brutality against the Assembly. Is he bigger than the people of J&K,â Lone said.Congress chief whip Nizamuddin Bhat the officers had challenged the authority of the Speaker by writing to the Assembly. âIt is absolutely unconstitutional. J&K Assembly is not a Panchayati board,â he said.PDPâs Waheed Parra moved a motion of privilege against two officials, stating that the chief minister had placed on record their conduct as they questioned the contents and language of a resolution of this House.âThe power of an elected legislature to initiate, deliberate upon, amend and adopt resolutions is a core parliamentary function. While officers are entitled to provide administrative or legal advice to the govt within the scope of their duties, such advice cannot be permitted to become an instrument for questioning, constraining or intruding upon the legislative privileges and authority of this House,â the motion reads.On Monday, while arguing for statehood restoration, CM Omar Abdullah had said law secretary and chief secretary had written to the Assembly asking it not to discuss the statehood resolution. âI am the law minister and this opinion has gone to you (Speaker) and I have not even seen it. I do not know whether the chief secretary is sending you a letter regarding my resolution,â he said. âCan you imagine this would happen in any state or UT that the chief minister moves a resolution in the Assembly and the law secretary gives an opinion against it. This can happen only here. And similar things happen here every day.âBJPâs Sunil Sharma, who is the leader of opposition in the Assembly, defended the officials and sought action against the chief minister and the Speaker. âIn this Assembly, a resolution was brought seeking the pre-1953 position of J&K, for which Omar Abdullahâs grandfather, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, had to spend 22 years in jail. Sheikh Abdullah was similarly seeking a separate Constitution, a separate flag, a requirement for anyone entering J&K to seek permission and a separate head of state for J&K.Late Jawaharlal Nehru government sent him to jail because there was no place for such things in the country,â Sharma said.âThe resolution brought by Omar Abdullah was unconstitutional. Government institutions and agencies should take serious note of it and should take action against his government,â he said.Sharma said it was an indication of Muslim sub-nationalism.He also said the Congress, which supported the resolution, will have to pay a political price for it as the BJP would take up the issue against the party at the national level.

World.title: Gadkari announces Rs 1,176 cr 6-lane bridge over Teesta
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Road transport and highways minister

on Wednesday said that his ministry has approved Rs 1,176 crore for the construction of a 6.9-km-long, 6-lane major bridge with approaches across Teesta river at Sevoke on NH-10 in Darjeeling district.

In a post on X, the minister said, âThe proposed bridge will significantly strengthen connectivity between Sikkim, North-Eastern states and

, facilitating smoother movement of passengers and freight. The project will support regional integration, trade and commerce, tourism and logistics, while contributing to sustained socio-economic development across the region.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He added that improved road infrastructure and enhanced connectivity will help reduce travel time, ease congestion and improve the efficiency of movement of goods and services, benefiting local communities, businesses and the wider regional economy.

Earlier this week, Gadkari had announced a decision to build a 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya), at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore. The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) to Siliguri.

Once completed, the two corridors will provide high-speed connectivity between UP and the North East.

World.title: Cabinet clears Rs 1,789cr intelligent traffic system for Delhi, first planned before 2010 CWG
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Paving the way for Delhi to get a smart, technology-driven traffic management system over the next couple of years, the Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the implementation of ITMS at an estimated cost of Rs 1,789 crore.

The project to be implemented by Delhi police will feature AI-enabled signals, real-time congestion detection, automated enforcement and priority movement for ambulances across 42 key corridors.

The proposal for an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) was first initiated ahead of the 2010 Commonwealth Games, though now the scale has been expanded to use the latest technology to detect nearly 20 types of violations and cover more stretches.

Announcing the decision, Union I&B minister Ashwini Vaihnaw said the project will add âbrainâ to Delhiâs traffic management system as it will make the cityâs traffic management infrastructure âintelligentâ by integrating existing traffic signals, CCTVs, and AI capabilities into a unified, centralised control system.

PM

, in a post on X, said the decision will âensure the usage of technology to boost âEase of Livingâ across Delhi.â





The project will be implemented in three phases over two years, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.

On the need for the project, Vaishnaw said that at present, Delhiâs 1,529 traffic signals run on fixed timings with manual interventions and these canât adjust on their own when traffic builds up at a junction. He added that the cameras installed to detect red-light jumping and speeding work in isolation as âthere is no single city-wide system that links signal control, enforcement, traffic information and diversions or that uses AI to flag wanted vehiclesâ.

He added that the ITMS brings signal control, enforcement and live traffic information onto one technology platform. Govt said under this new regime, adaptive signals will be synced across corridors and congestion can be spotted early. The AI-enabled system will detect violations and can flag stolen or hot-listed vehicles as well.

In an official statement, govt said the system will enable traffic signals to automatically adjust timings based on prevailing road conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors to reduce stoppages and delays.

It will also facilitate priority movement of ambulances and other emergency vehicles through green corridors, besides enabling quicker detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents, allowing police to take faster operational measures.

It said variable message signs and digital platforms will provide commuters with information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions.

Such information may also be shared with navigation service providers.

The system will strengthen automated enforcement against violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying repeat violators and vehicles linked to hit-and-run incidents.

Officials said the system will have multiple layers. The physical layer includes data centres, networks, controllers, sensors, and enforcement cameras that can read vehicle number plates automatically. The digital layer will integrate devices for real-time data capture and processing, while the application layer will cover traffic analytics, enforcement, parking, congestion and signal control, incident management, video systems, and adaptive traffic control.

The system will also assist police in handling vehicle breakdowns, debris on roads, accident detection, monitoring VVIP movements, and managing route diversions. During emergencies, it will also help ensure smooth and priority movement of ambulances and disaster response vehicles by monitoring and clearing routes, officials added.

P K Sikdar, a former director of Central Road Research Institute (CRRI), said the decision will provide additional smartness to the cityâs traffic.

"However, the smart city infrastructure and all these additional features need to be developed to an integrated platform with matured participation from all executive agencies of the city involved directly and indirectly in the transport system of the city," he added.

Sikdar said this integrated platform should serve enforcement against all types of violations to incident detection and emergency response, and also for the alerts to the road users. "Most importantly, the public transport system is required to be highly modernised to change the preference of the public for the personalized modes. This is the opportunity to change the future direction of the city; but that is likely to demand significantly more resources," he said.
